items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to avian influenza H5N1 in poultry

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza H5N1 in poultry (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to avian influenza H5N1 in poultry

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza in mammals (England)
items.description: The local authority must ensure compliance with and enforce regulations relating to avian influenza in mammals.

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza in mammals (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to avian influenza in mammals.

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza in wild birds (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to avian influenza in wild birds.

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza in wild birds (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to avian influenza in wild birds.

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza preventive measures (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to enforce regulations relating to preventive measures for avian influenza

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza preventive measures (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to enforce regulations relating to preventive measures for avian influenza

items.label: Animal welfare - avian influenza vaccination
items.description: A local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with Regulations relating to Avian Influenza vaccination.

items.label: Animal welfare - Bluetongue
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations concerning the identification and containment of bluetongue disease in livestock.

items.label: Animal welfare - cat and dog fur - enforcement
items.description: It is the duty of any weights and measures authority to enforce regulations regarding the placing on the market and the import to, or export from, the Community of cat and dog fur, and products containing such fur.

items.label: Animal welfare - cat and dog fur - inspection
items.description: The local weights and measures authority has the power to inspect and seize goods suspected to be cat and dog fur and to apply to Court for forfeiture orders in respect of goods which contravene the prohibition.

items.label: Animal welfare - cattle plague
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to cattle plague.

items.label: Animal welfare - clearance of sheep from common land
items.description: If a local authority is satisfied that any common land or any part of common land has on it sheep which are visibly affected with sheep scab, it may publish a notice requiring all persons keeping sheep on the land specified in the notice to move all those sheep off that land before the date specified in the notice.

items.label: Animal welfare - closed circuit television in slaughterhouses
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations regarding the mandatory use of closed circuit television in slaughterhouses.

items.label: Animal welfare - control of salmonella in turkey flocks
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Order relating to salmonella in turkey flocks.

items.label: Animal welfare - disease control in animals
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Regulations relating to disease control in animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - diseases of poultry (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Regulations relating to disease control in poultry.

items.label: Animal welfare - diseases of poultry (Wales)
items.description: A local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Regulations relating to disease control in poultry.

items.label: Animal welfare - dog breeding licensing
items.description: A local authority must be satisfied  with prescribed matters when considering the granting and renewing of a licence, must set out the compulsory conditions prescribed, must have regard to guidance issued by the Welsh Ministers and may charge fees to cover any reasonable expenses incurred in performing this function and for monitoring compliance with the Regulations.   Local authorities have powers to suspend, vary or revoke licenses and to enforce the Regulations.

items.label: Animal welfare - dog collars and identification
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce orders relating to the dogs wearing collars and identification when in a public place.

items.label: Animal welfare - enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to enforce regulations relating to various SIs as detailed in this order amending the regulations.

items.label: Animal welfare - enzootic bovine leukosis (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Order relating to Enzootic Bovine Leukosis.

items.label: Animal welfare - enzootic bovine leukosis (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Order relating to Enzootic Bovine Leukosis

items.label: Animal welfare - equine identification (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to equine identification

items.label: Animal welfare - equine identification (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Regulations relating to equine identification.

items.label: Animal welfare - establishments for laying hens (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to establishments at which 350 or more laying hens are kept.

items.label: Animal welfare - establishments for laying hens (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to establishments at which 350 or more laying hens are kept.

items.label: Animal welfare - export of horses
items.description: The local authority has a duty to enforce regulations relating to the conditions under which horses can be exported.

items.label: Animal welfare - export quarantine stations
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to export quarantine stations for cattle, sheep and goats, and all other ruminating animals and swine.

items.label: Animal welfare - farmed animals (England)
items.description: The local authority may prosecute for a breach of the regulations relating to the welfare of farmed animals

items.label: Animal welfare - farmed animals (Wales)
items.description: The local authority may prosecute for a breach of regulations relating to the welfare of farmed animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - foot and mouth disease - erection of signs
items.description: The local authority shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable after declaration of any foot and mouth disease zone, ensure that the boundaries of the following zones are indicated by signs erected in a conspicuous position on all roads entering the zones on which it considers susceptible animals are likely to be moved—(a)every temporary control zone;(b)every supplementary movement control zone;(c)every protection zone;(d)every surveillance zone;(e)every restricted zone;(f)every wild animal infected zone.

items.label: Animal welfare - foot and mouth disease enforcement
items.description: The local authority has to ensure compliance with and enforce regulations relating to foot and mouth disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - foot and mouth disease vaccination (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to Foot and Mouth Disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - foot and mouth disease vaccination (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to Foot and Mouth Disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - foot and mouth disease vaccination zones (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to erect signs in a conspicuous position on all roads entering a vaccination zone or a vaccination surveillance zone on which it considers susceptible animals are likely to be moved, as soon as is reasonably practicable after declaration of the zone.

items.label: Animal welfare - foot and mouth disease vaccination zones (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to erect signs in a conspicuous position on all roads entering a vaccination zone or a vaccination surveillance zone on which it considers susceptible animals are likely to be moved, as soon as is reasonably practicable after declaration of the zone.

items.label: Animal welfare - horse passport inspection
items.description: A local authority may appoint inspectors who may enter premises and take prescribed steps to enforce the Regulations

items.label: Animal welfare - horse passports enforcement
items.description: A local authority must enforce the Horse Passport Regulations 2009/1611.

items.label: Animal welfare - import of animal pathogens
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to the importation of animal pathogens which may cause disease in animals or poultry

items.label: Animal welfare - importation of animal and poultry products
items.description: The local authority may demand that the owner or the person in charge of any animal product or poultry product produce any licence or notice which has been served.

items.label: Animal welfare - importation of animals
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to the importation of cattle, sheep, goats and all other ruminating animals and swine.

items.label: Animal welfare - importation of birds, poultry and hatching eggs
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to the importation of birds, poultry and hatching eggs

items.label: Animal welfare - importation of processed animal protein
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance to and to enforce the order relating to the importation of processed animal protein

items.label: Animal welfare - infectious diseases of horses
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order regarding infectious diseases of horses.

items.label: Animal welfare - markets
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to the welfare of animals while they are in a market for sale or awaiting transportation.

items.label: Animal welfare - microchipping of dogs (England)
items.description: A local authority in whose area a dog is kept may authorise in writing any person to act for the purpose of enforcing these Regulations in its area.

items.label: Animal welfare - microchipping of dogs (Wales)
items.description: A local authority in whose area a dog is kept may authorise in writing any person to act for the purpose of enforcing these Regulations in its area.

items.label: Animal welfare - non-commercial movement of birds
items.description: An officer of the LA (a designated “competent authority” for the purposes of Article 10 in relation to Commission Decision 2007/25/EC as regards certain protection measures in relation to highly pathogenic avian influenza and movements of pet birds accompanying their owners into the Community) may serve a written notice on the person accompanying the bird, requiring that person to— (a)  return the bird to its country of origin, (b)  place the bird in quarantine for such period, at such place and subject to such conditions as may be specified in the notice, or (c)  where the return or quarantine of the bird is not possible, cause the bird to be destroyed by a date specified in the notice.  Where a notice is not complied with, an officer of the LA may seize the bird, detain it and arrange for it to be treated as required by the notice at the expense of the person on whom notice is served.

items.label: Animal welfare - notification of specified diseases
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the notification of specified diseases in animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - official controls (animals, feed and food, plant health fees etc)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to official controls for animals, feed and food, plant health fees etc

items.label: Animal welfare - permitted mutilation procedures (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to permitted mutilation procedures for any animal for identification, control of reproduction or other management purposes.

items.label: Animal welfare - permitted mutilation procedures (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to permitted mutilation procedures for any animal for identification, control of reproduction or other management purposes.

items.label: Animal welfare - pig records, identification and movement (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to records kept, identification requirements and movement of pigs.

items.label: Animal welfare - pig records, identification and movement (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to records kept, identification requirements and movement of pigs.

items.label: Animal welfare - pleuro-pneumonia
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to cases or suspected cases of pleuro-pneumonia in animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - poultry compartments
items.description: An inspector appointed by the local authority may enter premises kept as a poultry compartment and may require to inspect any documents or records relevant to the approval of a site as a compartment.

items.label: Animal welfare - prosecutions
items.description: A local authority may prosecute proceedings for an offence under the Act or Regulations made under the Act.

items.label: Animal welfare - psittacosis or ornithosis in poultry
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to psittacosis or ornithosis in poultry.

items.label: Animal welfare - rabies (importation of dogs, cats and other animals)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order which control the import of dogs, cats and other animals in order to prevent rabies.

items.label: Animal welfare - rabies control
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to rabies control.

items.label: Animal welfare - racing greyhounds
items.description: LAs must, on the receipt of an application in writing for a licence, grant or renew a licence to an operator, if satisfied that the licensing conditions are or will be met and any appropriate fee has been paid. An LA must carry out an inspection of a track to satisfy itself that the licensing conditions are or will be met before granting or renewing a licence; and may grant or renew a licence for any period of up to 3 years

items.label: Animal welfare - restrictions on animal movement (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and ensure restrictions in place on the movement of animals in cases of disease or suspected disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - restrictions on movement of animals (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and ensure restrictions in place on the movement of animals in cases of disease or suspected disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - salmonella and brucella
items.description: the local authority has a duty to ensure compline with and to enforce the order relating to salmonella and brucella.

items.label: Animal welfare - salmonella in broiler flocks
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to salmonella in broiler flocks

items.label: Animal welfare - salmonella in hatching eggs
items.description: An inspector appointed by the local authority may seize, destroy or dispose of any hatching eggs for the purpose of preventing the spread of salmonella.

items.label: Animal welfare - salmonella in poultry
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Order relating to salmonella in poultry.

items.label: Animal welfare - seizure in connection with the prevention of animal disease
items.description: A local authority has the power to seize anything (save for a live animal) in connection with the prevention of animal disease with a duty to destroy that thing where required for the prevention of spread of disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - sheep and goats (records, identification and movement) (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the keeping of records, identification and movement of sheep and goats.

items.label: Animal welfare - sheep and goats (records, identification and movement) (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the keeping of records, identification and movement of sheep and goats.

items.label: Animal welfare - sheep scab
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to sheep scab

items.label: Animal welfare - swine diseases
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations regarding African swine fever, classic swine fever (otherwise known as hog cholera) and swine vesicular disease.

items.label: Animal welfare - time of killing (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the killing of animals under licence or certificate in a slaughterhouse or elsewhere.

items.label: Animal welfare - time of killing (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the welfare of animals at the time of killing under licence or certificate in a slaughterhouse or elsewhere

items.label: Animal welfare - transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to transmissible spongiform encephalopathies in bovine animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to transmissible spongiform encephalopathies in bovine animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - transport (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to the conditions under which animals are transported.

items.label: Animal welfare - transport (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the order relating to the conditions under which animals are transported.

items.label: Animal welfare - tuberculosis (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to tuberculosis in cows and other bovine animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - tuberculosis (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to tuberculosis in cows and other bovine animals.

items.label: Animal welfare - welfare at time of killing
items.description: The local authority (as well as the competent authority) may appoint inspectors with powers to ensure compliance with these Regulations and the EU Regulation, including powers of entry and seizure and powers to issue enforcement notices.

items.label: Animal welfare - zoonoses monitoring (England)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations in relation to zoonoses or zoonotic agents in any premises on which any animal or animal feeding stuff is, or has been, present.

items.label: Animal welfare - zoonoses monitoring (Wales)
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations in relation to zoonoses or zoonotic agents in any premises on which any animal or animal feeding stuff is, or has been, present.

items.label: Animal Welfare – prohibition of live exports for slaughter
items.description: A local authority must enforce the Act to the extent required by Regulations.

items.label: Animals - detention of horses
items.description: A local authority may detain horses in certain circumstances and recover certain expenses from the owner.

items.label: Animals - sale of detained horses
items.description: A local authority may sell detained horses in certain circumstances.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - case reviews
items.description: In a case where a person has made a complaint about anti-social behaviour in a particular local government area, the relevant bodies in that area must carry out a review of the response to that behaviour (an “ASB case review)” if—(a)that person, or any other person, makes an application for such a review, and(b)the relevant bodies decide that the threshold for a review is met.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - charging for work on high hedges
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority may enter premises to carry out works for which a charge may be made in certain circumstances relating to high hedges.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - child safety orders
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with a court in the court's dealings with a child safety order.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - co-operation when making parenting orders
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with a court when the court wishes to make a parenting order.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - consultation
items.description: A local authority may respond to a consultation regarding the draft community remedy document.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - contracting out
items.description: A local authority may contract out of some of its functions in certain circumstances.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - high hedge complaints
items.description: A local authority must consider complaints regarding high hedges according to the procedures under this section.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - high hedges power of entry
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority may enter premises for the purposes of the exercise of the local authority's powers and duties relating to high hedges.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - notice to remove graffiti and fly posting
items.description: A local authority may serve a notice requiring the removal of graffiti or fly posting and recover its expenditure in so doing and must have regard to guidance from the Secretary of State or National Assembly.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - parental compensation order
items.description: A local authority may apply for a parental compensation order or a review of the order in certain circumstances.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - parenting contracts
items.description: A local authority may, having regard to Guidance from the Secretary of State, enter into a parenting contract if it has reason to believe a child or young person is or is likely to become engaged in anti-social behaviour.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - parenting contracts as social housing provider
items.description: A local authority may, where it is a registered provider of social housing, having regard to Guidance from the Secretary of State, enter into a parenting contract if it has reason to believe a child or young person is or is likely to become engaged in anti-social behaviour.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - parenting orders
items.description: A local authority may apply for a parenting order, for a child residing or appearing to reside in its area, if it has reason to believe a child or young person is or is likely to become engaged in anti-social behaviour.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - parenting orders as social housing provider
items.description: A local authority may, where it is a registered provider of social housing, apply for a parenting order, for a child residing or appearing to reside in its area, if it has reason to believe a child or young person is or is likely to become engaged in anti-social behaviour.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - penalty notices for graffiti and fly posting
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may issue a penalty notice for graffiti or fly posting.  The amount of the penalty should be as determined by regulations.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - public spaces protection order
items.description: Where a local authority has made, extended or varied a public spaces protection order it must publish the details it on its website and erect a notice adjacent to the public space concerned.  Likewise where it has discharged an order it must publish in the same manner the date and identify the order discharged.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - remedial notices for high hedges
items.description: A local authority may issue, withdraw or relax a remedial notice in relation to a complaint regarding high hedges.

items.label: Anti-social behaviour - sale of aerosol paints to children enforcement
items.description: It is the duty of every local weights and measures authority to consider, at least once in every period of twelve months, the extent to which it is appropriate for the authority to carry out in their area a programme of enforcement action in relation to section 54 and to the extent that they consider it appropriate to do so, carry out such a programme.

items.label: Apprenticeships - publication of information
items.description: A local authority with Apprenticeship Targets must publish and send to the Secretary of State prescribed information.

items.label: Apprenticeships - regulations regarding targets
items.description: A local authority with Apprenticeship Targets must have regard to the target and must comply with Regulations

items.label: Aquaculture - inspection of premises
items.description: The local authority has a duty to inspect aquaculture premises when required and comply with all requirements concerning aquatic animal health.

items.label: Areas of outstanding natural beauty - general duties
items.description: A local authority must in carrying out its functions have regard to preserving and enhancing the beauty of areas of outstanding natural beauty.

items.label: Areas of outstanding natural beauty - management plans
items.description: A local authority must produce and publish management plans in relation to areas of outstanding natural beauty as required by the Act.

items.label: Auction premises - registration
items.description: A local authority must licence auction premises in accordance with the terms of the Act.

items.label: Barriers at level crossings - financial contributions
items.description: A local authority may contribute to the expenses incurred for providing lifting or other barriers, lights, signs, or other devices or appliances for the protection or convenience of the public at or near any level crossing where a road is crossed by a railway.

items.label: Bathing and boating - byelaws
items.description: Where any part of the area of a local authority having power to make byelaws about public bathing and pleasure boats is bounded by or is to seaward of the low water mark, the authority may exercise that power as respects any area of the sea which is outside the area of the authority and within 1,000 metres to seaward of any place where that mark is within or on the boundary of the area of the authority.

items.label: Bathing waters - notification
items.description: Every local authority controlling a bathing water must disseminate specified information near it from 15 May to 30 September (the bathing season) including the bathing water's current classification as “poor”, “sufficient”, “good” or “excellent” and the source of more complete published information.  It has additional obligations regarding advice relating to waters rated as “poor”; and for publicising the advice and the reasons for any declassification of a former bathing water.  In the event of pollution events occurring at a bathing water, a local authority must inform the public about any health risks and provide other specified information.

items.label: Best value authorities - accounts
items.description: A best value authority must comply with any regulations regarding the keeping of accounts.

items.label: Best value authorities - conditions for new powers
items.description: A local authority must comply with any conditions prescribed by the Secretary of State relating to any new best value authority powers arising from section 6.

items.label: Best value authorities - failure to comply with best value duty
items.description: A local authority must comply with any review, inquiry or directions required by or coming from the Secretary of State in circumstances where the Secretary of State believes that the authority is not complying with its best value duties.

items.label: Best value authorities - fees for inspections
items.description: A local authority must pay the appropriate best value inspection fee.

items.label: Best value authorities - general duties
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements to secure continuous improvement in the way in which its functions are exercised, having regard to a combination of economy, efficiency and effectiveness and must take prescribed steps when doing so.

items.label: Best value authorities - inspections
items.description: A local authority must comply with the requirements of a best value inspection.

items.label: Best value authorities - non-commercial considerations in contracts
items.description: A local authority must comply with any order relating to the exclusion of non-commercial considerations in contracts.

items.label: Best value authorities - regard to guidance
items.description: A local authority must have regard to any guidance to or in respect of best value authorities issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Biofuel labelling
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with Regulations relating to Biofuel labelling.

items.label: Birmingham Commonwealth Games - direction to traffic authority
items.description: The local traffic authority must comply with any direction from the Secretary of State regarding traffic orders and must pay any associated expenses to the Secretary of State when in default.

items.label: Birmingham Commonwealth Games - games transport plan
items.description: Every local authority must when directed by the Secretary of State to do so must prepare and implement a Games transport plan.A “Games transport plan” means a plan that relates to one or more areas in England and addresses transport matters relating to the Games.An authority directed as stated must—(a) comply with the direction;(b)keep the Games transport plan under review;(c)if the authority consider it appropriate, revise the plan;(d)except in so far as the authority consider it undesirable for reasons of security, publish the plan and any revision.(e)implement the plan to the extent applicable.Before preparing or revising the plan, the authority must consult the persons specified in Regulations.

items.label: Birmingham Commonwealth Games - temporary prohibition or restrictins on roads
items.description: Section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act (RTRA) 1984 has effect in relation to a traffic authority for a road in England as if subsection (1)(c) of that section included the following purposes—(a)implementing a Games transport plan,(b)facilitating transport services in connection with the Games, and(c)facilitating travel by any person for a purpose connected to the Games.(2)The following do not apply in relation to an order made or notice issued by virtue of this section—(a)section 15 of the RTRA 1984;(b)regulations 6 and 8(3) of the Road Traffic (Temporary Restrictions) Procedure Regulations 1992 (S.I. 1992/1215).(3)An order made or notice issued by virtue of this section may not come into force before the beginning of the period of 21 days ending immediately before the day on which the Games begin.(4)An order made by virtue of this section must cease to have effect no later than the end of the period of 5 days beginning with the day after the day on which the Games end.(5)A notice issued by virtue of this section must cease to have effect no later than—(a)the end of the period of 21 days beginning with the day after the day on which the notice comes into force, or(b)the end of the period of 5 days beginning with the day after the day on which the Games end,whichever is earlier.

items.label: Birmingham Commonwealth Games - ticket touting
items.description: A local authority may enforce a ticket touting offence (England and Wales), advertising offence (England only) or trading offence (England Only) under sections 10, 13 and 16 of the Act.

items.label: Birmingham Commonwealth Games - trading
items.description: Every local authority must provide a copy of any guidance published by the Organising Committee to each relevant trader in the authority's area who the authority consider may be affected by section 16 (the trading offence), andmust provide each such relevant trader with whatever information the authority consider appropriate for the purpose of assisting the relevant trader to mitigate the effect of that section.“relevant trader”, in relation to a local authority, means either a person who holds a trading licence granted by the authority, or a person who has applied to the authority for such a licence, and whose application has not been determined or withdrawn.

items.label: Breeding of dogs - inspection of premises not covered by licence
items.description: A local authority may in certain circumstances inspect premises not covered by licence under the Breeding of Dogs Act 1973.

items.label: Bridges over railways and inland waterways
items.description: A local authority has responsibility for certain bridges over waterways and railways.

items.label: Building control - charges
items.description: LAs may fix and recover charges for the performance of their building control functions relating to building regulations according to a charging scheme governed by principles laid down in the Regulations.  Each LA is responsible for setting its own building control charges and for doing so within the accounting and administrative requirements laid down.

items.label: Building control - general powers
items.description: LAs may relax some of the building regulations, issue completion certificates where building work complies with regulations and carry out various testing.

items.label: Building regulations - breaking open of streets
items.description: A local authority may break open the streets in certain circumstances

items.label: Building regulations - compensation for damage
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation for damage sin certain circumstances.

items.label: Building regulations - compliance with directions
items.description: A local authority must comply with the directions of the Secretary of State or Welsh Ministers, and pay their expenses when exercising their default powers and comply with any transfer order made.

items.label: Building regulations - enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority may, issue an enforcement notice and in certain circumstances carry out the required works and charge the owner or occupier for the same.

items.label: Building regulations - entry of premises
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may, in certain circumstances enter premises to ensure compliance with building regulations.

items.label: Building regulations - execution of works
items.description: A local authority may, with the agreement of the owner or occupier of the premises execute works at the expense of the owner or occupier.

items.label: Building regulations - forms and notices
items.description: It is the duty of local authorities to issue forms and notices, authenticate and serve the same in writing and to comply with any statutory instruments.

items.label: Building regulations - indemnity of Members and officers
items.description: A local authority must indemnify its Members and officers in certain circumstances

items.label: Building regulations - power to prosecute
items.description: A local authority may commence the prosecution of offences under this Act.

items.label: Building regulations - recovery of expenses
items.description: A local authority may recover its expenses and interest for work done in connection with the Act in certain circumstances.

items.label: Building regulations - sale of materials
items.description: A local authority may sell materials removed from premises in certain circumstances.

items.label: Building safety - application of guidance
items.description: Local authorities and fire and rescue authorities must take  guidance from the Building safety Regulator into account, when carrying out any directions from the Regulator.

items.label: Building safety - assistance etc. to the regulator
items.description: A local authority or a fire and rescue authority may at the request of the building safety regulator (Health and Safety Executive) do anything for the purpose of -(a)  facilitating the exercise by the regulator of a relevant function relating to:- the regulation of higher-risk buildings - higher risk building work- regulation of any work for which the regulator is the building control authorityor(b)  enabling the local authority or fire and rescue authority to facilitate the exercise by the regulator of a relevant function.

items.label: Building safety - co-operation with the regulator
items.description: The Regulator, local authorities and fire and rescue authorities must comply with Schedule 3 relating to co-operation and sharing of information in the exercise of their relevant functions in relation to higher risk buildings.

items.label: Building safety - compliance with direction of the regulator
items.description: A relevant authority must comply with a direction of the building safety Regulator in relation to higher-risk buildings , providing the Regulator has complied with the correct procedure before making the Direction.

items.label: Building safety - ensuring staff competence
items.description: When assisting the Regulator in matters relating to higher-risk buildings a relevant authority must ensure that any of its staff involved in providing relevant assistance to the regulator have the appropriate skills, knowledge, experience and behaviours."Relevant assistance" means anything done by the authority pursuant to a request or direction, for the purpose of facilitating the exercise by the regulator of a relevant function.A local authority must also comply with any regulations issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Building safety - information sharing with the regulator
items.description: Local authorities and fire and rescue authorities may share information with the Regulator and others in accordance with Schedule 3.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations - execution of Act
items.description: It is the duty of local authorities to carry this Act into execution, subject to sections 91ZD,  the provisions of Part I of the Public Health Act 1936 relating to united districts and joint boards;section 151 of the Local Government, Planning and Land Act 1980 (urban development areas); section 1(3) of the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 (port health authorities); Regulations and the provisions of 91ZA and 91ZB (relating to the duties of the Regulator) .  It is the function of local authorities to enforce building regulations in their areas.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – a Local Authority acting as Building Control Authority restricted activities and functions
items.description: A local authority acting as building control authority may out carry out a restricted activity in relation to any work only through a registered building inspector, acting on the authority's behalf, whose registration has effect in relation to work of that description.Before each exercise of a restricted function in relation to any work, a building control authority must obtain and consider the advice of a registered building inspector whose registration has effect in relation to work of that description.The registered building inspector who carries out the restricted activity, or advises on the exercise of the restricted function, may (but need not) be employed by the authority. must keep, maintain, make publicly available and provide information from such registers as are prescribed.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – acceptance or rejection of initial notice
items.description: A local authority must either accept or reject a notice from a registered building control approver in accordance with the prescribed grounds and within the prescribed period.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – advertisement of proposals to relax Building Regulations
items.description: A local authority must advertise proposals to relax building regulations in local newspaper in certain circumstances, within at a timescale specified by section 9 and must consider relevant representations.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – applications for the relaxation of Building Regulations
items.description: A local authority must pass any application for relaxation of Building Regulations to the appropriate National Authority and must respond to the consultation arising from the National Authority.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – cancellation of initial notice
items.description: A local authority must cancel an initial notice in certain prescribed circumstances by following the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – cancellation of Initial Notice when work becomes higher-risk building
items.description: A local authority must cancel an initial notice when a building becomes a higher risk building in prescribed circumstances by following the prescribed procedure and must give a copy of the notice to the Regulator.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Compliance Notices
items.description: A local authority in England may, give a compliance notice as prescribed by section 35B to a person who appears to the authority to have contravened, be contravening or be likely to contravene - (a) a relevant provision of building regulations, or(b) a requirement imposed by virtue of such a provision.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Consideration of transfer of certificate and report
items.description: Where a registered building control approver gives a transfer certificate and a transfer report to a local authority in accordance with section 53B(3), the local authority must consider and accept or reject the certificate and report before the end of the relevant period in the prescribed manner. The local authority may request further information to enable it do so. NOTE this is a power AND a duty.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Continuing failure to meet standards
items.description: A local authority may challenge the Regulator’s recommendation (transfer of functions to the Secretary of State or another local authority) in relation to a continuing failure to meet standards.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – continuing requirements, power to execute work, recover costs and give directions
items.description: Where continuing requirements of The Building Regulations have been breached a local authority may execute the works themselves and recover their reasonable costs in doing so and/or by notice direct the owner or occupier of the building to carry out the required work.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – final certificate
items.description: Where applicable a local authority must consider, accept or reject a Final Certificate.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – keeping of Register
items.description: It is the duty of local authorities to keep a register of prescribed information required by the Act.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Means of access by which refuse or faecal matter is removed from a building
items.description: A local authority may consent of the building control authority to the closure or obstruct the means of access by which refuse or faecal matter is removed from a building, and in giving their consent may impose such conditions as they think fit with respect to the improvement of an alternative means of access or the substitution of other means of access.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – new initial notice
items.description: A local authority must take prescribed steps where a new initial notice is given under section 53(7)(a) of the Building Act 1984.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – plans certificates
items.description: Where applicable a local authority must consider, accept or reject and may rescind a Plans Certificate taking into account prescribed grounds. NOTE - this is a power AND a duty.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – prohibition on exercising certain functions or exercising certain proceedings whilst initial notice is in force
items.description: For as long as the initial notice is in force the function of enforcing building regulations that is conferred on a local authority by section 91(2) is not exercisable in relation to the work to which the notice relates, and accordingly—(a)  a local authority may not give a notice under section 35B, 35C or 36(1) above in relation to that work, and(b)  a local authority may not institute proceedings under section 35 above for a contravention that arises out of the carrying out of that work.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – provision of drainage
items.description: A local authority may when considering an application for building control for a building or an extension to a building require it to drain into a sewer in certain circumstances.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Provision of exits from certain types of building to which the public have access
items.description: A local authority must reject an application for building control approval for a building or an extension to a building if it cannot be shown that the building or extension as adequate means of ingress or egress.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – provision of water supply
items.description: A local authority must reject an application for building control approval for a house unless satisfactory provision for supply of water has been made.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Public Body’s Notice
items.description: A local authority must consider and accept or reject a public body notice in the prescribed manner.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Recording and furnishing information
items.description: Every local authority shall keep, in such manner as may be prescribed, a register containing such information as may be prescribed with respect to initial notices, amendment notices, notices under section 51C, public body's notices, transfer reports and certificates given to them, including information (where applicable) as to whether such notices, reports or certificates have been accepted or rejected and must keep the same available for public inspection at all reasonable hours.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Regulator’s Improvement Notice
items.description: Subject to the right to appeal a local authority must comply with an Improvement Notice received from the Regulator.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Regulator’s Serious Contravention Notice
items.description: Subject to the right to appeal a local authority must comply with a Serious Contravention Notice received from the Regulator.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – removal or alteration of offending work
items.description: A local authority may, without prejudice to their right to take proceedings for a fine in respect of the contravention, may by notice require the owner to remove or alter the offending work.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Stop Notices
items.description: A local authority in England may, give a stop notice as prescribed by section 35C to a person appearing to the authority to be in control of any work if it appears to the authority that - (a) the carrying out of the work would contravene a provision of building regulations prescribed for the purposes of this paragraph,(b) a compliance notice relating to the work has been contravened, or(c) the work contravenes a provision of building regulations or a requirement imposed by virtue of such a provision, and the risk of serious harm (as defined by section 35C is met).

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – tests for conformity with the Building Regulations
items.description: A local authority may, where work to which building regulations are applicable is proposed or carried out, utilise the powers listed in section 33 for the purpose of ascertaining whether any provision of building regulations is or would be contravened-(a) by or in connection with the work, or(b) in relation to the building that the work has been, is being or will be carried out on.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – the Local Authority to be the Building Control Authority
items.description: A local authority will be the Building Control Authority save in situations where sections 91ZA or 91ZB (higher risk buildings in England) provide that the Regulator shall be the Building Control Authority; and will also be the Building Control Authority where Regulations under section 91ZD provide that it is the Building Control Authority (in respect of higher risk buildings in Wales).

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – the Local Authority to reject the Building Regulator’s notice
items.description: A local authority must reject the Building Regulator’s notice under section 91ZB if prescribed grounds exist and must have regard to and comply with Building Regulations.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – Use of materials unsuitable for a permanent building
items.description: A local authority may when considering an application for building control reject the use of materials unsuitable for a permanent building or otherwise attach conditions to their use.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – use of short lived materials
items.description: A local authority may when considering an application for building control reject the use of short lived materials or otherwise attach conditions to their use.

items.label: Buildings and building regulations – variation of work
items.description: Where applicable a local authority must consider, accept or reject or may impose conditions upon a notice of variation of work taking into account prescribed grounds. NOTE - this is a power AND a duty.

items.label: Burial and cremation - charging for municipal funeral
items.description: An authority may recover from the estate of the deceased person expenses incurred under subsection (1) or subsection (2) above.

items.label: Burial and cremation - crematoria fees
items.description: A local authority may charge fees for cremations.

items.label: Burial and cremation - crematoria regulations
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations concerning crematoria and burning.

items.label: Burial and cremation - donations of land, money or property for crematoria
items.description: A local authority may accept donations of land, money or property to enable them to provide and maintain crematoria.

items.label: Burial and cremation - municipal funerals
items.description: It shall be the duty of a local authority to cause to be buried or cremated the body of any person who has died or been found dead in their area, in any case where it appears to the authority that no suitable arrangements for the disposal of the body have been or are being made otherwise than by the authority.

items.label: Burial and cremation - person in care accommodation (England)
items.description: Any council which is the local authority for the purposes of the Local Authority Social Services Act 1970 may cause to be buried or cremated the body of any deceased person who immediately before his death was being provided with accommodation under Part 1 of the Care Act 2014

items.label: Burial and cremation - person in care accommodation (Wales)
items.description: A local authority within the meaning of the Social Services and Well-being (Wales) Act 2014 may cause to be buried or cremated the body of any deceased person who immediately before his death was being provided with accommodation under Part 4 of that Act.

items.label: Burial and cremation - provision of crematoria
items.description: A local authority may provide and maintain burial grounds or cemeteries, or anything essential, ancillary or incidental thereto and may provide and maintain crematoria.

items.label: Bus network accessibility plan
items.description: A local transport authority whose area is in England must, before 27 October 2026, publish a bus network accessibility plan in relation to the authority's area containing the prescribed information.

items.label: Bus services - advanced quality partnership scheme - variation or revocation
items.description: The authority or authorities responsible for a Scheme may vary or revoke Scheme.

items.label: Bus services - advanced quality partnership scheme postponement
items.description: The authority or authorities must, as detailed in the Section-(a)     provide each of the specified facilities or take each of the specified measures not later than the date specified for it to be provided or taken under the scheme, and(b)     continue to provide the facilities or keep the measures in effect throughout the remainder of the period for which the scheme is in operation.

items.label: Bus services - advanced quality partnership schemes
items.description: A local transport authority whose area is in England, or two or more such authorities acting jointly, may make an advanced quality partnership scheme if they are satisfied that the scheme will contribute to the implementation of their local transport policies.

items.label: Bus services - advanced quality partnership schemes - regulations and guidance
items.description: The Transport Authorities must comply with Regulations  and have regard to Guidance issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Bus services - advanced ticketing schemes
items.description: A local transport authority or two or more such authorities acting jointly, may make a ticketing scheme (an "advanced ticketing scheme") covering the whole or any part of their area, or combined area, if they consider that the proposed scheme-(a)     would be in the interests of the public, and(b)     would contribute to the implementation of their local transport policies.

items.label: Bus services - assessment and approval of franchising schemes
items.description: Subject to Regulations, a franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, proposing to make a franchising scheme must carry out an assessment as required by Section 123B, publish the same and where necessary obtain the Secretary of State's approval.

items.label: Bus services - audit of franchising schemes
items.description: Subject to Regulations, a franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, proposing to make a franchising scheme must carry out an independent audit of the scheme, whilst having regard to the Secretary of State's guidance.

items.label: Bus services - civil penalties for bus lane contraventions
items.description: A local authority may levy charges for bus lane contravention in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services - compliance with enhanced partnership plans or schemes
items.description: A local authority or authorities must comply with their own enhanced partnership plans and schemes.

items.label: Bus services - consultation on franchising schemes
items.description: Subject to Regulations, a franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, proposing to make a franchising scheme must carry out a consultation exercise in relation to the scheme, in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services - enforcement of mandatory travel concessions
items.description: A local authority may take proceedings to enforce mandatory travel concessions for free travel for elderly and disabled persons.

items.label: Bus services - enhanced partnership plans and schemes
items.description: A local transport authority or two or more such authorities acting jointly, may make-(a)     an enhanced partnership plan in relation to the whole or part of their area, or combined area, and(b)     one or more enhanced partnership schemes relating to the whole or part of the area to which the plan relates.The authority must also list socially necessary schemes and must review and amend the same from time to time.

items.label: Bus services - enhanced partnership plans and schemes - frequency of service
items.description: An enhanced partnership scheme may specify requirements about the frequency or timing of particular local services or local services of particular descriptions.

items.label: Bus services - enhanced partnership scheme notification
items.description: If a local transport authority or two or more such authorities acting jointly make or modify an enhanced partnership scheme to provide bus services the authorities must provide the Traffic Commissioner with certain information.

items.label: Bus services - facilities and measures for enhanced partnership plans and schemes
items.description: Any facilities and measures set out in an enhanced partnership scheme must comply with the requirements of the section.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes
items.description: Subject to Regulations, a franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may make a franchising scheme covering the whole or any part of their area, or their combined area.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes - interim service where operator failure
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may provide an interim service in circumstances of operator failure.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes - obtaining information
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may obtain information regarding local services in connection with Franchising Schemes.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes - postponement of local service contracts
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may postpone Local Service Contracts in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes - regulations and guidance
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, must comply with Regulations and have regard to Guidance issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes - restrictions on local service contracts
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, must comply with restrictions on Local Service Contracts where a franchising scheme is in force.

items.label: Bus services - franchising schemes - service permits
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may grant, attach conditions to, revoke or suspend a service permit.

items.label: Bus services - guidance for enhanced partnership plans or schemes
items.description: A local authority or authorities must have regard to Guidance regarding enhanced partnership plans and schemes.

items.label: Bus services - guidance on advanced ticketing schemes
items.description: If a local transport authority or two or more such authorities, must have regard to Guidance from the Secretary of State when making an advanced ticketing scheme may make a scheme.

items.label: Bus services - information from service operator
items.description: A local authority may obtain information from service providers regarding local bus services.

items.label: Bus services - information when creating a new enhanced partnership plan or scheme
items.description: If a local transport authority or two or more such authorities acting jointly, are preparing an enhanced partnership plan or scheme, the authority or any of the authorities may, in connection with preparing the plan or scheme, require an operator of a local service in their area or combined area to supply relevant information.

items.label: Bus services - joint and through ticketing schemes
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may make a joint and through ticketing scheme as part of their local transport policy.

items.label: Bus services - making an advanced quality partnership scheme
items.description: If, after taking the steps described in section 113G, an authority or authorities decide that it is appropriate to make the advanced quality partnership scheme, they may make it as proposed or with modifications. The Scheme must contain certain proscribed particulars.

items.label: Bus services - making an advanced ticketing scheme
items.description: If a local transport authority or two or more such authorities, propose to make an advanced ticketing scheme may make a scheme but must comply with various requirements when so doing.

items.label: Bus services - making information available
items.description: A local authority must having considered certain matters make information about bus services available.

items.label: Bus services - mandatory travel concessions
items.description: A local authority must issue a permit for free travel to elderly and disabled persons in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services - notice and consultation of advanced quality partnership schemes
items.description: If an authority or authorities propose to make an advanced quality partnership scheme, they must give notice of the proposed scheme in such manner as they consider appropriate for drawing it to the attention of persons in the area to which it relates. The notices must contain the required particulars and be sent to the statutory consultees.

items.label: Bus services - notice and consultation of advanced ticketing schemes
items.description: If a local transport authority or two or more such authorities, propose to make an advanced ticketing scheme, they must give notice of the proposed scheme and undertake consultation.

items.label: Bus services - notice and making content of enhanced partnership plans and schemes
items.description: If made, enhanced partnership plans and schemes must comply with the prescribed notice requirements and contain the prescribed content.

items.label: Bus services - postponement of advanced quality contract scheme
items.description: If it appears to the authority or authorities appropriate to do so, they may decide that any of the dates specified the scheme may be postponed, subject to restrictions.

items.label: Bus services - postponement of enhance partnership plans or schemes
items.description: If it appears to a local authority or authorities that have made an enhanced partnership scheme appropriate to do so, they may decide that certain dates relating to the Scheme are to be postponed by such period as they think fit, subject to limitations

items.label: Bus services - preparation, notice and consultation for enhanced partnership plans and schemes
items.description: A proposed enhanced partnership scheme must be prepared, notice of the same given and be subject to consultation

items.label: Bus services - provision of information
items.description: If a local transport authority or two or more such authorities acting jointly, must comply with Regulations requiring the provision of information about bus services.

items.label: Bus services - publication of franchising scheme
items.description: Subject to Regulations, a franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, proposing to make a franchising scheme must publish the scheme, in the required manner.

items.label: Bus services - regulations for enhanced partnership plans or schemes
items.description: A local authority or authorities must comply with Regulations regarding enhanced partnership plans and schemes.

items.label: Bus services - reimbursement of operator for mandatory travel concessions
items.description: A local authority must reimburse the transport operator in respect of mandatory travel concessions for free travel for elderly and disabled persons.

items.label: Bus services - revocation and variation of enhanced partnership plans and schemes
items.description: An enhanced partnership scheme may be revoked or varied.

items.label: Bus services - revocation of enhanced partnership plan or scheme
items.description: A local authority or authorities may revoke their own enhanced partnership plans and schemes, but must comply with notice and consultation requirements.

items.label: Bus services - revocation of franchising scheme
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may revoke a franchising scheme in accordance with the provision of the statute.

items.label: Bus services - variation of franchising scheme
items.description: A franchising authority, or two or more franchising authorities acting jointly, may vary a franchising scheme in accordance with the provision of the statute.

items.label: Bus Services Act 2025
items.description: A relevant authority must have regard to Guidance issued by the Secretary of State regarding the provision and design of floating bus stops and must comply with Regulations regarding to the provision of information to the Secretary of State regarding the same.

items.label: Bus services joint and through ticketing schemes - making of scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly when making a joint and through ticketing scheme must comply with certain conditions.

items.label: Bus services joint and through ticketing schemes - notice and consultation
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly proposing to make a joint and through ticketing scheme must comply with certain notice and consultation requirements.

items.label: Bus services of enhanced partnership plans and schemes
items.description: A local authority or authorities may vary their own enhanced partnership plans and schemes but must comply with notice and consultation requirements.

items.label: Bus services quality contract scheme - approval of proposed scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly proposing to make a quality contract scheme must apply to the appropriate national body for approval.

items.label: Bus services quality contract scheme - making of scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly, when making a quality contract scheme must comply with certain requirements including the appeals procedure.

items.label: Bus services quality contract scheme - new scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may make a quality contract scheme as part of their local transport policy.

items.label: Bus services quality contract scheme - notice and consultation
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly proposing to make a quality contract scheme as part of their local transport policy must observe certain notice and consultation requirements.

items.label: Bus services quality contract scheme - postponement of scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may postpone a quality contract scheme in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services quality contract schemes - continuance of schemes
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may continue a quality contract scheme for further periods in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services quality contract schemes - guidance about schemes
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly must comply with guidance relating to quality contract schemes.

items.label: Bus services quality contract schemes - regulations about schemes
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly must comply with regulations relating to quality contract schemes.

items.label: Bus services quality contract schemes - tendering for contracts
items.description: The authority, or the authorities acting jointly, must invite tenders for the provision of services to which the scheme relates for such period and on such basis as may be specified in the invitation to tender.

items.label: Bus services quality contract schemes - variation or revocation
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may vary or revoke a quality contract scheme for further periods in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - guidance about schemes
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly, providing a bus partnership scheme must have regard to guidance.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - making of scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly proposing to make a quality partnership scheme as part of their local transport policy must comply with certain requirements when making the scheme.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - new scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may make a quality partnership scheme as part of their local transport policy.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - notice and consultation
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly proposing to make a quality partnership scheme as part of their local transport policy must observe certain notice and consultation requirements.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - postponement of scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly may postpone a quality partnership scheme in certain circumstances.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - provision of facilities
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly must provide specified facilities for the duration of the scheme.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - regulations
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly, providing a bus partnership scheme must comply with regulations.

items.label: Bus services quality partnership scheme - variation or revocation of scheme
items.description: A local authority or two or more authorities acting jointly, providing a bus partnership scheme may vary or revoke the scheme.

items.label: Business and service delivery - Coronavirus tier restrictions
items.description: Where a local authority runs a business or provides a service, it must have regard to the Schedules of the Regulations which describe which businesses and services are affected and to what extent depending upon which of the three tiers that local authority’s area is in.

items.label: Business improvement district - additional contributions and action
items.description: A local authority may make contributions or take action towards BID arrangements for its area.

items.label: Business improvement district - administration of BID levy
items.description: A local authority comply with statutory instruments regarding administration of the BID Levy.

items.label: Business improvement district - appeal against veto
items.description: A local authority must comply with the outcome of any appeal against its veto of BID proposals.

items.label: Business improvement district - approval in ballot
items.description: A local authority must carry out a ballot regarding BID proposals in the required manner.

items.label: Business improvement district - arrangements
items.description: A local authority may make business improvement district arrangements for all or part of its area.

items.label: Business improvement district - BID levy
items.description: A local authority must calculate the BID Levy in accordance with any BID arrangements in force for its area.

items.label: Business improvement district - BID proposals
items.description: A local authority comply with statutory instruments regarding the drawing up, content and approval of BID proposals.

items.label: Business improvement district - BID revenue account
items.description: A local authority must when BID arrangements are in force for its area keep and maintain a BID revenue account.

items.label: Business improvement district - commencement and duration of BID arrangements
items.description: The billing authority concerned must ensure that BID arrangements which give effect to the proposals are made by the time the arrangements are to come into force and are to have effect for such period as may be specified in the arrangements in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Business improvement district - compliance
items.description: A local authority must comply with any BID arrangements  in force for its area.

items.label: Business improvement district - veto
items.description: A local authority may veto BID proposals in certain prescribed circumstances taking certain prescribed steps.

items.label: Business improvement districts - ballot regulations
items.description: The returning officer for local elections in the billing authority area is to be the ballot holder for any ballot in respect of BRS-BIDs required under the Regulations and must follow prescribed arrangements for the conduct and determination of a ballot.  A billing authority may recover the costs of a BRS-BID ballot or a renewal ballot from the BRS-BID proposer or BRSBID body in the prescribed circumstances; may veto BRS-BID proposals in the prescribed period and circumstances, but is subject to the appeals provision.  It must have regard to prescribed rules regarding the imposition, administration, collection, recovery and application of the BRS-BID levy.

items.label: Business improvement districts - BRS-BID levy prescribed rules
items.description: A billing authority must have regard to prescribed rules regarding the imposition, administration, collection, recovery and application of the BRS-BID levy.

items.label: Business improvement districts - recovery of ballot costs
items.description: A billing authority may recover the costs of a BRS-BID ballot or a renewal ballot from the BRS-BID proposer or BRSBID body in the prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Business improvement districts - veto of BRS-BID proposals
items.description: A billing authority may veto BRS-BID proposals in the prescribed period and circumstances, but is subject to the appeals provision.

items.label: Business rate supplement - accounting
items.description: LAs may treat specified items as debits or credits to the revenue account, must make good any deficits in the BRS revenue accounts of a levying authority or a functional body out of general funds and must make refunds and credits where the imposition of a BRS has come to an end or has been cancelled by the Secretary of State under section 24 of the Act.

items.label: Business rate supplement - expenses
items.description: LAs may deduct administrative expenses in relation to collection and recovery of the Business Rate Supplement.

items.label: Business rates - accounting provisions for BRS
items.description: A local authority must comply with accounting provisions in connection with business rate supplement.

items.label: Business rates - BRS collection and enforcement and administrative expenses
items.description: A local authority must comply with Regulations regarding collection and enforcement and administrative expenses in connection with business rate supplements.

items.label: Business rates - BRS relief
items.description: A levying authority that imposes a BRS may apply such reliefs in relation to the BRS as it thinks appropriate

items.label: Business rates - calculation of chargeable amount where BRS imposed
items.description: The authority must calculate the chargeable amount which each person who is to be subject to a BRS imposed for a financial year is to be liable to pay in respect of that year.

items.label: Business rates - compliance with guidance for BRS
items.description: Local authority must comply with guidance issued by the Secretary of State when carrying out its functions under the Act.

items.label: Business rates - directions on cancellation of BRS
items.description: A levying authority, a billing authority or a functional body must comply with a direction given to it, or a requirement imposed on it by the Secretary of State in relation to the cancellation of a BRS.

items.label: Business rates - interaction with BID levy where BRS imposed
items.description: A levying authority must set rules for the purposes of cases where a person is, by reference to a hereditament, liable for BID levy for the whole or part of a financial year in respect of which the person is, in relation to that hereditament, subject to a BRS imposed by the authority.

items.label: Business rates - notice of BRS to billing authority
items.description: A levying authority which is not a billing authority must, for each financial year for which it intends to impose a BRS, give a written notice relating to the BRS to each billing authority which is a lower-tier authority in relation to it.
