items.description: A local authority (coroner’s relevant authority) (if not paid by the coroner) must pay expenses to a person under the Regulations and return any receipts if requested.  It must reimburse the coroner in respect of payments in submitted accounts (if correct) keep a record of all fees and expenses paid for 3 years; submit those records to the Chief Coroner if requested and indemnify the Coroner for costs reasonably incurred.

items.label: Coroners - appointment of senior, area and assistant coroners
items.description: A local authority must appoint a senior coroner for its area  and area and assistant coroners as directed by the Lord Chancellor.

items.label: Coroners - provision of staff and accommodation
items.description: A local authority must secure the provision of whatever officers and other staff are needed by the coroners for that area to carry out their functions; must provide, or secure the provision of, accommodation that is appropriate to the needs of those coroners in carrying out their functions and must maintain, or secure the maintenance of, that accommodation.

items.label: Cosmetic procedures - licensing and enforcement
items.description: A local authority must issue premises and personal licences and enforce Regulations relating to the carrying out of cosmetic procedures.

items.label: Cosmetics - enforcement of regulations
items.description: The local weights and measures authority is responsible for enforcement of regulations concerning the safety and labelling of cosmetic products.

items.label: Cosmetics - inspection, sampling and seizure
items.description: The local weights and measures authority has the power to inspect premises, sample and seize goods which do not comply with regulations on cosmetic products.

items.label: Cottage holdings - prohibition
items.description: A local authority must not sell, let or acquire land to be used as a cottage holding.

items.label: Council tax - administration, penalties and enforcement
items.description: A local authority must comply with provisions regarding administration, penalties and enforcement.

items.label: Council tax - alteration of requisite calculations (England)
items.description: A local authority must comply with the Regulations when making the calculations which fall within those Regulations.

items.label: Council tax - alteration of requisite calculations (Wales)
items.description: A local authority must comply with the Regulations when making the calculations which fall within those Regulations.

items.label: Council tax - calculation of base
items.description: A local authority must follow the prescribed rules for the calculation of the council tax base

items.label: Council tax - consultation with ratepayers
items.description: A local authority must consult ratepayers in certain circumstances.

items.label: Council tax - default reduction schemes
items.description: The regulations contain the default scheme for reductions and appeals prescribed by the Secretary of State under the Local Government Finance Act 1992 (as amended by the Local Government Finance Act 2012) where a local authority has failed to make its own scheme by 31 January.

items.label: Council tax - demand notices
items.description: Specified information must be included in council tax demand notices including the dwelling to which the notice relates, the valuation band applicable to the dwelling, the amount of council tax payable in respect of the dwelling and comparisons with the preceding year.  Precepting authorities and levying bodies must also supply information to billing authorities

items.label: Council tax - designation and nomination in relation to excessive council tax
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure relating to designation and nomination.

items.label: Council tax - discretionary charges for empty dwellings
items.description: A local authority may exercise powers under regulations relating to empty dwellings.

items.label: Council tax - discretionary discounts in England
items.description: A local authority may exercise its powers arising from regulations relating to discounts.

items.label: Council tax - discretionary discounts in Wales
items.description: A local authority may exercise powers relating to discounts contained in regulations.

items.label: Council tax - excessive council tax
items.description: A local authority must determine whether its relevant basic amount of council tax for a financial year is excessive.

items.label: Council tax - functions to be discharged only by authority
items.description: A local authority may not delegate certain matters.

items.label: Council tax - increases by precepting authority
items.description: An authority which is a major or local precepting authority must notify its billing authorities if it has set an excessive relevant basic amount of council tax for a financial year by a specified date.Where a billing authority holds a referendum on behalf of a major or local precepting authority it can recover its costs from the precepting authority unless it has failed to do so or is in default.

items.label: Council tax - information for purposes of setting council tax
items.description: A local authority must provide certain information to a billing authority in the manner prescribed by regulations.

items.label: Council tax - issue of precepts by local precepting authorities
items.description: A local authority must issue a precept in accordance with section 41.

items.label: Council tax - issue of precepts by major precepting authorities
items.description: For each financial year a major precepting authority shall issue a precept or precepts in accordance with section 40.

items.label: Council tax - levying and collection
items.description: Each local authority must levy and collect a tax, to be called council tax, which is payable in respect of dwellings situated in its area.

items.label: Council tax - listing and appeals
items.description: A local authority must comply with the content of the Regulations relating to the content of lists and appeals.

items.label: Council tax - listing of valuation bands
items.description: A local authority must comply with the content of the Regulations relating to the content of lists and appeals.

items.label: Council tax - precepting authorities information
items.description: Regulations making provision about information in council tax demand notices including the dwelling to which the notice relates, the valuation band applicable to the dwelling, the amount of council tax payable in respect of the dwelling and comparisons with the preceding year and whether an authority's relevant basic amount of council tax for a year is excessive.  Precepting authorities and levying bodies must also supply information to billing authorities.

items.label: Council tax - provision of information to any precepting authority
items.description: A billing authority must supply prescribed information within a prescribed period to any precepting authority which has power to issue a precept to the billing authority.

items.label: Council tax - provision of information to Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must comply with a request for information from the Secretary of State.

items.label: Council tax - rating appeals
items.description: A local authority must comply with the appeals procedure set out in the Regulations

items.label: Council tax - reduced amounts
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations relating to reduced amounts.

items.label: Council tax - reduction schemes
items.description: A local authority must make a council tax reduction scheme.

items.label: Council tax - reduction schemes (Wales)
items.description: A local authority (a billing authority in Wales) must make a scheme specifying the reductions which are to apply to amounts of council tax payable by persons, or classes of person considered to be in financial need.

items.label: Council tax - referendum on excessive council tax
items.description: A local authority must hold a referendum regarding its council tax in certain circumstances and take such other steps as are required.

items.label: Council tax - regulations
items.description: A local authority must comply with certain regulations made under the Act regarding powers to require information, offences and penalties.

items.label: Council tax - regulations and directions on excessive council tax
items.description: A local authority must comply with various regulations and directions.

items.label: Council tax - regulations on discounts in England
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations relating to discounts.

items.label: Council tax - regulations on discounts in Wales
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations relating to discounts.

items.label: Council tax - regulations on empty dwellings
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations relating to empty dwellings.

items.label: Council tax - restrictions on voting by members
items.description: A local authority must ensure that members do not vote in certain circumstances.

items.label: Council tax - setting of council tax
items.description: For each financial year and each category of dwellings in its area, a billing authority shall, in accordance with regulations, set an amount of council tax.

items.label: Council tax - substitute calculations by local precepting authority where excessive council tax
items.description: A local authority must make substitute calculations in certain circumstances and to take other prescribed steps.

items.label: Council tax - substitute calculations by major precepting authority where excessive council tax
items.description: A local authority must make substitute calculations in certain circumstances and take other prescribed steps.

items.label: Council tax - valuation tribunal
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure set out in the Valuation Tribunal for England (Council Tax and Rating Appeals) (Procedure) Regulations 2009/2269.

items.label: Council tax benefit - funding and administration
items.description: A local authority must fund and administer council tax benefit.

items.label: Council tax benefits - nature of benefits
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding council tax benefits.

items.label: Council tax reduction - fraud (England)
items.description: A local authority (billing authority) may require information from specified persons for the purpose of preventing, detecting and securing evidence of the commission of offences connected with a reduction under a council tax reduction scheme and impose penalties in connection with council tax reduction schemes.It may invite a person to agree to pay a penalty as an alternative to prosecution for an offence relating to the award of a reduction under a council tax reduction scheme or impose a penalty of £70 on a person in prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Council tax reduction - fraud (Wales)
items.description: A local authority (billing authority) may require information from specified persons for the purpose of preventing, detecting and securing evidence of the commission of offences connected with a reduction under a council tax reduction scheme and impose penalties in connection with council tax reduction schemes.It may invite a person to agree to pay a penalty as an alternative to prosecution for an offence relating to the award of a reduction under a council tax reduction scheme or impose a penalty of £70 on a person in prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Councils in Wales - council funds
items.description: A local authority in Wales must establish and maintain a council fund.

items.label: Councils in Wales - service agency agreements
items.description: A local authority in Wales may enter into a service agency agreement with another.

items.label: Counter terrorism - assessment and support panel
items.description: A local authority must ensure that there is an assessment and support panel for its area.

items.label: Counter terrorism - compliance with guidance
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State or from Welsh Ministers.

items.label: Counter terrorism - membership of assessment and support panel
items.description: A local authority must be a member of the assessment and support panel for its area, appoint a representative and co-operate with the other members in carrying out its functions.

items.label: Counter terrorism - prevention of people from falling into terrorism
items.description: A local authority must, in the exercise of its functions, have due regard to the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism.

items.label: Counter terrorism - regard to guidance from Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must, in the exercise of its duty under the Act, have regard to Guidance from the Secretary of State.

items.label: Country parks - provision
items.description: A local authority may provide, maintain and manage a country park, acquire land to enable it to do so and issue byelaws regarding its use.

items.label: Countryside - access agreement terms
items.description: A local authority may impose terms into access agreements to prevent land becoming excepted land.

items.label: Countryside - access agreements
items.description: A local authority may enter into an access agreement to allow public access to the open countryside.

items.label: Countryside - access orders
items.description: A local authority may make access orders in certain circumstances in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Countryside - access to open country, rivers, canals and woodlands
items.description: A local authority may exercise powers under Part V of the National Parks and Countryside Act 1949 in relation to certain strips of land bordering rivers, canals and woodlands.

items.label: Countryside - acquisition of land for public access
items.description: A local authority may acquire land for public access.

items.label: Countryside - byelaws for National Parks, AONB or access land
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws in relation to national parks, areas of outstanding natural beauty or land or a waterway to which the public are given access by an agreement or order in their area.

items.label: Countryside - camping and picnic sites
items.description: A local authority may provide camping and picnic sites and may acquire land in order to do so.

items.label: Countryside - compensation for access orders
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation where it makes an access order in certain circumstances.

items.label: Countryside - contribution to towards expenses of other local authorities
items.description: A local authority may make contributions towards expenditure incurred by any other local authority under the National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949.

items.label: Countryside - control of boats in national parks
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws to control the use of boats on lakes in a national park in its area.

items.label: Countryside - display of maps and notices
items.description: A local planning authority shall have power, as respects any land in their area which is subject to an access agreement or order, to defray or contribute towards, or to undertake to defray or contribute towards, expenditure incurred or to be incurred in relation to the land by any person interested therein in displaying, at places where the public obtain access to any such land any reproduction of the relevant map prepared by the local planning authority under section 78 of the Act of 1949, or any notice specifying restrictions on access to the land or any part thereof.

items.label: Countryside - economic and social interests
items.description: A local authority must have regard to agriculture, forestry and the economic and social interests of the countryside when exercising functions under various pieces of legislation.

items.label: Countryside - enforcement of access
items.description: A local authority may enforce access to the countryside in certain circumstances.

items.label: Countryside - local access forums
items.description: The appointing authority for any area shall in accordance with regulations establish for that area, or for each part of it, an advisory body to be known as a local access forum.

items.label: Countryside - maps of land subject to public access
items.description: A local authority must compile and maintain maps of land subject to public access.

items.label: Countryside - national park wardens
items.description: A local planning authority whose area consists of or includes the whole or any part of a National Park may appoint such number of persons as may appear to the authority to be necessary or expedient to act as wardens as respects any land within the National Park subject to certain conditions.

items.label: Countryside - national parks facilities
items.description: A local authority may provide various facilities for national parks in its area.

items.label: Countryside - non-discrimination for use of facilities
items.description: A local authority must not discriminate against people from outside its area in relation to the exercise of its powers under the Act.

items.label: Countryside - provision of and charging for facilities
items.description: A local authority may provide facilities in connection with the exercise of its powers under the Act and may charge for so doing.

items.label: Countryside - suspension of access due to fire risk
items.description: A local authority may suspend access to the countryside where they are satisfied that, by reason of any exceptional conditions of weather for the time being prevailing, access by the public to the land or any part of it is likely to result in fires occurring on it.

items.label: Countryside - wardens in National Parks, AONB or access land
items.description: A local authority may appoint wardens in respect of any land for which byelaws have been made or could be made under section 90.

items.label: Countryside -natural beauty and amenity
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the desirability of conserving the natural beauty and amenity of the countryside when exercising its functions as to land.

items.label: Countryside and country parks - byelaws
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws in relation to country parks and other land as specified in regulations.

items.label: COVID secure business obligations - Coronavirus Immediate Restriction Notice (CIRN)
items.description: A Coronavirus Immediate Restriction Notice can be issued by enforcement officers where rapid action is needed to close a premises or restrict an activity to stop the spread of the virus, without first issuing a CIN to stop the spread of the virus. Closure will be for a 48-hour period initially. The local authority will be required to review the notice. A CIRN can be withdrawn or allowed to expire where the premise has taken necessary steps to remedy unsafe practices.Where necessary, a local authority can decide to issue a CRN at the end of the 48 hours, so that the premises is required to close for a further 7-day period, or where it is assessed that the premises is causing a serious and imminent threat to public health, a direction can be issued under separate regulations.

items.label: COVID secure business obligations - Coronavirus Improvement Notice (CIN)
items.description: A Coronavirus Improvement Notice can be issued by a local authority when a business is failing to fulfil a provision set out in the relevant coronavirus regulations. This will often be the first step for local authority enforcement officers to encourage businesses to remedy unsafe practices. A CIN will be applied for a minimum of 48 hours. Its actual duration will be at the discretion of the local authority enforcement officer.

items.label: COVID secure business obligations - Coronavirus Restriction Notice (CRN)
items.description: A Coronavirus Restriction Notice may be issued by a local authority when there has been a breach of the provisions of the relevant coronavirus regulations, and a premises has failed to comply with the terms of a Coronavirus Improvement Notice, where this non-compliance creates a risk of exposure to coronavirus.Following the 7-day period of application, a CRN can be withdrawn or allowed to expire where the premise has taken necessary steps to remedy unsafe practices.

items.label: COVID secure business obligations - fixed penalty notices
items.description: A local authority officer designated for the purposes of this regulation may issue a fixed penalty notice to any person that the officer reasonably believes has committed an offence under this Part and is (in the case of an individual) aged 18 or over.No more than one fixed penalty notice may be issued in relation to a failure to comply with a single Coronavirus Improvement Notice, Coronavirus Immediate Restriction Notice or Coronavirus Restriction Notice.

items.label: COVID secure business obligations - prosecutions
items.description: Where a recipient issued with a Coronavirus Improvement Notice, a Coronavirus Immediate Restriction Notice or a Coronavirus Restriction Notice fails to comply with such a notice the local authority may bring about proceedings for an offence.  Proceedings may not be initiated until the end of a period of 28 days from the day after the notice was issued and may only be initiated where the appropriate fixed penalty has been paid before the end of this period.

items.label: Crematoria - temporary restrictions on use
items.description: A person who is responsible for a crematorium must ensure that, during the emergency period, the crematorium is closed to members of the public, except for funerals or burials. The above does not apply to the grounds surrounding a crematorium, including any burial ground or garden of remembrance.

items.label: Crime and disorder - anti-social behaviour orders
items.description: A local authority may apply for an anti-social behaviour order if certain conditions are met.

items.label: Crime and disorder - combination agreements
items.description: Two or more local authorities may enter into a combination agreement for their area with regard to reducing crime and disorder and must comply with prescribed requirements in so doing.

items.label: Crime and disorder - committee
items.description: A local authority must have a crime and disorder committee with powers of scrutiny and to make reports and recommendations.

items.label: Crime and disorder - consideration of crime and disorder implications
items.description: Without prejudice to any other obligation imposed on it, it shall be the duty of each authority to which this section applies to exercise its various functions with due regard to the likely effect of the exercise of those functions on, and the need to do all that it reasonably can to prevent, crime and disorder in its area.

items.label: Crime and disorder - formulation and implementation of strategies
items.description: A local authority shall, with regard to its area, in accordance with section 5 and with regulations formulate and implement a strategy for the reduction of crime and disorder, drug use and serious violence in the area.

items.label: Crime and disorder - review of anti-social behaviour orders
items.description: A local authority must take part in a review of an anti-social behaviour order in certain circumstances.

items.label: Crime and disorder - sharing of information
items.description: A relevant authority is under a duty to disclose to all other relevant authorities any information held by the authority which is of a prescribed description, at such intervals and in such form as may be prescribed.

items.label: Crime reduction - breach of drinking banning order
items.description: A local authority may bring proceedings in respect of the breach of a drinking banning order.

items.label: Crime reduction - drinking banning order in county court
items.description: A local authority may make an application in the county court for a drinking banning order or to vary or discharge that order if certain conditions are met.

items.label: Crime reduction - drinking banning order in magistrates court
items.description: A local authority may make an application in the magistrates' court for a drinking banning order or to vary or discharge that order if certain conditions are met.

items.label: Criminal Behaviour Order - review
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with the chief officer of police when reviewing a criminal behaviour order and have regard to guidance published by the Secretary of State when so doing.

items.label: Crystal glass - enforcement of regulations
items.description: A local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the description and labelling of crystal glass.

items.label: Cycle tracks - conversion of footpaths into cycle tracks
items.description: A local highway authority may, to the extent allowed by the Act, in the case of any footpath for which they are the highway authority by order made by them and either-(a)     submitted to and confirmed by the Secretary of State, or(b)     confirmed by them as an unopposed order,designate the footpath or any part of it as a cycle track, with the effect that, on such date as the order takes effect in accordance with the following provisions of this section, the footpath or part of the footpath to which the order relates shall become a highway which for the purposes of the 1980 Act is a highway maintainable at the public expense and over which the public have a right of way on pedal cycles (other than pedal cycles which are motor vehicles) and a right of way on foot.

items.label: Damage - compensation
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation for damages caused when exercising any powers of this Act where the person sustaining the damage is not in default.

items.label: Dangerous buildings - demolition and recovery of expenses
items.description: A local authority may demolish or carry out other works upon a ruinous or dangerous building or wall or anything affixed thereon if the same is not carried out by the owner and may charge the owner for that work or recover cost by selling materials.

items.label: Dangerous dogs - seizure, entry of premises and inspection
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may, with a warrant, enter premises, inspect and seize a dangerous dog and other evidence.

items.label: Dangerous excavations
items.description: A local authority may deal with dangerous excavations.

items.label: Dangerous trees
items.description: A local authority may deal with dangerous trees.

items.label: Dangerous wild animals - inspection of premises
items.description: A competent person authorised by a local authority may inspect premises for the purposes of the Act and the local authority may recover certain costs connected with the inspection.

items.label: Dangerous wild animals - licensing
items.description: A local authority shall not grant a licence for the keeping of a dangerous wild animal unless certain conditions are met.

items.label: Dangerous wild animals - seizure and disposal of animals without compensation
items.description: A local authority may seize and dispose of dangerous wild animals without compensation and recover costs in certain circumstances.

items.label: Data protection - appointment of data protection officer
items.description: All public bodies must appoint a data protection officer.

items.label: Data protection - compliance
items.description: A local authority must comply with the Data Protection Act 1998.

items.label: Data protection - GDPR compliance
items.description: All public bodies must comply with the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulations and of the Data Protection Act 2018.

items.label: Data Use and Access – Enforcement of Regulations
items.description: A local authority must, if ordered to do so by Regulations, enforce Regulations made under the Act.

items.label: Delegation of planning functions
items.description: A local planning authority must comply with Regulations issued by the Secretary of State regarding the delegation of planning functions.

items.label: Democracy - elections of councillors
items.description: A local authority must select one of the three statutory options for council elections.

items.label: Democracy - promotion or opposition of local or personal Bills
items.description: Where a local authority, other than a parish or community council, are satisfied that it is expedient to promote, or any local authority are satisfied that it is expedient to oppose, any local or personal Bill in Parliament, the local authority may, but only in accordance with regulations, promote or oppose the Bill accordingly, and may defray any expenses incurred in relation to this action.

items.label: Democracy - schemes and orders for elections
items.description: A local authority must comply with any prescribed scheme for elections or other order.

items.label: Derelict land - Planting of trees and treatment
items.description: A local authority may carry out works to improve land including derelict land including the planting of trees and may compulsorily acquire derelict land for that purpose.

items.label: Detained young persons – Keeping an EHC plan
items.description: Where an authority was maintaining an EHC plan immediately before the beginning of his or her detention or where the home authority has secured the preparation of an EHC plan the home authority must keep the EHC plan while a person is detained in relevant youth accommodation.

items.label: Detained young persons – post detention education, health and care needs
items.description: In certain circumstances a local authority must carry out an assessment of a detained persons post detention education, health and care needs.

items.label: Detained young persons – securing EHC Plan
items.description: In certain circumstances a local authority must secure an EHC plan for a detained young person.

items.label: Detained young persons – supply and charge for goods and services
items.description: A local authority may provide goods and services to a person or body providing a service to a detained young person under section 74 and may charge for the same.

items.label: Development control - response to consultation
items.description: A local authority must respond to consultation in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Development of land
items.description: A local authority may for the benefit of its area develop land including powers to construct, repair and maintain.

items.label: Direct payments - determination of eligibility
items.description: The regulations identify the eligibility criteria for persons entitled to receive direct payments from local authorities in England

items.label: Direct payments - review, repayment and termination
items.description: A responsible authority must review the making of direct payments:a) at least once within the first year of the direct payments being made, b) at appropriate intervals, not exceeding twelve months, thereafterc) where they receive information that the payment has not been used as intendedAs a result of any review they may require repayment or may terminate any provision of direct payments

items.label: Disability - National Autism Strategy
items.description: A local authority must comply with National Autism Strategy guidance issued by Secretary of State.

items.label: Disabled children - short breaks
items.description: Every local authority shall provide services designed to assist individuals who provide care for such children to continue to do so, or to do so more effectively, by giving them breaks from caring.The authority should:give families the choice to access short breaks services using a direct payment;• publish a statement of their short breaks services on their website;• keep their short breaks statement under review;

items.label: Disabled facilities grant - approved purposes
items.description: A local authority must only consider an application for a disabled facilities grant for approved purposes.

items.label: Disabled facilities grant - occupier's certificate
items.description: A local authority must only consider an application for a grant if by an occupier applicant if it is accompanied by an occupier's certificate.

items.label: Disabled facilities grant - owner's and tenant's applications
items.description: A local authority must only consider an application for a grant if certain conditions, as detailed in the legislation, are met.

items.label: Disabled facilities grant - owner's certificate
items.description: A local authority must only consider an application for a grant if by an owner applicant if it is accompanied by an owner's certificate.

items.label: Disabled facilities grant - tenant's certificate
items.description: A local authority must only consider an application for a grant if by a tenant applicant if it is accompanied by a tenant's certificate.

items.label: Disabled people - consultation on accommodation for infirm or disabled people
items.description: A local authority shall from time to time consult together with respect to the nature and extent of the accommodation needed for people who by reason of infirmity or disability (whether arising from age or otherwise) are in need of accommodation of a special character

items.label: Disabled persons - access to and facilities at public buildings
items.description: A local authority must provide parking and sanitary facilities suitable for persons with a disability in buildings to which the public has access, including maintained schools and offices.

items.label: Disabled persons - assessment by local authorities of needs of disabled persons
items.description: If it falls to a local authority to decide whether the needs of a disabled person call for the provision by the authority of any statutory services for that person, the authority shall afford an opportunity to the disabled person or his authorised representative to make, within such reasonable period as the authority may allow for the purpose, representations

items.label: Disabled persons - badges for display on motor vehicles
items.description: A local authority must issue motor vehicle badges in the prescribed form for motor vehicles driven by, or used for the carriage of, disabled persons, maintain a register of such badges and withdraw them in certain circumstances.

items.label: Disabled persons - co-option to local authority committees
items.description: A local authority when appointing a committee of the authority under any enactment, and the members of the committee include or may include persons who are not members of the authority, then in considering the appointment to the committee of such persons regard shall be had, if the committee is concerned with matters in which the chronically sick or disabled have special needs, to the desirability of appointing to the committee persons with experience of work among and of the needs of the chronically sick and disabled, and to the person or persons with that experience being or including a chronically sick or disabled person or persons.

items.label: Disabled persons - consultation before co-opting representative to committee
items.description: Where any enactment provides for the appointment or co-option to any council, committee or body of one or more persons with special knowledge of the needs of disabled persons, such appointment or co-option shall only be made after consultation with such organisation or organisations of disabled people as may be appropriate in each case.

items.label: Disabled persons - disabled persons leaving special education
items.description: Where a local authority have made a SEN statement in respect of a child and the statement is still maintained by the authority when they review the statement the authority shall at that time require the appropriate officer to give to the authority his opinion as to whether the child is or is not a disabled person.

items.label: Disabled persons - duty of local authority to take into account abilities of carer
items.description: Where a disabled person is living at home and receiving a substantial amount of care on a regular basis from another person (who is not a person employed to provide such care by any body in the exercise of its functions under any enactment), and it falls to a local authority to decide whether the disabled person's needs call for the provision by them of any services for him under any of the welfare enactments, the local authority shall, in deciding that question, have regard to the ability of that other person to continue to provide such care on a regular basis.

items.label: Disabled persons - duty to consider needs of disabled persons
items.description: When requested to do so by—(a) a disabled person,(b) his authorised representative, or(c) any person who provides care for him in the circumstances mentioned in section 8,a local authority shall decide whether the needs of the disabled person call for the provision by the authority of any services in accordance with section 2(1) or (4) of the 1970 Act (provision of welfare services).In the case of a local authority in England this section applies only if the disabled person is aged under 18.

items.label: Disabled persons - information as to need for and existence of welfare services
items.description: A local authority must appraise the need for certain welfare service, make sure that information regarding those services is generally available and is specifically provided to those in need where relevant.

items.label: Disabled persons - persons discharged from hospital
items.description: Where a local authority receive a notification given with respect to a person that a person is to be discharged from a hospital after having received medical treatment for mental disorder as an in-patient for a continuous period of not less than 6 months, the authority shall make arrangements for an assessment of the needs of that person with respect to the provision of any services under any of the welfare enactments.

items.label: Disabled persons - provision of housing services
items.description: A local authority must consider the needs of disabled persons when considering the housing need for their area.

items.label: Disabled persons - provision of welfare services
items.description: A local authority must provide certain welfare services, such as adaptations in the home, to certain individuals.

items.label: Disabled persons - public conveniences
items.description: A local authority in the provision of a public sanitary convenience must ensure that it caters, in so far as it is in the circumstances both practicable and reasonable, for the needs of disabled persons.

items.label: Disabled persons - review of expected leaving dates from full - time education of disabled persons
items.description: The authority shall keep under review the date when any disabled student is expected to cease to receive relevant full-time education.

items.label: Disabled persons - rights of authorised representatives of disabled persons
items.description: A local authority shall permit the authorised representative of a disabled person, if so requested by the disabled person to act as their representative in connection with the provision by the authority of any services in the exercise of any of their functions under the welfare enactments, or to accompany the disabled person (otherwise than as his representative) to any meeting or interview held by or on behalf of the authority in connection with the provision by them of any such services.

items.label: Disabled persons - sheltered employment
items.description: A local authority may provide employment and training opportunities designed to meet the needs of registered disabled person.

items.label: Disabled persons - taking into account ability of carer
items.description: Where a disabled person is living at home and receiving a substantial amount of care on a regular basis from another person (who is not a person employed to provide such care by any body in the exercise of its functions under any enactment), and it falls to a local authority in Wales or Scotland to decide whether the disabled person's needs call for the provision by them of any services for him under any of the welfare enactments, the local authority shall, in deciding that question, have regard to the ability of that other person to continue to provide such care on a regular basis.

items.label: Disabled persons - transition for children to adult care and support
items.description: A local authority must carry out a needs assessment under the care act for children reaching the age of 18 to whom this act applies and for whom they are responsible under the this Act.

items.label: Disclosure of information - for research purposes
items.description: A local authority may disclose information for research purposes in certain circumstances and must have regard to any Code of Practice when so doing.

items.label: Disclosure of information - relating to public sector debt
items.description: A local authority may disclose information held by the person in connection with any of the person's functions to another specified person for the purposes of the taking of action in connection with debt owed to a public authority or to the Crown. The local authority must comply with certain restrictions, any Regulations and any Code of Practice when so doing.

items.label: Disclosure of information - to gas and electricity suppliers
items.description: A local authority may disclose information to gas and electricity suppliers to improve public service delivery in certain circumstances and must have regard to regulations and any code of practice when so doing.

items.label: Disclosure of information - to Statistics and Registration Service
items.description: A local authority must disclose certain information to the Statistics and Information Service in certain circumstances.

items.label: Disposal of waste - use and charging for facilities
items.description: A local authority may permit another person to use facilities provided by the authority in pursuance of the preceding provisions of this section and may provide for the use of another person any such facilities as the authority has power to provide in pursuance of those provisions and may charge in certain circumstances.

items.label: Disused burial grounds - transfer to local authority
items.description: A local authority may accept that certain disused burial grounds be transferred into its possession.

items.label: Disused tips - compensation for damage and disturbance during remedial operations
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation for damage and disturbance arising from remedial operations and works of reinstatement in certain circumstances.

items.label: Disused tips - contribution notice for remedial operations
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances, apply to the court for a contribution order in respect of the expense involved in remedial operations and works of reinstatement.

items.label: Disused tips - criminal proceedings in relation to remedial works
items.description: A local authority may bring criminal proceedings for offences under Part II of the Act.

items.label: Disused tips - direction for remedial operations
items.description: A local authority may by notice in the prescribed form require the owner of a disused tip to carry out remedial operations or cancel such a notice.

items.label: Disused tips - grants towards expenditure for remedial works
items.description: A local authority must comply with the conditions of any grants made by the Secretary of State

items.label: Disused tips - information
items.description: A local authority may require information necessary to assess the stability of a disused tip and whether it presents a danger to public safety.

items.label: Disused tips - recovery of expenses for remedial works
items.description: A local authority may recover its expenses connected to remedial works in certain circumstances.

items.label: Disused tips - remedial operations and works of reinstatement
items.description: A local authority may carry out remedial operations and works of reinstatement in certain circumstances and may sell materials in certain circumstances.

items.label: Disused tips - right of entry for remedial operations and reinstatement
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances, enter land to carry out remedial operations and works of reinstatement.

items.label: Disused tips - right to enter land etc.
items.description: A person duly authorised by a local authority may enter land to perform inspections and investigations and to carry out exploratory tests.

items.label: Dog control orders - designation
items.description: A local authority may make an order providing for an offence or offences relating to the control of dogs in respect of any land in its area.  an offence relates to the control of dogs if it relates to one of the following matters:  (a)fouling of land by dogs and the removal of dog faeces;  (b)the keeping of dogs on leads;  (c)the exclusion of dogs from land;  (d)the number of dogs which a person may take on to any land.

items.label: Dog control orders - fixed penalty notice
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may issue a Fixed Penalty Notice in the prescribed form relating to the breach of a dog control order.

items.label: Dog control orders - request for personal details
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may require an individual to whom he wishes to issue a Fixed Penalty Notice to provide him with his name and address.

items.label: Domestic abuse - annual reports
items.description: As soon as reasonably practicable after the end of each financial year, a relevant local authority in England must submit to the Secretary of State an annual report in relation to the exercise of the authority's functions under this Part during the year. In accordance with the requirements of the section and any Regulations.

items.label: Domestic abuse - co-operation with Domestic Abuse Commissioner
items.description: A public authority must co-operate with the Domestic Abuse Commissioner when requested.

items.label: Domestic abuse - disclosure of information
items.description: A local authority may disclose certain information, in certain circumstances, when assisting the Domestic Abuse Commissioner.

items.label: Domestic abuse - domestic homicide review report
items.description: A local authority that establishes a domestic homicide review  must send a copy of any report setting out the conclusions of the review to the Domestic Abuse Commissioner.The copy must be sent as soon as reasonably practicable after the report is completed.

items.label: Domestic abuse - local partnership board
items.description: A local authority must appoint a domestic abuse local partnership board for the purposes of providing advice to the authority about—(a)  the exercise of the authority's functions under section 57, and(b)  the provision of other local authority support in the authority's area.This must be done in accordance with the requirements of that section.

items.label: Domestic abuse - monitoring of strategy
items.description: A local authority must monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of the strategy for supporting victims of domestic abuse in its area.

items.label: Domestic abuse - regard to guidance from Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the Guidance of the Secretary of State when exercising its functions under this Act.

items.label: Domestic abuse - response to Commissioner's recommendations
items.description: A local authority must respond to the Domestic Abuse Commissioner recommendations in the manner specified and within the timeframe specified by section 16.

items.label: Domestic abuse - strategy for victim support
items.description: A local authority must prepare and publish a strategy for the provision of support for victims of domestic abuse in its area.

items.label: Domestic abuse - support for victims
items.description: A local authority must assess, or make arrangements for the assessment of, the need for accommodation-based support in its area.

items.label: Door to door collections licence
items.description: A local authority must issue a door to door collections licence, in accordance with the requirements of the Act, if the requirements of the Act are satisfied.

items.label: Dry cleaning - regulation
items.description: A local authority must regulate dry cleaning activities in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Early years - assessment arrangements
items.description: An English local authority must make provision to ensure the accuracy and consistency of foundation profile assessments made by early years providers in their area.An authority must have regard to any guidance given by the Qualifications and Curriculum Authority in exercising their function with regard to foundation profile assessments.

items.label: Early years - foundation stage profile data
items.description: Local authorities must supply information about individual children receiving early years provision in their area to the Secretary of State when requested to do so.  Authorities must  ensure that schools have a secure electronic system to submit EYFS profile data and that all other EYFS providers have an appropriate means for accuratelyrecording profile results, and submitting data to their LA if requested.

items.label: Early years - learning and development requirements
items.description: Early years providers must have regard to the relevant provisions of the "Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage" published by the Secretary of State in securing that the early years provision they provide meets the learning and development requirements.

items.label: Early years - welfare requirements
items.description: A local authority must comply with obligatory requirements in relation to welfare in securing early years provision

items.label: Early years provision - information about young children
items.description: The regulations identify when a local authority will have the responsibility of the duties of a prescribed person pursuant to the Childcare Act 2006.

items.label: Education -  education for persons aged 19 and over
items.description: A local authority may secure education and training provision for persons aged 19 or over.

items.label: Education - academic and vocational qualifications
items.description: A local authority may award or authenticate academic or vocational qualifications.

items.label: Education - accessibility of schools
items.description: A local authority in England and Wales must, in relation to schools for which it is the responsible body, prepare and implement an accessibility strategy, an accessibility plan and further such strategies and plans at such times as may be prescribed.

items.label: Education - accounts of maintained schools
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must prepare, keep and distribute accounts as required by regulations.

items.label: Education - action plans in response to inspection
items.description: A local authority and the governing bodies of the schools which it maintains must complete, publish and distribute an action plan in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - additional governors in schools causing concern
items.description: A local authority may appoint additional governors in a school causing concern in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - admissions appeal arrangements
items.description: A local authority shall make arrangements for admissions appeals in accordance with any relevant provisions of the appeals code.

items.label: Education - admissions arrangements
items.description: A local authority must comply with the statutory scheme for admissions arrangements.

items.label: Education - admissions forums
items.description: A local education authority shall in accordance with regulations establish for their area a body, to be known as an admission forum, for the purpose of advising the authority on such matters connected with the exercise of the authority's functions under this Chapter as may be prescribed, and advising the admission authorities for maintained schools in the area for which the forum is established onsuch matters connected with the determination of admission arrangements, and such other matters connected with the admission of pupils,as may be prescribed.

items.label: Education - advisory services
items.description: A local authority must comply with a direction to obtain advisory services.

items.label: Education - approved qualifications for persons under 19
items.description: A local authority and the governing bodies of the schools which it maintains must ensure only approved qualifications are utilised in schools.

items.label: Education - arrangements for government of new schools
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements for the constitution of a temporary governing body for a new maintained school.

items.label: Education - assessments relating to learning difficulties
items.description: A local authority must carry out assessments for persons aged over 16, but under 25, who have learning difficulties and comply with guidance when so doing.

items.label: Education - attendance outside school premises
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may require pupils to attend anywhere outside of the school premises for the purposes of education or training.

items.label: Education - board and lodging at boarding schools
items.description: A local authority of a maintained school should charge for board and lodging provided at a boarding school in accordance with regulations.The amount of the charge should not exceed the cost to the local authority.In certain circumstances, as defined in regulations, the authority should not charge for some or all of the costs of board and lodging.

items.label: Education - categories of maintained school
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must ensure that a maintained school belongs to one of prescribed categories.

items.label: Education - certification of statements by the Auditor General for Wales
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions for certifying financial statements by the Auditor General for Wales.

items.label: Education - change of school category
items.description: A local authority or a governing body of a maintained school may change school categories.

items.label: Education - charges and remissions policy
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school must prepare, keep under review and publish a charges and remissions policy and may only charge in accordance with that policy, section 457 and regulations.

items.label: Education - charges at boarding academies
items.description: Where a registered pupil is provided with board and lodging at an academy, the authority must pay an amount which is determined by conditions as specified in Regulations to the proprietor of an academy in respect of board and lodging.

items.label: Education - charges for early years provision
items.description: Maintained schools may charge for Early Years provision where it is not provided in pursuance of the duty imposed by section 7 of the Childcare Act 2006 (duty to secure prescribed early years provision free of charge), the early years provision is for a pupil who is below compulsory school age, and must not otherwise be funded by the local authority in accordance with regulations made under section 47 of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998 (determination of school's budget share).

items.label: Education - Chief Education Officer
items.description: A local authority must appoint a chief education officer.

items.label: Education - children in youth detention
items.description: A local authority must arrange education for children (aged under 19) in youth detention.

items.label: Education - children not in mainstream education
items.description: Each local authority shall make arrangements for the provision of suitable education at school or otherwise than at school for those children of compulsory school age who, by reason of illness, exclusion from school or otherwise, may not for any period receive suitable education unless such arrangements are made for them.

items.label: Education - children not receiving education at a school
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements for the provision of suitable education at school or otherwise than at school for those children of compulsory school age who, by reason of illness, exclusion from school or otherwise, may not for any period receive suitable education.

items.label: Education - children with special educational needs in nursery education
items.description: A local authority and any education provider must have regard to the code of practice on special educational needs when discharging its duties with regard to early years/nursery education.

items.label: Education - clerk to the governing body
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must appoint a clerk in accordance with the regulations.

items.label: Education - closure of schools causing concern
items.description: A local authority must comply with a direction from the National Assembly that a school should close.

items.label: Education - co-operation with careers advisors
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must co-operate with providers of independent career guidance.

items.label: Education - code for school admissions
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with the code for school admissions.

items.label: Education - code of practice for local authorities and maintained schools
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must have regard to the code practice for local authorities and maintained schools when discharging its duties.

items.label: Education - collaboration between education bodies
items.description: Local authorities and governing bodies can develop joint working arrangements under The Education (Wales) Measure 2011 and these regulations make further provision in relation to the arrangements that may be made for their functions to be discharged by joint committees.

items.label: Education - collaboration between schools
items.description: Where prescribed by regulations the governing bodies of two or more schools maintained by a local authority may collaborate.

items.label: Education - complaints management
items.description: A local education authority must consult governing bodies and make arrangements for the consideration and disposal of complaints.    A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with Regulations regarding the provision of information.

items.label: Education - complaints procedure in maintained schools
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must establish and publicise a complaints procedure.

items.label: Education - compulsory purchase of land
items.description: A local authority may compulsorily purchase land for educational purposes where authorised to do so by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Education - consideration of parental representations
items.description: A local authority must consider and respond to parental representations.

items.label: Education - consideration of regional SEN provision
items.description: A local authority in Wales, must when directed to do so by the National Assembly, consider whether their SEN duties could be carried out more efficiently or effectively if regional provision was made.

items.label: Education - consultation and guidance on provision for named individuals
items.description: Before giving notice requiring a further education institution to provide education for a named individual, a local authority must consult the governing body of the institution, and such other persons as the authority think appropriate.In deciding whether to require a particular institution to provide education to a particular individual a local authority in England must have regard to any guidance given from time to time by the Secretary of State

items.label: Education - consultation with pupils
items.description: The local authority of a maintained school and its governing body in relation to the exercise of their school related functions must have regard to guidance about consultation with pupils.

items.label: Education - continuous service for employment on change of employer
items.description: There is a duty to recognise continuity of service for employment purposes as follows. If an employee of the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority is taken into the employment of the authority or an employee of a local authority is taken into the employment of the governing body of a school maintained by the authority his period of employment at the time of the change of employer counts as a period of employment with the second employer, and the change does not break the continuity of the period of employment.

items.label: Education - control and use of school premises
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may control and use the school premises.

items.label: Education - conversion to academy
items.description: A local authority and the school’s governing body must where an Academy order under section 4(A1) or (1)(b) take all reasonable steps to facilitate the conversion of the school into an Academy.

items.label: Education - core entitlement over school age
items.description: A local authority in England must exercise their functions in such a way as to secure that the core entitlement, as described in regulations, is satisfied in relation to persons in their area who are over compulsory school age but under 19.In exercising their functions as required, a local authority in England must have regard to any guidance given from time to time by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Education - deduction of General Teaching Council fees from salaries
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulation regarding the deduction of General Teaching Council fees from teacher's salaries.

items.label: Education - delegated budget for maintained schools
items.description: A local authority must provide the schools which it maintains with a delegated budget.

items.label: Education - designation of grammar schools
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with the legislative framework relating to the continuance and cessation of grammar schools.

items.label: Education - determination of disputes
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by them may refer a dispute with the other party to the Secretary of State.

items.label: Education - determination of post-compulsory education awards
items.description: A local education authority shall determine, in respect of each financial year, whether to grant post-compulsory education awards and, if it is going to do so in that year, whether it is to do so generally, or only in the cases of eligible persons who satisfy such criteria as may be determined by the authority.

items.label: Education - determination of school budget share in England
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the determination of a school's budget share.

items.label: Education - determination of school budget share in Wales
items.description: A local authority must comply with Regulations regarding the determination of a school's budget share or with a direct or order from the National Assembly.

items.label: Education - direct payments for person with SEN or learning disability assessment
items.description: A local authority may make direct payments in prescribed circumstances to assist persons with SEN or a learning disability assessment.

items.label: Education - directed regional SEN provision
items.description: A local authority in Wales, must comply with directions from the National Assembly regarding regional provision for SEN.

items.label: Education - direction of appointment of members of education committees
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State in relation to the constitution of education committees.

items.label: Education - direction requiring discontinuance of community or foundation special schools
items.description: A local authority must comply with a direction from the National Assembly regarding the discontinuance of community or foundation special schools.

items.label: Education - direction to admit a child to a specified school
items.description: A local authority may direct the admission of a child to a school in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - disposal of land on discontinuance of a school
items.description: A local authority must comply with provisions relating to the disposal on land on discontinuance of a school.

items.label: Education - disposal or change of use of school playing fields
items.description: A local authority must obtain the appropriate consent before disposing of or changing the use of a school playing field.

items.label: Education - distribution of information about further education institutions
items.description: A governing body of a secondary school maintained by a local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State requiring the distribution of information regarding further education.

items.label: Education - distribution of information about schools providing secondary education
items.description: A governing body of a primary school maintained by a local authority must treat all requests from secondary schools regarding the distribution of information, equally.

items.label: Education - duties in relation to welfare of children
items.description: The local authority of a maintained school and its governing body must exercise its education function with a view to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, having regard to guidance when so doing.

items.label: Education - early transfer to secondary education
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements to enable children to be withdrawn from primary education for the purpose of receiving secondary education in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - early years development partnership
items.description: A local authority in Wales must develop an early years development and childcare partnership.

items.label: Education - early years provision
items.description: A local authority must secure the early years provision (570 hours over at least 38 weeks) free of charge to the children and in the manner prescribed.

items.label: Education - education action zones or forums.
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must comply with regulations regarding education action zones or forums.

items.label: Education - education provision for persons above compulsory school age
items.description: A local authority must secure that sufficient education and training provision is provided for young people of 6th form age and for young people aged between 19 and 24 who are subject to a learning difficulty assessment and must co-operate with each other and have regard to guidance when doing so.

items.label: Education - education standards grants
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations governing education standards grants.

items.label: Education - education supervision orders
items.description: Before instituting proceedings under sections 443 or 444 of the Act, a local authority must consider whether to apply to the court for an education supervision order.

items.label: Education - educational conferences
items.description: A local education authority may organise, or participate in the organisation of, conferences for the discussion of questions relating to education, and expend such sums as may be reasonable in paying, or contributing towards, any expenditure incurred in connection with conferences for the discussion of such questions, including the expenses of any person authorised by them to attend such a conference.

items.label: Education - educational records
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulations regarding educational records.

items.label: Education - educational research
items.description: A local education authority may make such provision for conducting, or assisting the conduct of, research as appears to them to be desirable for the purpose of improving the educational facilities provided for their area.

items.label: Education - employment of children
items.description: A local authority may serve notice upon an employer requiring an employer to provide it with certain information and may serve a notice prohibiting or restricting the employer from employing children. A local authority may commence proceedings against a person who contravenes or fails to comply with such notices.

items.label: Education - encouragement for persons over compulsory school age
items.description: A local authority in England must encourage participation in education and training by persons in their area who are are over compulsory school age but under 19 or are aged 19 or over but under 25 and are subject to learning difficulty assessment.A local authority must also encourage employers to participate in the provision of education and training for such persons.

items.label: Education - encouragement of education and training for persons over compulsory school age
items.description: A local authority must encourage participation in education by young people of 6th form age and for young people aged between 19 and 24 who are subject to a learning difficulty assessment and by employers and have regard to guidance when so doing..

items.label: Education - encouragement of employers and pupils to participate in work experience
items.description: A local authority must encourage participation in work experience by employers and by those eligible under section 560A.

items.label: Education - entering pupils for public examinations
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must, in certain circumstances, enter pupils for public examinations.

items.label: Education - establishment, maintenance and assistance of nursery schools
items.description: A local authority may establish, maintain and assist nursery schools.

items.label: Education - establishment, maintenance and assistance of primary and secondary schools
items.description: A local authority may establish, maintain and assist primary and secondary schools for children of compulsory school age.

items.label: Education - exemption from sex education
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with a parental request that his or her child be excused from sex education.

items.label: Education - facilities for recreation and social and physical training for school age children
items.description: A local authority must secure that the facilities for primary and secondary education provided for their area include adequate facilities for recreation and social and physical training.

items.label: Education - facilities for recreation and social and physical training in further education
items.description: A local authority may provide facilities for recreation and social and physical training as part of the facilities for further education provided (whether or not by them) for their area.

items.label: Education - facilities for recreation and training for children under 13
items.description: A local authority must secure that the facilities for primary and secondary education provided for their area include adequate facilities for recreation and social and physical training for children who have not attained the age of thirteen.

items.label: Education - failure to comply with school attendance order
items.description: A local authority may issue proceedings for breach of a school attendance order.

items.label: Education - failure to secure regular attendance at school
items.description: A local authority may issue proceedings for failing to secure regular attendance at school.

items.label: Education - federations of schools
items.description: Where prescribed by regulations the governing bodies of two or more schools maintained by a local authority may establish a federation.

items.label: Education - financial reporting
items.description: Governing bodies of maintained schools (other than maintained nursery schools and pupil referral units) must prepare annual statements, in the prescribed format, about the school's financial position at the end of year and send to the local authority who must then send the statements to the Secretary of State.

items.label: Education - financial resources for school sixth forms
items.description: A local authority and the governing bodies of the schools which it maintains must comply with any conditions laid down by Welsh Ministers relating to the allocation of financial resources.

items.label: Education - financial scheme
items.description: A local authority must prepare and maintain a financial scheme relating to the financing of schools.

items.label: Education - financial statements
items.description: A local authority must prepare financial statements as required by regulations. in respect of its educational expenditure.

items.label: Education - formation of or investment in companies to provide services
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may form a governing body company to deliver certain prescribed functions and services.

items.label: Education - free early years budget provision
items.description: A local authority proposing  to allocate an amount of relevant financial assistance to a relevant childcare provider for a funding period out of the authority's individual schools budget for the period, must comply with regulations issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Education - full-time education for 16 to 18 year olds
items.description: A local authority may secure education and training provision for young people aged 16 to 18.

items.label: Education - funded nursery education
items.description: The local authority in Wales must have regard to guidance from the Assembly when making arrangements under section 118 of the School Standards and Frameworks Act 1998.

items.label: Education - general default powers
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by them must comply with directions from the Secretary of State in relation to a declaration that they are in default of their duties.

items.label: Education - general responsibility for conduct of schools
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must conduct its school with a view to promoting high standards of educational achievement and in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Education - general responsibility for education
items.description: A local authority must in so far as their powers enable them to do so contribute towards the spiritual, moral, mental and physical development of the community by securing that efficient primary education and secondary education and, in the case of a local authority in England, further education and to achieve high standards and fulfil potential.

items.label: Education - governers' report in Wales
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by the local authority in Wales shall, once in every school year, prepare a governing body report as required by regulations.

items.label: Education - governing body reports
items.description: A local authority may require any school maintained by it to provide such reports as it requires relating to the discharge of the governing body's functions.

items.label: Education - guidance on academy conversion
items.description: A local authority and the school’s governing body must comply with the Directions of the Secretary of State regarding a proposed conversion.

items.label: Education - health and safety on school premises or for activities elsewhere
items.description: A governing body of certain maintained schools must comply with a direction given by the local authority concerning the health and safety of persons on the school's premises or taking part in any school activities elsewhere.

items.label: Education - home school agreements
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must adopt a home school agreement accompanied by a parental declaration.

items.label: Education - identifying children not receiving education
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements to identify children of compulsory school age who are not registered pupils at a school and who are not receiving suitable education otherwise than at school and have regard to guidance when so doing.

items.label: Education - implementation of National Curriculum in England
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must ensure that school implements the National Curriculum.

items.label: Education - implementation of National Curriculum in Wales
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must ensure that school implement the national curriculum.

items.label: Education - incorporation of governing body
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must be corporate and must be incorporated in accordance with regulations and having regard to guidance.

items.label: Education - infant class size
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must comply with regulations regarding infant class sizes and must prepare a statement setting out the arrangements which the authority propose to make for the purpose of securing that any limit imposed is complied with.

items.label: Education - information about child in alternative provision
items.description: A local authority may request such information regarding the education of children in alternative provision as is allowed for by the Regulations

items.label: Education - information on school hours
