items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a maintained school must comply with regulations regarding the making of information regarding school hours and other prescribed information available.

items.label: Education - information regarding admissions
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must publicise information about school admissions.

items.label: Education - information requested by school adjudicator
items.description: A local authority or a governing body of a maintained school must comply with a request by the school adjudicator for certain information.

items.label: Education - inspections of local education authorities
items.description: A local authority must provide the Chief Inspector with such information and such rights of entry as he requires in connection with an inspection.

items.label: Education - instruments of government
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must have an instrument of government which determines the constitution of the governing body and other matters relating to the school and which must accord with regulations.

items.label: Education - interim executive members for schools causing concern
items.description: A local authority may order, having taken prescribed steps that the governing body of a maintained school will consist of interim executive members.

items.label: Education - intervention in schools causing concern
items.description: A local authority may intervene in a school causing concern in certain circumstances and must take certain prescribed steps before so doing.

items.label: Education - Key Stage 1 assessments
items.description: In any school year a local authority must carry out the functions imposed on it by regulations in relation to at least 10% of the schools it maintains at which an assessment under these regulations is being administered in that school year (“monitored schools”).The authority should visit at least 10% of relevant schools and should submit information to the Department as required.

items.label: Education - late school admissions
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must not refuse to admit a child to a school where the late application was due to circumstances beyond the child's control.

items.label: Education - leisure time activities for certain under 25's
items.description: A local authority must, so far as reasonably practicable, secure for qualifying young persons in the authority's area access to sufficient educational leisure-time activities which are for the improvement of their well-being, and sufficient facilities for such activities; and  sufficient recreation and leisure-time activities for the same purpose.

items.label: Education - local curricula for students age 16 to 18
items.description: A local authority and the governing bodies of the schools which it maintains must ensure delivery of local curricula entitlements.

items.label: Education - local curriculum for key stage 4
items.description: A local authority must form for its area one or more local curricula in accordance with section 116A of the 2002 Act and these Regulations in sufficient time before the start of a school year to enable pupils to elect to follow a course of study in accordance with regulation 8.

items.label: Education - local curriculum key stage 4 in Wales
items.description: A local authority must form, plan and deliver one or more local curricula for key stage 4 pupils in the prescribed manner.

items.label: Education - maintenance and other funding of schools
items.description: A local authority must maintain a maintained school and defray its expenditure.

items.label: Education - manner of provision of sex education
items.description: The governing body and head teacher shall take such steps as are reasonably practicable to secure that where sex education is given to any registered pupils at a maintained school, it is given in such a manner as to encourage those pupils to have due regard to moral considerations and the value of family life. and must have due regard to guidance when so doing.

items.label: Education - modifications to employment legislation
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with modifications made to employment legislation applying during financial delegation.

items.label: Education - modifications to trust deeds
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with modifications made by order to trust deeds.

items.label: Education - National Curriculum exceptions by direction and regulations in England
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must modify or not apply the National Curriculum where directed to do so by the Secretary of State

items.label: Education - National Curriculum exceptions by direction and regulations in Wales
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must modify or not apply the national curriculum where directed to do so by the Assembly.

items.label: Education - National Curriculum minimum requirements in England
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must ensure that school meets the minimum requirements on the National Curriculum as set out in section 78 of the Act.In exercising any function which may affect the provision of sex education in maintained schools every local authority in England must have regard to relevant guidance issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Education - National Curriculum minimum requirements in Wales
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must ensure that school meets the minimum requirements on the national curriculum as set out in section 99 of the Act.

items.label: Education - new schools
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations relating to new schools.

items.label: Education - notice by governing body to discontinue foundation or voluntary school.
items.description: A governing body of a foundation or voluntary school wishing to discontinue the same must give notice as required by this section.

items.label: Education - notification of pupil not entitled to course of study
items.description: A headteacher must comply with the Regulations when deciding not to award or to remove an entitlement of a pupil to a course of study.

items.label: Education - nursery education
items.description: A local authority must secure provision for nursery education in accordance with regulations and guidance.

items.label: Education - nutritional requirements for food and drink on school premises
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulations relating to nutritional standards for food and drink provided on school premises.

items.label: Education - parent council for foundation school
items.description: A governing body of certain foundation schools maintained by a local authority must establish a parent council in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Education - parental preferences
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements for enabling parents to express a parental preference and to provide advice or assistance in respect of the same.

items.label: Education - parenting contracts
items.description: LAs/Governing Bodies applying or entering into must bear the costs associated with the requirements of parenting orders or contracts including in each case the costs of providing counselling or guidance programmes and may recover the costs from another LA or GB by agreement

items.label: Education - participation in international surveys
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with a request from the Secretary of State that it participates in a survey.

items.label: Education - partnership agreements and statements
items.description: A local authority must enter into a partnership agreement with the governing body of each school maintained by that authority, or each such school of a prescribed class when required to do so by Regulations.

items.label: Education - payment of fees for SEN pupils at non-maintained schools
items.description: A local authority must pay fees for SEN pupils attending institutions not maintained by a local authority in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - payment of school expenses and grants
items.description: A local authority, for the purpose of enabling persons to take advantage of any educational facilities available to them, may in such circumstances as may be specified in or determined in accordance with regulations pay such expenses of children attending community, foundation, voluntary or special schools as may be necessary to enable them to take part in any school activities and grant scholarships, exhibitions, bursaries and other allowances in respect of persons over compulsory school age.

items.label: Education - payments in respect of dismissal
items.description: A local authority must meet the cost of the dismissal, resignation or retirement of staff employed by the governing body in schools maintained by the same in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - penalty notice for failure to secure regular attendance at school
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may issue a penalty notice where it appears that a parent has committed an offence under section 444.

items.label: Education - permitted charges for pupils at maintained schools
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school may charge for matters allowed for by section 455.

items.label: Education - persons detained in youth accommodation
items.description: A local authority has certain duties arising from and restricted to the purpose of regulations in respect of persons detained in youth accommodation.

items.label: Education - pilot schemes for direct payments
items.description: A local authority must comply with an order from the Secretary of State regarding pilot schemes for assisting persons with SEN or a learning disability assessment with direct payments.

items.label: Education - political indoctrination
items.description: A local education authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must forbid political indoctrination and adopt a balanced approach to political issues.

items.label: Education - post-compulsory education awards
items.description: A local education authority shall have power, in any financial year in relation to which this regulation applies to them, to grant a post-compulsory education award, that is to say a scholarship, an exhibition, a bursary, or an other allowance, granted in respect of an eligible person for the purpose of enabling that person to take advantage of any educational facilities available to him.

items.label: Education - primary and secondary schooling
items.description: A local authority must secure sufficient primary and secondary schooling in their area for the needs of all children of compulsory school age. This includes securing that special educational provision is made for pupils who have special educational needs and the expediency of securing the provision of boarding accommodation (in boarding schools or otherwise) for pupils for whom education as boarders is considered by their parents and the authority to be desirable.

items.label: Education - prohibition of charges for admission to a maintained school
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school must not charge for admission to the school in relation to the provision of education to pupils of compulsory school age or for full time education for those aged over 16, but under 19.

items.label: Education - prohibition of charges for provision of education at a maintained school
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school must not charge for education for registered pupils unless it is allowed for by the sections 451 or 452 or by Regulations.

items.label: Education - prohibition of incidental charges
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school may not charge for incidental charges save where allowed for by section 454 or by regulations.

items.label: Education - prohibition on charging for examination fees
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school may not charge for entering registered pupil into a prescribed public examination.

items.label: Education - promotion of high standards in primary and secondary education
items.description: A local authority must exercise its functions so as to promote high standards, ensure fair access to opportunity for education and training and fulfilment of potential.

items.label: Education - property on trust
items.description: A local authority may hold and administer property upon trust for educational purposes.

items.label: Education - proposals for discontinuance of a maintained school
items.description: A local authority must publish its proposals for the discontinuance of a community, voluntary, foundation or maintained nursery school in accordance with this section.

items.label: Education - proposals for establishment or alteration of a maintained school
items.description: A local authority must publish its proposals for the establishment or alteration of a community, voluntary or foundation school in accordance with this section.

items.label: Education - proposals regarding community or foundation special schools
items.description: A local authority must publish its proposals for the establishment, alteration or discontinuance of community or foundation special schools in accordance with this section.

items.label: Education - provision and funding of higher education in maintained schools
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may arrange the provision to pupils at the school courses in preparation for professional examinations at a higher level or providing education at a higher level.      A governing body may exercise the power in relation to a particular pupil only if they are satisfied that the provision to that pupil of the course in question will not to any significant extent interfere with the other education with which he is being provided at the school.

items.label: Education - provision for improving behaviour
items.description: The governing body of a maintained school may require any registered pupil to attend at any place outside the school premises for the purpose of receiving educational provision which is intended to improve the behaviour of the pupil.  Any such provision must comply with regulations.

items.label: Education - provision for named individuals
items.description: A local authority may by notice given to the governing body of an institution in England within the further education sector, which provides education suitable to the requirements of persons over compulsory school age but under the age of 19, require them to provide specified individuals with such education falling as is appropriate to the individuals' abilities and aptitudes or withdraw such a requirement.A local authority may specify an individual in a notice only if the individual is in the authority's area, and is over compulsory school age but under the age of 19.

items.label: Education - provision for persons over compulsory school age
items.description: A local authority in England must secure that enough suitable education and training is provided to meet the reasonable needs of persons in their area who are over compulsory school age but under 19, and persons in their area who are aged 19 or over but under 25 and are subject to learning difficulty assessment.

items.label: Education - provision of board and lodging
items.description: A local authority may provide board and lodging for certain children and young people subject to certain conditions.

items.label: Education - provision of careers guidance in schools
items.description: The governing body of a school maintained by the local authority, or the local authority for a pupil referral unit, must ensure that pupils are provided with independent career guidance.

items.label: Education - provision of careers information at schools and other institutions
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must provide pupils with careers information.

items.label: Education - provision of community facilities
items.description: The governing body of a maintained school shall have power to provide any facilities or services whose provision furthers any charitable purpose for the benefit of pupils at the school or their families, or people who live or work in the locality in which the school is situated.

items.label: Education - provision of curriculum information
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must provide a careers information provider with such curriculum information as it requests.

items.label: Education - provision of education at non-maintained schools
items.description: A local authority may arrange for primary or secondary educational provision at schools not maintained by a local authority.

items.label: Education - provision of education for those aged over sixteen
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must decide whether or not to provide education to those aged 16+ but must only cease provision with the consent of the local authority.

items.label: Education - provision of higher and further education
items.description: A local authority shall have power to secure the provision for their area of such facilities for higher education as appear to them to be appropriate for meeting the needs of the population of their area; secure the provision of higher education for persons [from other areas] and do anything which appears to them to be necessary or expedient for the purposes of or in connection with such provision.

items.label: Education - provision of information
items.description: A local education authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulations regarding the provision of information.

items.label: Education - provision of information on learner travel
items.description: A local authority must provide such of the information specified in Part 2 of the Schedule to these Regulations as is in its possession on request and free of charge to the persons prescribed in the regulations

items.label: Education - provision of information to the Secretary of State by governing body
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with a request from the Secretary of State for certain information.

items.label: Education - provision of teaching services for day nurseries
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may provide teaching services to day nurseries in certain circumstances with the approval of the local authority.

items.label: Education - provision of work experience for people over compulsory school age
items.description: A local authority may secure the provision of work experience for people aged between 16 and 18. It may also secure work experience for people aged between 19 and 24 who are subject to a learning disability assessment.

items.label: Education - publication and provision of materials
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school in Wales, must publish and provide certain materials when directed to do so by the National Assembly.

items.label: Education - publication of learner travel information
items.description: A local authority must publish the information specified in Part 1 of the Schedule to these Regulations in the manner prescribed and at the times prescribed.

items.label: Education - pupil or student information
items.description: The responsible person must provide relevant information about a pupil or student who is attending an educational institution to an English local authority with an education function where that information is required for the provision of services under section 68 and 70 of the same act..

items.label: Education - pupil referral units (PRU)
items.description: Local authorities must establish management committees to run pupil referral units (PRUs) in their area, and make provision for the constitution and procedures of such committees.

items.label: Education - pupil registration
items.description: The proprietor of every school shall cause to be kept an admission register and except in the case of a school of which all the pupils are boarders, an attendance register.The contents of the admissions register and the attendance register must be as specified in regulations.

items.label: Education - pupils to be educated in accordance with their parents' wishes
items.description: A local authority must in performing its powers and duties must have regard to the general principle that children should be educated in accordance with their parents' wishes in so far as that is compatible with the provision of efficient instruction and training and the avoidance of unreasonable public expenditure.

items.label: Education - pupils with EHC plan in England
items.description: The special educational provision for any pupil specified in an EHC plan maintained for the pupil may include provision—  excluding the application of the National Curriculum for England, orapplying the National Curriculum for England with such modifications as may be specified in the plan.

items.label: Education - pupils with statements of special educational needs in Wales
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may not apply or may modify the national curriculum in statements of special educational need.

items.label: Education - rationalisation of school places
items.description: A local authority and a governing body of a school maintained by it must comply with a direction from the National Assembly to bring forward proposals for the rationalisation of school places.

items.label: Education - recoupment for cross border provision
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations governing payments for cross border provision of education.

items.label: Education - recoupment for excluded pupils
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations governing recoupment for excluded pupils.

items.label: Education - recovery of wasted examination fees
items.description: A local authority or governing body of a maintained school may only recover wasted examination fees in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - registration of pupils
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must keep a school register in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Education - religious education and worship
items.description: A local authority and governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must secure due provision of religious education and collective worship and must ensure that all registered pupils take part in a daily act of collective worship.

items.label: Education - reserve power to prevent a breakdown of discipline
items.description: A local authority may exercise its reserve power to prevent a breakdown of discipline in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - restriction on selection by ability or aptitude
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may not make arrangements for admission based upon ability and aptitude other than those prescribed by legislation.

items.label: Education - revocation of school attendance orders
items.description: A local authority must revoke a school attendance order at the request of the parent in certain circumstances.

items.label: Education - school admissions for looked after children
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the admission of looked after children to schools.

items.label: Education - school attendance orders
items.description: A local authority must issue and serve a school attendance order in certain circumstances in accordance with the prescribed procedure including amendments to SEN statements where necessary.

items.label: Education - school attendance targets.
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulations regarding school attendance targets.

items.label: Education - school day and school year
items.description: Amends Regulations 3 and 4 of the Education (School Day and School Year) (England) Regulations 1999/3181 so as to reduce the number of school sessions that need to be held in school year 2021/2022 and changes the way what counts as a qualifying session in that school year.

items.label: Education - school development plans
items.description: Governing bodies must draw up a school development plan in order to assist it to exercise its responsibility for conducting a maintained school with a view to promoting high standards of educational achievement with the prescribed contents and revise it annually and following an inspection by HMI for Education and Training in Wales.

items.label: Education - school performance targets
items.description: A governing body of a maintained school  in Wales  must comply with regulations made by Welsh Ministers regarding performance targets.

items.label: Education - schools budget
items.description: LAs must make an initial determination of the schools budget before 14 February preceding a funding period and notify schools' governing bodies of the amount of their budget shares and how the budget share was calculated together with estimates of the budget shares for the following two funding periods. It must determine a formula for budget shares and consult on any changes made.  Various factors and criteria must be taken into account in determining budget shares and which must be dealt with in schemes

items.label: Education - securing of work experience placements
items.description: A local authority must encourage participation in work experience by persons in their area who over compulsory school age but under 19 or who are aged 19 or over but under 25 and are subject to learning difficulty assessment.An authority must also encourage employers to participate in the provision of work experience for such persons

items.label: Education - SEN personal budgets
items.description: Local authorities must make arrangements to ensure information, advice and support is available in relation to personal budgets for children and young people with SEN for whom there is an EHC plan.  They must consider prescribed criteria and procedures when considering whether to make; reduce; stop or request repayment of a direct payment; provide the written reasons for its decision with a right to a review.

items.label: Education - SEN regulations
items.description: Local authorities must have regard to prescribed procedures and Regulations which supplement the procedural framework for assessing a child or young person with special educational needs, and the procedure for making, reviewing, amending and ceasing to maintain an EHC plan, set out in Part 3 of the Children and Families Act 2014.

items.label: Education - sex education statements of policy
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must make, keep up to date and provide free of charge a statement of policy on sex education.

items.label: Education - staff in schools with or without religious character
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by it, must comply with regulations with regard to the appointment and dismissal of teachers at schools with or without a religious character.

items.label: Education - staffing of community, voluntary controlled, community special, maintained nursery schools
items.description: A local authority must be the employer in community, voluntary controlled, community special and maintained nursery schools and has certain powers and duties accordingly.

items.label: Education - staffing of foundation, voluntary aided and foundation special schools
items.description: A governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must be the employer in voluntary aided and foundation and foundation special schools and has certain powers and duties accordingly.

items.label: Education - students age 16 to 18
items.description: Local authorities/schools must make the determination of the pupil's relevant school or institution under section 33D(1) of the 2000 Act within 5 working days following receipt of the pupil's request The school/local authority must follow a prescribed procedure when determining, reviewing or determining whether the student is entitled to follow or continue with a course of study.

items.label: Education - supply of information following teacher dismissal
items.description: The local authority of a maintained school must where appropriate supply the Secretary State with prescribed information in a situation where a teacher's employment terminates in circumstances where there is (alleged) gross misconduct.

items.label: Education - supply of information to General Teaching Council
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulation requiring them to supply information to the GTC for Wales in circumstances relating to dismissals or resignations relating to misconduct or incompetence.

items.label: Education - suspension of delegated budget for financial mismanagement
items.description: A local authority may suspend a delegated budget of a maintained school for financial mismanagement.

items.label: Education - suspension of right to a delegated budget for schools causing concern
items.description: A local authority may, having taken prescribed steps, suspend the right of the governing body of a maintained school to a delegated budget.

items.label: Education - suspension of statutory requirements
items.description: A local authority may apply to the Secretary of State or National Assembly to have certain statutory requirements suspended or altered.  The application must be in the prescribed form and the application process is subject to prescribed steps.

items.label: Education - teacher appraisal
items.description: The local authority of a maintained school and its governing body must comply with regulations regarding teacher appraisals.

items.label: Education - teacher health and fitness
items.description: The local authority of a maintained school and its governing body must comply with regulations regarding teacher health and fitness for certain activities.

items.label: Education - teachers pay and conditions
items.description: A local authority and governing body of a maintained school must ensure that maintained schools comply with an Order and any guidance made regarding teachers pay and conditions.

items.label: Education - teachers pay and conditions in education action zones
items.description: A governing body of a maintained school may where there is an education action zone in force apply to the Secretary of State for an order giving it control over teachers pay and conditions.  The local education authority shall do anything necessary to give effect to the governing body's determination.

items.label: Education - teaching services for day nurseries
items.description: Subject to the concurrence of the governing body of the school, a local education authority may, in accordance with arrangements made by them for that purpose, make available to a day nursery the services of any teacher who is employed by them in a nursery school or in a primary school having one or more nursery classes, and has agreed to provide his services for the purposes of the arrangements.

items.label: Education - temporary exceptions to National Curriculum for individual pupils in England
items.description: A head teacher of a school maintained by a local authority may, where prescribed, not apply or may modify the national curriculum in relation to an individual pupil.

items.label: Education - temporary exceptions to National Curriculum for individual pupils in Wales
items.description: A head teacher of a school maintained by a local authority may, where prescribed, not apply or may modify the National Curriculum in statements of special educational need in relation to an individual pupil.

items.label: Education - term and holiday dates
items.description: A local authority or the governing body, depending on the type of maintained school, must set the start and end dates of school terms and comply with regulations when so doing.

items.label: Education - training and support of governors
items.description: The local education authority shall (to the extent that they are not otherwise required to secure the provision of such information) secure that every governor is provided, free of charge, with such information as they consider appropriate in connection with the discharge of his functions as governor, and secure that there is made available to every governor, free of charge, such training as they consider necessary for the effective discharge of those functions.

items.label: Education - transfer of staff and land
items.description: A local authority must comply with staff and land transfer provision in  respect of schools which become community, foundation, voluntary or community special schools.

items.label: Education - transition plans
items.description: A governing body of a maintained school must co-operate with other governing bodies to draw up transition plans from primary to secondary school and comply with guidance.

items.label: Education - unreasonable exercise of functions
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by them must comply with directions from the Secretary of State in relation to an unreasonable exercise of their functions.

items.label: Education - voluntary contributions for the benefit of the school
items.description: A local authority or the governing body of a maintained school may request or receive voluntary contributions  for the benefit of the school or any school activities that accord with section 460.

items.label: Education - warning notice for schools causing concern
items.description: A local authority must comply with a direction from the Welsh Ministers to issue a Teachers' pay and conditions warning notice.

items.label: Education and children's social work - expenditure
items.description: A local authority must comply with a request of Secretary of State for information about planned and actual expenditure on education or children's social services functions

items.label: Education and training - provision for 14 - 19 year olds
items.description: A local authority must incorporate arrangements as to education and training suitable to the requirements of persons during the period beginning with the start of the academic year in which they attain the age of 15 and ending when they attain the age of 19 into co-operation arrangements under section 10 of the Children Act 2004.

items.label: Education and training - sharing of information
items.description: Any person authorised by the relevant legislation may provide information to a person or organisation identified in the legislation for the purpose of enabling or facilitating any relevant function related to education and training.

items.label: Education and training - supplementary powers for provision of services
items.description: A local authority may co-operate with another local authority in delivering its section 68 duty under the same act and may provide, secure the provision of or participate in the provision of services for encouraging, enabling or assisting the effective participation in education or training of—(i)young persons, or(ii)relevant young adults,(including such persons from other areas) otherwise than in accordance with section 68.

items.label: Education and training - young people and young adults
items.description: A local authority must make available to young persons and relevant young adults such services as it considers appropriate to encourage, enable or assist the effective participation of those persons in education or training.

items.label: Education establishment and registered childcare providers - complying with temporary continuity direction
items.description: A local authority must comply with a temporary continuity direction given by the Secretary of State (England) or by Welsh Ministers (Wales) relating to education, training or childcare and ancillary services of facilities.

items.label: Education establishment and registered childcare providers - disapplying or modifying enactments
items.description: A local authority must comply with Notices given by the Secretary of State (England) or by Welsh Ministers (Wales) disapplying or modifying enactments relating to such facilities. The enactments that can be disapplied of modified are defined by the Schedule 16, but this list is subject to amendment by the Secretary of State or Welsh Ministers by passing of Regulations.

items.label: Education establishment and registered childcare providers - issuing of temporary continuity direction
items.description: A local authority if and to the extent that powers are delegated to it, by the Secretary of State or by Welsh Ministers, may issue temporary continuity directions relating to education, training or childcare and ancillary services of facilities.

items.label: Education establishment and registered childcare providers - publication of temporary continuity direction
items.description: Where a local authority has been authorised to issue temporary continuity directions the authority must publish such directions and must give a copy of the directions to the person responsible for the facility to which the direction applies.  The published version of the direction should not identify any individual without their permission.

items.label: Education establishments and childcare providers temporary closure - direction
items.description: The local authority must comply with any temporary closure direction that requires the responsible body of any educational institution or registered childcare provider to which the direction applies to take reasonable steps to secure that persons do not, for a specified period, attend premises of the institution.

items.label: Elections - alteration to years of ordinary elections of parish councillors
items.description: A district council may pass a resolution to alter the years in which parish councillors are elected.

items.label: Elections - appointment of registration officer
items.description: In England the council of every district and London borough shall appoint an officer of the council to be registration officer for any constituency or part of a constituency conterminous with or situated in the district or borough, in relation to any constituency part of which consists of some or all of the area of the City and the Inner and Middle Temples, the Common Council shall appoint an officer to be registration officer for that part of the constituency and in Wales, the council of every county or county borough shall appoint an officer of the council to be registration officer for any constituency or part of a constituency coterminous with or situated in the area of the council.

items.label: Elections - appointment of returning officer
items.description: In England every non-metropolitan county council shall appoint an officer of the council to be the returning officer for elections of councillors of the county and every district council shall appoint an officer of the council to be the returning officer for the elections of councillors of the district and an officer of the council to be the returning officer for elections of councillors of parishes within the district. In Wales the council of every county or county borough shall appoint—an officer of the council to be the returning officer for elections of councillors of the county or county borough; andan officer of the council to be the returning officer for elections of councillors of communities within the county or county borough.

items.label: Elections - assistance to returning officer
items.description: A local authority may appoint officers to assist the returning officer.

items.label: Elections - change of name of electoral area
items.description: A local authority may pass a resolution to change the name of an electoral area.

items.label: Elections - discharge of registration duties
items.description: It shall be the duty in England, of a district council or London borough council and in Wales, of a county or county borough council to assign such officers to assist the registration officer as may be required for carrying out his functions under this Act.

items.label: Elections - notice to Electoral Commission on passing resolution for election by halves or thirds
items.description: A district council adopting a scheme for elections by halves or by thirds must inform the Local Government Boundary Commission for England that it has passed that resolution.

items.label: Elections - notice to Electoral Commission on passing resolution for whole council elections
items.description: A district council passing a resolution for whole council elections must give notice of that resolution to the Local Government Boundary Commission for England.

items.label: Elections - notification of change of name of electoral area
items.description: A local authority must obtain the approval of the Electoral Commission before changing the names of certain electoral areas and must inform the Electoral Commision, the Boundary Commission for England, Office of National Statistics and the Director General of the Ordnance Survey once the resolution has been passed.      In a two tier area a county must inform the district or a district inform the county within whose area the electoral area lies.

items.label: Elections - order by Electoral Commission for election by halves or thirds
items.description: A council must produce an explanatory document and make the document available for inspection as soon as practicable after the Electoral Commission have made an order for elections by halves or for elections by thirds in relation to it.

items.label: Elections - polling districts and stations
items.description: For elections of county councillors in England, the county council may divide an electoral division into polling districts, and may alter any polling district, and for elections of London borough or district councillors the London borough or district council may divide the London borough or district or any ward thereof into polling districts, and may alter any polling district.For elections of county or county borough councillors in Wales, the county or county borough council may divide an electoral division into polling districts and may alter any polling district.

items.label: Elections - publicity of explanatory document for elections by halves or thirds
items.description: A district council adopting a scheme for elections by halves or by thirds must, produce make available and publicise an explanatory document.

items.label: Elections - publicity of explanatory document for whole council elections
items.description: A district council adopting a scheme for whole council elections must, produce and publicise an explanatory document.

items.label: Elections - register of electors - compilation and maintenance
items.description: A Registration Officer shall compile, canvass for and maintain a register of electors for both national and local elections.

items.label: Elections - register of electors - publication
items.description: A Registration Officer shall publish a revised version of the Register of Electors in certain circumstances and make certain alterations.

items.label: Elections - register of proxies
items.description: A registration officer may require another registration officer to provide information as soon as reasonably practicable about whether a proxy has an entry in a relevant register.

items.label: Elections - resolution for elections by halves
items.description: A non-metropolitan district council that was formerly subject to a scheme for elections by halves, but is for the time being subject to a scheme for whole-council elections, may resolve that it is to revert to being subject to a scheme for elections by halves.    The council must comply with requirements when passing a resolution for elections by halves.

items.label: Elections - resolution for elections by thirds
items.description: A district council that was formerly subject to a scheme for elections by thirds, but is for the time being subject to a scheme for whole-council elections,may resolve that it is to revert to being subject to a scheme for elections by thirds.  A council must comply with requirements in passing a resolution for elections by thirds.

items.label: Elections - resolution for whole-council elections
items.description: A district council that is subject to a scheme for elections by halves or by thirds may resolve that it is to be subject instead to the scheme for whole-council elections.  A council must comply with requirements in passing a resolution for whole-council elections.

items.label: Electoral areas - provision of information to Boundary Commission
items.description: A local authority must comply with a request for information from the Local Government Boundary Commission for England in connection with its functions under the Act.

items.label: Electoral areas - request for Boundary Commission review.
items.description: A local authority may request the Local Government Boundary Commission for England to conduct a review of the Council's area and make recommendations as to single member electoral areas.

items.label: Electoral register - supply of information
items.description: Local authorities (electoral registration officers) must supply national and local political parties, for a limited period, with information as to whether entries on an electoral register were either made following an application under the system of individual electoral registration or were included as a result of the entry having been confirmed in accordance with the transitional arrangements for the new system. The information may only be used for the purposes of electoral registration (or of civil or criminal proceedings) and may not be used after 7th May 2015.

items.label: Electrical equipment safety - enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Regulations relating to electrical equipment for domestic use .

items.label: Emergencies - advice and assistance to the public
items.description: A local authority shall provide advice and assistance to the public in connection with the making of arrangements for the continuance of commercial activities by the public, or the continuance of the activities of bodies other than public or local authorities whose activities are not carried on for profit, in the event of an emergency. and must comply with regulations and have regard to guidance when so doing.

items.label: Emergencies - assess, plan and advise
items.description: A local authority must assess risk in respect of emergencies, prepare and maintain plans as prescribed and in so doing comply with Regulations and have regard to guidance.

items.label: Emergencies - charging for advice and assistance
items.description: A local authority may charge for advice and assistance in relation to the giving of information to the public regarding the continuation of certain activities during an emergency as allowed for by regulations.

items.label: Emergencies - consultation, co-operation and delegation
items.description: A Minister of the Crown may by order require an authority to perform a function in connection with an emergency.  The order may require the authority to consult, collaborate, delegate, co-operate or provide information to another person or body.

items.label: Emergencies - disclosure of information
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding disclosure of information in connection with a function of the provider or of the recipient which relates to emergencies.

items.label: Emergencies - enforcement action
items.description: A local authority may take enforcement action in respect of the failure by another responsible authority to comply with the Act.

items.label: Emergencies - provision of information to Government
items.description: A local authority must comply with a request from a Minister of the Crown for information about action taken in relation to any emergency.

items.label: Emergencies or disasters - expenditure
items.description: A local authority may incur expense or make grants or loans to certain bodies in certain circumstances in situations where there is an emergency or a disaster.

items.label: Emergency plan - extraction sites
items.description: A local authority must draw up an emergency plan, ensure compliance with and enforce the Regulations

items.label: Employment and training - arrangements
items.description: A local Authority may enter into arrangements with the Secretary of State pursuant to the Employment  and Training Act 1973

items.label: Employment of children - byelaws
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws to regulate the employment of children.

items.label: Employment of children in sreet trading - byelaws
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws to regulate the employment of children in street trading.

items.label: Energy information - enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure that suppliers are in compliance with regulations relating to indication by labelling and standard product information of the consumption of energy and other resources by energy-related products.  The authority has a duty to enforce these regulations.

items.label: Energy measures report - regard when exercising functions
items.description: A local authority must have regard to energy measures reports published by the Secretary of State when exercising their functions.

items.label: Energy performance of buildings - enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to enforce regulations regarding the energy performance of buildings and the availability of energy performance certificates.  The authority has a duty to enforce these regulations.

items.label: Entertainment - provision of facilities
items.description: A local authority may provide or contribute to the provision of certain entertainments for use by the public.

items.label: Environment - assessment of damage and remediation
items.description: Where the Regulations apply to the local authority and damage has been caused the local authority must assess that damage notify the operator of any remedial action and in certain circumstances served a remediation notice in the prescribed form.

items.label: Environment - co-operation regarding flood risk
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with other named bodies when exercising its functions under these Regulations.

items.label: Environment - compensation for damage under instruction
items.description: Where local authority has instructed the operator to takes steps that have themselves resulted in environmental damage the authority may have to pay certain costs to the operator.

items.label: Environment - damage enforcement notice
items.description: Where the regulations apply to the local authority and environment damage seems likely the local authority must take all practicable steps, may serve an enforcement notice and may carry out certain operations itself.

items.label: Environment - damage prevention and remediation
items.description: Where a local authority has granted a permit pursuant to Part II or in some circumstances Part III of the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2010 it must enforce that permit.

items.label: Environment - damage under environmental permitting
items.description: If damage as prescribed is caused by an activity that requires a permit or registration under the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2010 and the LA is responsible for granting the permit, the LA must enforce the provisions of Part 2 and, if the damage is to land, Part 3.

items.label: Environment - flood risk and flood hazard maps
items.description: A local authority must prepare (within any time limits prescribed) in relation to each relevant flood risk area—(a) a flood hazard map, and(b) a flood risk map.Following a review by the lead agency, a local authority may revise its flood hazard map or flood risk map.

items.label: Environment - flood risk assessment
items.description: A local authority must, (subject to Part V) prepare a preliminary assessment report in relation to flooding in its area and a Welsh local authority must do so by a prescribed date. The local authority must have regard to relevant guidance when so doing.

items.label: Environment - flood risk assessment review
items.description: A local authority must  (subject to Part V) review—(a) the preliminary assessment report prepared by it under regulation 10, and(b) its determination and identification of flood risk areas under regulation 14.Following a review, a lead local authority may prepare a revised preliminary assessment report.The first review must be completed before 22nd June 2017.Subsequent reviews must be carried out at intervals of no more than 6 years.

items.label: Environment - flood risk management plan
items.description: A local authority must prepare (within any time limits prescribed) a flood risk management plan in relation to each relevant flood risk area.Following a review by the lead agency, a local authority may revise its flood risk management plan.

items.label: Environment - information requests regarding flood risk
items.description: A local authority may require information in relation to the exercise of its functions under the Regulations from certain other bodies.

items.label: Environment - provision of information regarding flood risk
items.description: A local authority must provide information to certain bodies in relation to the exercise of the functions of those bodies under the Regulations.

items.label: Environment - review of flood hazard and flood risk maps
items.description: A local authority must review each flood hazard map and each flood risk map prepared by it under regulation 19.Following a review, a lead local flood authority may prepare—(a) a revised flood hazard map;(b) a revised flood risk map.The first review must be completed before 22nd June 2019.Subsequent reviews must be carried out at intervals of no more than 6 years.

items.label: Environment - review of flood risk management plan
items.description: A local authority must review its Flood Risk Management PlanFollowing a review, a lead local flood authority may prepare—(a) a revised flood hazard map;(b) a revised flood risk map.The first review must be completed before 22nd June 2021.Subsequent reviews must be carried out at intervals of no more than 6 years.Following a review, the lead local flood authority must prepare a revised flood risk management plan.

items.label: Environment - significant flood risk
items.description: A local authority must (subject to Part V)—determine whether, in its opinion, there is a significant flood risk in its area, andidentify the part of the area affected by the risk (the “flood risk area).In so doing it must also have regard to appropriate guidance and the dispute resolution mechanism in relation to the final determination

items.label: Environmental damage - appointment of authorised persons
items.description: Where the Regulations apply the local authority may appoint authorised persons to exercise its powers and carry out its duties in accordance with the Regulations

items.label: Environmental damage - carrying out remedial work
items.description: Where the Regulations apply to the local authority and damage has been caused the local authority may carry out remedial works itself in certain circumstances

items.label: Environmental damage - provision of information by operator
items.description: Where the Regulations apply the local authority may require the operator to provide it with certain information

items.label: Environmental damage - recovery of costs for remedial work
items.description: Where the Regulations apply the local authority may, in certain circumstances, take action to recover its costs

items.label: Environmental damage - requests from interested parties
items.description: Where the Regulations apply the local authority must consider requests for action from interested parties

items.label: Environmental Delivery Plans - Consultation
items.description: A local authority may respond to a consultation by Natural England regarding an Environmental Delivery Plan.

items.label: Environmental Delivery Plans – Duty to co-operate
items.description: A local authority must cooperate  Natural England regarding an Environmental Delivery Plan and carry out certain development related actions when requested to do so by Natural England, having regard to Guidance from the Secretary of State when so doing.

items.label: Environmental health - EC fertilisers
items.description: The local authority has a to to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the marking of EC fertilisers.

items.label: Environmental protection - appeals as respect authorisations
items.description: A local authority must comply with the outcome of any appeal.

items.label: Environmental protection - authorisation for prescribed process
items.description: A local authority must consider applications to carry out prescribed processes.

items.label: Environmental protection - co-operation with Office for Environmental Protection
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with the office of Environmental Protection.

items.label: Environmental protection - compliance with Information Notice
items.description: A local authority must comply with the requirements of an Information Notice issued by the Office of Environmental Protection.

items.label: Environmental protection - conditions of authorisations
items.description: A local authority must place certain conditions in any authorisations.

items.label: Environmental protection - control of pesticides
items.description: If there has been a breach in relation to any pesticide the local authority shall have power to seize or dispose of it or to require that some other person shall dispose of it; to seize or dispose of anything treated with it or to require that some other person shall dispose of any such thing; or to direct some other person to take such remedial action

items.label: Environmental protection - enforcement action in the High Court
items.description: A local authority may take enforcement action in the High Court in circumstances where criminal proceedings would provide insufficient sanction.

items.label: Environmental protection - enforcement notices
items.description: If the enforcing authority is of the opinion that the person carrying on a prescribed process under an authorisation is contravening any condition of the authorisation, or is likely to contravene any such condition, the authority may serve on him a notice (an enforcement notice).

items.label: Environmental protection - enforcement powers (for control of pesticides)
items.description: An authorised person may enter any land/vehicle and/or obtain information if he has reasonable grounds to believe that any pesticide is being or has been used

items.label: Environmental protection - fees and charges for authorisations
items.description: A local authority must charge fees for authorisations in accordance with the Secretary of State's scheme.

items.label: Environmental protection - local nature recovery strategy
items.description: Where required to do so by the Secretary of State a local authority must prepare, publish and review a local nature recovery strategy.

items.label: Environmental protection - obtaining of information from persons and authorities
items.description: A local authority must provide with a Notice from the Secretary of State requesting the provision of information.

items.label: Environmental protection - prohibition notices
items.description: If the enforcing authority is of the opinion, as respects the carrying on of a prescribed process under an authorisation, that the continuing to carry it on, or the continuing to carry it on in a particular manner, involves an imminent risk of serious pollution of the environment the authority shall serve a notice (a prohibition notice) on the person carrying on the process.

items.label: Environmental protection - public register of information
items.description: A local authority must maintain a public register of prescribed information.

items.label: Environmental protection - response to decision notice
items.description: A local authority must respond to a decision notice issued by the Office of Environmental Protection within the period allowed for by the legislation.

items.label: Environmental protection - revocation of authorisation
items.description: A local authority may revoke an authorisation in certain circumstances.

items.label: Environmental protection - smoke free premises
items.description: Premises must be smoke free to the extent that they are open to the public or used as a place of work.

items.label: Environmental protection - variation of authorisations
items.description: A local authority may vary an authorisation in certain circumstances.

items.label: Equality - duty to eliminate discrimination, enhance equality and foster good relations
items.description: A local authority must in the exercise of its functions have due regard to the need to eliminate discrimination, enhance equality of opportunity and to enhance good relations.

items.label: Equality - prepare and publish an equality objective
items.description: A local authority must prepare and publish equality information as required by secondary legislation

items.label: Equality - public sector duty regarding socio-economic inequalities
items.description: An authority to which this duty applies must, when making decisions of a strategic nature about how to exercise its functions, have due regard to the desirability of exercising them in a way that is designed to reduce the inequalities of outcome which result from socio-economic disadvantage.

items.label: Equality - publication of information to demonstrate compliance
items.description: A local authority must publish equality information as required by secondary legislation.

items.label: Events - health and safety notifications
items.description: If in relation to a required permission to hold an event. for a reason related to the health or safety of any person, or for reasons that include such a reason, the decision has effect to—(i) stop the holding of the event,(ii) impose restrictions on the holding of the event,(iii) impose conditions to be met in connection with the holding of the event, or(iv) do all, or any two, of those things.The local authority must take prescribed steps to notify relevant people of that decision and to review that decision if required.

items.label: Execution of works outside of area
items.description: A local authority may carry out works outside of its area unless the contrary intention appears in the authorising statute.

items.label: Expenditure - concurrent functions of two or more authorities
items.description: Two or more local authorities may make arrangements for defraying any expenditure incurred by one of them in exercising any functions exercisable by both or all of them.

items.label: Expenditure - not otherwise authorised
items.description: A local authority may incur expenditure which in their opinion is in the interests of and will bring direct benefit to their area or any part of it or all or some of its inhabitants, but a local authority shall not, by virtue of this subsection, incur any expenditure for a purpose for which they are, either unconditionally or subject to any limitation or to the satisfaction of any condition, authorised or required to make any payment by or by virtue of any other enactment; nor unless the direct benefit accruing to their area or any part of it or to all or some of the inhabitants of their area will be commensurate with the expenditure to be incurred.

items.label: Explosives - licence for manufacture/storage
items.description: A local authority may issue a licence for the manufacture or storage of explosives.  Where a licence has been issued the authority may revoke, vary or transfer the licence where the conditions comply with regulations and the authority considers it appropriate to do so.

items.label: Explosives licence - enforcement
items.description: The local authority must enforce regulations relating to the manufacture and storage of explosives.

items.label: Fair trading - Sunday trading
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the Sunday Trading Act 1994.

items.label: Fairs - setting dates and abolition
items.description: A local authority shall be responsible for the abolition of fairs and moving the days upon which fairs are to be held.

items.label: Families - forced marriage protection order
items.description: A local authority is a relevant third party for the purposes of applying for a forced marriage protection order under section 63C(2) of the Family Law Act 1996

items.label: Feed hygiene - enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to animal feed hygiene, sampling etc.

items.label: Fees for licensing and inspection of dog breeding premises
items.description: A local authority may charge fees for the granting of licences or for the inspection of premises under the Act.

items.label: Fertilisers and animal feeding stuff - analysis of feeding stuff sample
items.description: An inspector appointed by a local authority must collect and have analysed any fertiliser or feeding stuff sample when requested to do so by a purchaser.

items.label: Fertilisers and animal feeding stuff - division and analysis of samples
items.description: An agricultural analyst appointed by a local authority must deal with samples taken by an inspector in the prescribed manner.

items.label: Fertilisers and animal feeding stuff - enforcement
items.description: A local authority must appoint an agricultural analyst and such inspectors and deputy agricultural analysts as they think necessary to enforce the legislation.

items.label: Fertilisers and animal feeding stuff - power of entry and to take samples
items.description: An inspector appointed by a local authority may enter premises and take samples of fertiliser or feeding stuff.

items.label: Finance - accounting practices
items.description: A local authority must comply with statutory instruments regarding the accounting practices that it should follow.

items.label: Finance - affordable borrowing limit
items.description: A local authority must determine its affordable borrowing limit.

items.label: Finance - Audit and inspection
items.description: Local authorities and fire authorities in Wales are public bodies whose accounts are required to be audited in accordance with section 39 of the Public Audit (Wales) Act 2004 and must ensure financial management of the body is adequate and effective and have a sound system of internal control which is regularly reviewed.   They must keep records, prepare accounts, sign, give notice, publicise and allow inspection as prescribed.

items.label: Finance - borrowing money
items.description: A local authority may borrow money for any purpose relevant to its functions under any enactment, or for the purposes of the prudent management of its financial affairs.  Any borrowing is subject to conditions as specified in regulations.

items.label: Finance - budget calculations
items.description: A chief finance officer of a local authority must report on the robustness of estimates and the adequacy of financial reserves.

items.label: Finance - budget monitoring
items.description: A local authority must review its budget calculations during the year from time to time.

items.label: Finance - budgets and council tax
items.description: Local authorities (billing authorities and major precepting authorities) in Wales must calculate their budget requirements for a financial year and the basic amount of their council tax as prescribed.

items.label: Finance - compliance with terms of grant for service excellence/best value
items.description: A local authority must comply with the terms of any grant made for service excellence/best value.

items.label: Finance - compliance with terms of grants
items.description: A local authority must comply with the terms of any grant made by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Finance - control of credit arrangements
items.description: A local authority must comply with restrictions imposed in relation to it entering into credit arrangements.

items.label: Finance - council funds and accounts
items.description: A local authority must comply with the rules relating to funds, accounts and returns in the manner prescribed and must appoint an officer to have overall responsibility for the administration of those affairs.

items.label: Finance - payments towards local authority indebtedness
items.description: A local authority must comply with the terms of any payment made to deal with its indebtedness.

items.label: Finance - power to invest
items.description: A local authority may invest for any purpose relevant to its functions under any enactment, or for the purposes of the prudent management of its financial affairs.

items.label: Finance - providing information to the Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must provide the Secretary of State with such information relating to borrowing and investment as he shall request.

items.label: Finance - Public service pension scheme
items.description: A local authority must comply with the pension scheme regulations made by the responsible authority.

items.label: Finance - regard to guidance from Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must comply with guidance and statutory instruments issued by the Secretary of State with regard to its borrowing and investment powers and duties.

items.label: Finance - report on inadequacy of controlled reserve
items.description: A chief finance officer of a local authority must report upon any inadequacy of any controlled reserve.

items.label: Finance - transfer of headroom
items.description: A local authority may transfer any headroom that it has in relation to a borrowing limit to another local authority in certain circumstances.

items.label: Finance - use of capital receipts
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding capital receipts

items.label: Fire and rescue - arrangements for discharge of functions by others
items.description: A fire and rescue authority may enter into arrangements with another fire and rescue service or another person to enable it to carry out its duties.

items.label: Fire and rescue - arrangements with other employers of fire-fighters
items.description: A fire and rescue authority may enter into arrangements with other (non-fire and rescue service) employers of fire-fighters to enable it to carry out its duties.

items.label: Fire and rescue - authorisation for Chief Constable to carry out Fire and Rescue functions
items.description: A Mayor of a combined authority may authorise the Chief Constable to carry out the functions of a fire and rescue authority where an Order has been made by the Secretary of State, to the extent permitted by the Order.

items.label: Fire and rescue - best value
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with the best value/measures regime.

items.label: Fire and rescue - charging by authorities
items.description: A fire and rescue authority may charge a person for any action taken by the authority in the United Kingdom or at sea or under the sea, and  otherwise than for a commercial purpose subject to provisions and limits defined in this section, sections 18B and 18C.

items.label: Fire and rescue - co-operation with creation of corporation sole
items.description: The Secretary of State may make proposals for an Order to create a corporation sole as the fire and rescue authority for the area specified in the order, andfor the person who is for the time being the police and crime commissioner for the relevant police area to be for the time being that fire and rescue authority. The relevant local authorities must cooperate with those proposals.

items.label: Fire and rescue - collaboration agreement
items.description: A Fire and Rescue Body may enter into a collaboration agreement with an ambulance trust or with a police body in England. A collaboration agreement is an agreement in writing that sets out how the parties to the agreement will work together in discharging their functions.

items.label: Fire and rescue - conditions of service of fire brigade members
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with a Direction made by the Secretary of State regarding the conditions of service of fire brigade members.

items.label: Fire and rescue - consideration of collaboration agreement
items.description: A Fire and Rescue Body must keep under consideration whether entering into a collaboration agreement with one or more other relevant emergency services in England could be in the interests of the efficiency or effectiveness of that service and those other services. The Body must share any proposals and consider any such proposals received from others.

items.label: Fire and rescue - directions for public safety purposes
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with a direction of the Secretary of State given for public safety purposes.

items.label: Fire and rescue - directions relating to particular fires and emergencies
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with direction from the Secretary of State to take, or not to take, action specified in the direction in relation to a fire specified in the direction, or an emergency of another kind specified in the direction.

items.label: Fire and rescue - directions to make arrangements with another fire authority
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with a direction of the Secretary of State to enter into arrangements under Section 16.

items.label: Fire and rescue - emergencies
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with regulations made by the Secretary of State relating to emergencies.

items.label: Fire and rescue - equipment, facilities, services and organisations
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with an order of the Secretary of State to utilise the Secretary of State's equipment or facilities etc.

items.label: Fire and rescue - exercise of powers at or under sea
items.description: If a fire and rescue authority has power to act, or is required to act, outside the authority's area, the authority may exercise the power, or perform the duty, at sea or under the sea.

items.label: Fire and rescue - fire fighting
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must make provision for the purposes of  extinguishing fires in its area, and protecting life and property in the event of fires in its area.

items.label: Fire and rescue - fire hydrants
items.description: The expenses incurred by a water authority in relation to a fire hydrant are to be borne by the fire and rescue authority in whose area the hydrant is located.

items.label: Fire and rescue - fire safety
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must make provision for the purpose of promoting fire safety in its area.

items.label: Fire and rescue - firefighters pension schemes
items.description: Fire and rescue authorities are appointed as the “scheme managers” and “scheme employer” and pay contributions and otherwise act in accordance with the regulations as prescribed.

items.label: Fire and rescue - general powers of authorities
items.description: Subject to the boundaries defined in section 5B a fire and rescue authority may do:  - anything it considers appropriate for the purposes of the carrying-out of any of its functions  - anything it considers appropriate for purposes incidental to its functional purposes  - anything it considers appropriate for purposes indirectly incidental to its functional purposes through any number of removes  - anything it considers to be connected with any of its functions, or  anything it may do under the above  - for a commercial purpose anything which it may do under any of the above paragraphs otherwise than for a commercial purpose.

items.label: Fire and rescue - improvement plans
items.description: A fire and rescue authority (Wales) must publish the required information as soon as is reasonably practicable after 31 December in the year prior to the financial year to which the improvement plan relates.

items.label: Fire and rescue - intervention by Secretary of State
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must comply with an order made by the Secretary of State under the intervention protocol.

items.label: Fire and rescue - National Framework
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must have regard to the National Framework when carrying out its functions.

items.label: Fire and rescue - obtaining information and investigating fires
items.description: A fire and rescue authority may authorise officers to enter premises at a reasonable time for the purposes of obtaining information or investigating fires.

items.label: Fire and rescue - other services
items.description: A fire and rescue authority may provide the services of any persons employed by it or any equipment maintained by it to any person for any purpose that appears to the authority to be appropriate.  A fire and rescue authority may provide services under this section outside as well as within the authority's area.

items.label: Fire and rescue - powers of fire-fighters etc in an emergency
items.description: A fire and rescue authority may authorise its fire fighters, in writing, to undertake certain actions in an emergency.

items.label: Fire and rescue - reinforcement schemes
items.description: A fire and rescue authority must enter into reinforcement schemes with other fire and rescue authorities and notify the Secretary of State when so doing.

items.label: Fire and rescue - reports, returns and information to Secretary of State
