items.label: Local government - information for overview and scrutiny
items.description: LA overview and scrutiny committees may obtain information from their relevant partner authorities, and ensure that executives of LA exclude confidential information when publishing their responses to reports and recommendations of overview and scrutiny committees.

items.label: Local government - joint discharge of functions
items.description: A local authority when adopting executive arrangements may jointly discharge its functions in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Local government - joint exercise of functions
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with Regulations relating to the joint exercise of their functions.

items.label: Local government - joint overview and scrutiny
items.description: Two or more local authorities may appoint a joint overview and scrutiny committee to make reports or recommendations to any of the authorities or their executives about matters affecting their areas and if so must comply with the administrative requirements contained in the Regulations.

items.label: Local government - local authority executives
items.description: A local authority in Wales must adopt one of the permitted forms of government.

items.label: Local government - mayor and cabinet executive
items.description: A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements consisting of a mayor and cabinet executive must accord with section 14.

items.label: Local government - mayor and council manager executive
items.description: A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements consisting of a mayor and council manager must accord with section 16.

items.label: Local government - meetings and proceedings
items.description: The meetings and proceedings of a local authority must comply with Schedule 12 of the Local Government Act 1972.

items.label: Local government - monitoring officer
items.description: A local authority must refer certain matters to its monitoring officer for investigation.

items.label: Local government - officer responsible for financial administration of certain authorities
items.description: On and after the commencement day the Common Council shall make arrangements for the proper administration of such of its financial affairs as relate to it in its capacity as a local authority, police authority or port health authority, and secure that one of its officers has responsibility for the administration of those affairs.

items.label: Local government - outline fall back proposals for executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority in Wales may apply to Welsh ministers for the approval of outline fall back proposals.

items.label: Local Government - overview and scrutiny
items.description: A local authority cannot refer to an overview and scrutiny committee the excluded matters specified in article 3, but can refer a matter which consists of an allegation of systemic failure of a LA to discharge a function for which the LA is responsible, notwithstanding the fact that the allegation specifies matters which would otherwise be excluded by virtue of article 3.

items.label: Local government - overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must include provision for an overview and scrutiny committee.

items.label: Local government - overview and scrutiny committees
items.description: A local authority in Wales must ensure that executive arrangements provide for one or more overview and scrutiny committees.

items.label: Local government - overview and scrutiny sub-committees
items.description: The overview and scrutiny committee of a local authority may appoint sub-committees.

items.label: Local government - payment of officer expenses
items.description: A local authority may pay its officers' expenses.

items.label: Local government - payments to dependants under superannuation schemes
items.description: A local authority may make payments from its superannuation fund to the dependants of employees killed in or as a result of military service.

items.label: Local government - political balance on committees, duty to allocate seats to political groups
items.description: It shall be the duty of a relevant authority having power from time to time to make appointments to a body to which this section applies to review the representation of different political groups on that body

items.label: Local government - political restriction of officers and staff
items.description: It shall be the duty of every local authority to prepare and maintain a list of politically restricted posts and deposit that list prepared with their proper officer and to revise that list as and when necessary

items.label: Local government - post election surveys
items.description: A local authority must conduct a survey after each ordinary election to the council of the county or county borough and to each community in the local authority's area by asking prescribed questions of councillors and unsuccessful candidates who have stood for election as councillors in the local authority's area. The questions relate to gender, sexual orientation, language, race, age, disability, religion or belief, health, education and qualifications, employment, work as a councillor, party affiliation, involvement with the third sector and length of political activity.  Survey information must be collated in an electronic spreadsheet. Details relating to the spreadsheet will be included in guidance.

items.label: Local government - principles governing conduct of members
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with principals governing the conduct of members.

items.label: Local government - procurement
items.description: Certain bodies may submit an expression of interest in providing services on behalf of specified authorities in the exercise of any of those relevant authorities’ functions under powers contained in Chapter 2 of Part 5 of the Localism Act 2011.  Fire authorities are added to the list of relevant authorities and may specify prescribed grounds on which an expression of interest may be rejected.

items.label: Local government - promotion of adequate use of records
items.description: A local authority may take steps to make adequate use of its records by promoting the same in various ways.

items.label: Local government - proposals for executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority in Wales must draw up and publicise its proposals for executive arrangements in the prescribed manner.

items.label: Local government - provision of information to another authority with executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority must provide certain information to another authority with executive arrangements in certain circumstances.

items.label: Local government - public contracts
items.description: Local authorities (as contracting authorities) must have regard to the regulations in relation to how they award public contracts for the execution of works, the supply of products or the provision of services.

items.label: Local government - public health functions
items.description: Local authorities must exercise prescribed public health functions in their area including arranging the weighing and measuring of certain children, health checks for eligible persons, access to sexual health services, a public health advice service to any clinical commissioning groups in their area, health protection arrangements against any threat to the health of the local population, including infectious disease, environmental hazards and extreme weather events.  A local authority may make and recover charges in respect of certain steps taken in the exercise of its duty as to health improvement, but not in respect of anything which the local authority is required to do in exercise of its prescribed public health functions.

items.label: Local government - records
items.description: A local authoriy decision-making officer must produce a written record of any category of prescribed decision as soon as reasonably practicable after the decision making officer has made the decision and must contain prescribed information.  The local authority must publicise the decision (unless it contains confidential or exempt information) as prescribed.

items.label: Local government - recoupment of education costs
items.description: A local authority must pay and claim recoupment of money as prescribed where a person belonging to the area of one authority (“the home authority”) in England is educated by another authority (“the providing authority”) in England or Wales.

items.label: Local government - referendum following petition, direction or order
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations requiring a referendum.

items.label: Local government - referendum on governance
items.description: An LA must hold a referendum on whether a local authority should change to a different form of governance if a valid petition is received with the support of at least 5% of the local government electors in the authority's area.The LA must follow the prescribed procedure including giving public notice of notices received and any referendum to be held.

items.label: Local government - referendum on proposals for executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority in Wales whose proposals include an elected mayor must hold a referendum and take other steps in accordance with section 27.

items.label: Local government - referendum regarding change of governance arrangements
items.description: A local authority wishing to change its governance arrangements must in certain circumstances hold a referendum.

items.label: Local government - referral arrangements for overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must adopt certain referral arrangements regarding its overview and scrutiny committee.

items.label: Local government - regard to guidance (Wales)
items.description: A local authority in Wales must have regard to guidance issued by the Welsh Ministers.

items.label: Local government - register of members interests
items.description: A local authority must maintain and disclose a register of members' interests.

items.label: Local government - reports and returns
items.description: A local authority must comply with requests from the Secretary of State for reports and returns.

items.label: Local government - requirements for companies/Trusts under control or subject to influence of local authorities
items.description: It shall be the duty of every local authority to ensure, so far as practicable, that any company/Trust under its control complies with any provisions made by the Secretary of State

items.label: Local government - resolution and publicity for executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority in Wales must pass an appropriate resolution and comply with publicity requirements before executive arrangements can operate.

items.label: Local government - resolution for change of governance arrangements
items.description: A local authority wishing to change its governance arrangements must comply with the prescribed procedure for passing resolution.

items.label: Local government - responding to overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority or its executive must respond to its overview and scrutiny committee in certain circumstances.

items.label: Local government - response by partner authority to overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority must respond to the overview and scrutiny committee of a partner authority in certain circumstances.

items.label: Local government - response to overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority in Wales or its executive must respond to certain matters reviewed by its overview and scrutiny committees.

items.label: Local government - review of flood risk function in committee system
items.description: A local authority with a committee system which is a lead local flood authority must review and scrutinise flood risk functions and may take certain steps.

items.label: Local Government - risk management directions
items.description: A local authority must comply with risk management directions given by the Secretary of State.The following are “risk-mitigation directions”—(a)a direction that sets limits in relation to the borrowing of money by the local authority;(b)a direction that requires the local authority to take action specified in the direction.

items.label: Local government - scrutiny officers
items.description: A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must designate an officer to promote, support and guide the overview and scrutiny committee and other members of the authority.

items.label: Local government - service of public notices
items.description: A local authority must serve public notices in the manner prescribed.

items.label: Local government - standards committee
items.description: A local authority must establish a standards committee.

items.label: Local government - supply of and use of goods and services
items.description: Subject to certain limitations a local authority may enter into an agreement for all or any of the following purposes  (a) the supply by the authority to the body of any goods or materials;  (b) the provision by the authority for the body of any administrative, professional or technical services;  (c) the use by the body of any vehicle, plant or apparatus belonging to the authority, the placing at the disposal of the body of the services of any person employed in connection with the vehicle or other property in question; and  (d) the carrying out by the authority of works of maintenance in connection with land or buildings for the maintenance of which the body is responsible.

items.label: Local government - terms of office and retirement of councillors in England
items.description: A local authority must comply with the requirements of section 6 and 7 of of the Local Government Act 1972 with regard to election of, terms of office and retirement of councillors.

items.label: Local government - terms of office and retirement of councillors in Wales
items.description: A local authority must comply with the requirements of section 25 of the Local Government Act 1972 with regard to election of, terms of office and retirement of councillors.

items.label: Local government - timing of elections
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations regarding the timing of elections.

items.label: Local government - transparency
items.description: Local authorities in England must comply with Part 2 of the Local Government Transparency Code 2015 .

items.label: Local Government associations - subscriptions
items.description: A local authority may pay reasonable subscriptions, whether annually or otherwise, to the funds of any association of local authorities formed (whether inside or outside the United Kingdom) for the purpose of consultation as to the common interests of those authorities and the discussion of matters relating to local government, or of any association of officers or members of local authorities which was so formed.

items.label: Local government England - permitted forms of government
items.description: A local authority must adopt one of the permitted forms of government.

items.label: Local government finance - accounts
items.description: Local authorities must follow detailed rules for the preparation, approval and publication of their statement of accounts.

items.label: Local government finance - revenue support grant England
items.description: Where the sum shown by the relevant calculation (in an amending report) as falling to be paid to a receiving authority for the financial year concerned is less than that shown as falling to be paid to it by the relevant previous calculation, a sum equal to the difference shall be paid by the authority to the Secretary of State.

items.label: Local government finance - revenue support grant Wales
items.description: The Welsh Ministers shall calculate what sum, if any, falls to be paid to each receiving authority by way of revenue support grant for the year in accordance with the basis of distribution agreed.  Where the Welsh Ministers make a calculation that shows a decrease in the sum that falls to be paid to a receiving authority, the authority shall pay to the Welsh Ministers a sum equal to the difference.

items.label: Local government in England - access to information and record keeping
items.description: A local authority must comply with certain steps regarding access to information and record keeping.

items.label: Local government in England - elected mayors
items.description: A local authority wishing to have an elected mayor must comply with regulations regarding elected mayors.

items.label: Local government in England - executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must ensure that they are as prescribed.

items.label: Local government in England - leader and cabinet executive
items.description: A local authority operating executive arrangements that provide for a leader and cabinet executive must include certain provisions regarding the executive leader and may include other provisions.

items.label: Local government in England - preparation and maintenance of constitution
items.description: A local authority must prepare and keep up to date a constitution.

items.label: Local government in Wales - access to information and record keeping
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with certain steps regarding access to information and record keeping.

items.label: Local government in Wales - elected mayors
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with certain prescribed steps with regard to elected mayors and comply with regulations if made.

items.label: Local government in Wales - executive arrangements
items.description: A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements must ensure that they are as prescribed.

items.label: Local government in Wales - leader and cabinet executive
items.description: A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements consisting of a leader and cabinet executive must accord with section 15.

items.label: Local government in Wales - preparation and maintenance of constitution
items.description: A local authority in Wales must prepare, keep up to date and make available a document regarding their constitution.

items.label: Local government re-organisation - Plans, reviews, schemes etc.
items.description: Each preparing council which is a county council and each shadow council shall prepare for the whole of its area, and if required by the enactment concerned publish plans, reviews, schemes, statements and strategies as detailed in Regulations.

items.label: Local government reference of matter to overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority in Wales must refer certain matters to its overview and scrutiny committees.

items.label: Local information - research and collection
items.description: A local authority may conduct, or assist in the conducting of, investigations into, and the collection of information relating to, any matters concerning the county or any part of the county.

items.label: Local information - submission to Minister on request
items.description: A local authority must comply with a request from the Secretary of State to provide him with any information collected.

items.label: Local land charges - compensation
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain cases of non-registration or defective official search

items.label: Local land charges - general charge
items.description: A local authority may register a general charge with the Chief Land Registrar against land in certain circumstances.

items.label: Local land charges - official search of register
items.description: A local authority must allow an official search of the register following payment of the prescribed fee.

items.label: Local land charges - personal search of register
items.description: A local authority must allow a personal search of the register following payment of the prescribed fee.

items.label: Local land charges - register and index
items.description: A local authority must keep a local land charges register and a local land charges register, which may be in electronic form.

items.label: Local land charges - registration
items.description: A local authority must as respects a local land charge apply to the Chief Land Registrar for its registration in the local land charges register.

items.label: Local land charges - rules
items.description: A local authority must comply with rules prescribed by the Lord Chancellor when carrying out its functions under the Local Land Charges Act 1975.

items.label: Local land charges - specification of fees
items.description: A local authority must specify and publish its fees relating to land charges and have regard to guidance when so doing.

items.label: Local transport plans
items.description: A local authority must develop and carry out policies for the promotion and encouragement of safe, integrated, efficient and economic transport to, from and within their area.

items.label: Local transport plans - approval of plans
items.description: A local authority in Wales must submit their transport plan to the National Assembly for approval and amend the same if required.

items.label: Local transport plans - modification order and directions
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with a modification order or Directions made by the National assembly with regard to its transport plans.

items.label: Local transport plans - review and alteration in England
items.description: A local authority must keep their transport plan under review and alter the same where required and consult where required.

items.label: Local transport plans - review and alteration in Wales
items.description: A local authority in Wales must keep its transport plan under review and alter the same as required. It must also take such other steps as are required.

items.label: London Mayor or Assembly member - disqualification due to sexual offences etc.
items.description: A person is disqualified from being elected or being the Mayor or an Assembly member in the Greater London Authority if the person is subject to:(a)  any relevant notification requirements, or(b)  a relevant order.Where that notification or order is in relation to sexual offences etc. and is given or made on or after 28 June 2022.The terms for disqualification are defined by section 21A.

items.label: Long distance routes - provision of facilities
items.description: A local authority whose area includes a long distance route may provide facilities for accommodation, meals and refreshments.

items.label: Long-distance routes - ferry services
items.description: A local authority may establish a ferry service to connect a long distance route where it crosses water.

items.label: Looked after children - additional functions of the responsible authority
items.description: It is the duty of each local authority to take reasonable steps to keep in touch with a relevant child for whom they are the responsible authority, whether he is within their area or not; to appoint a personal adviser for each relevant child; and to carry out an assessment of his needs (where there is not already a pathway plan) with a view to determining what advice, assistance and support it would be appropriate for them to provide

items.label: Looked after children - admission to school
items.description: A school governing body as admissions authority and a local authority where it is the admissions authority must comply with the Regulations with regard to the admissions of looked after children to school.

items.label: Looked after children - appointment of independent reviewing officer
items.description: If a local authority are looking after a child, they must appoint an individual as the independent reviewing officer for that child's case.

items.label: Looked after children - children's homes provided by appropriate national authority
items.description: Where a local authority place a child they are looking after in a children's home provided, equipped and maintained by an appropriate national authority, they must do so on such terms as that national authority may from time to time determine.

items.label: Looked after children - designated person for former looked after pupils (academy)
items.description: An academy must designate a member of the staff at the school (the “designated person”) as having responsibility for promoting the educational achievement of registered pupils formerly within state care and ensure that the designated person undertakes appropriate training and has regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Looked after children - designated person for former looked after pupils (maintained school)
items.description: A Governing Body of a maintained school must designate a member of the staff at the school (the “designated person”) as having responsibility for promoting the educational achievement of registered pupils formerly within state care and ensure that the designated person undertakes appropriate training and has regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Looked after children - designated teacher
items.description: A school governing body must ensure that the designated teacher for looked after pupils meets with the requirements of Regulation 3.

items.label: Looked after children - functions in respect of former relevant children
items.description: Each local authority shall have the duties towards a person who has been a relevant child and a person who was being looked after by them when he attained the age of eighteen, and a former relevant child. This includes children who have been detained or who are in hospital who were previously looked after.

items.label: Looked after children - general duty of local authority
items.description: It shall be the duty of a local authority looking after any child to safeguard and promote his welfare; and to make such use of services available for children cared for by their own parents as appears to the authority reasonable in his case.

items.label: Looked after children - independent visitors
items.description: A local authority looking after a child must appoint an independent person to be the child's visitor in prescribed circumstances

items.label: Looked after children - independent visitors (Wales)
items.description: In Wales where it appears to a local authority in relation to any child that they are looking after that communication between the child and a parent of his, or any person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him, has been infrequent; or he has not visited or been visited by (or lived with) any such person during the preceding twelve months,and that it would be in the child's best interests for an independent person to be appointed to be his visitor for the purposes of this paragraph, they shall appoint such a visitor.

items.label: Looked after children - information regarding child trust funds
items.description: When required to do so by regulations or by authorised officers of the Inland Revenue an authority must make documents available for inspection on behalf of the Inland Revenue or by a person appointed under regulations, ormust provide to the Inland Revenue or to such a person any information which the Inland Revenue or (as the case may be) the person may require for the discharge of any function relating to child trust funds.

items.label: Looked after children - living outside England and Wales
items.description: A local authority may, with the approval of every person who has parental responsibility for the child arrange for, or assist in arranging for, any other child looked after by them to live outside England and Wales.

items.label: Looked after children - maintenance
items.description: It is the duty of a local authority to maintain a child they are looking after in other respects apart from the provision of accommodation.

items.label: Looked after children - needs assessment and pathway plan
items.description: It is the duty of the responsible local authority to appoint a personal adviser for a former relevant child and to assess their needs and prepare a pathway plan.

items.label: Looked after children - notification of death
items.description: If a child who is being looked after by a local authority dies, the authority shall notify the appropriate national authority and shall, so far as is reasonably practicable, notify the child's parents and every person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him.

items.label: Looked after children - other children living outside England and Wales
items.description: A local authority may, with the approval of every person who has parental responsibility for the child arrange for, or assist in arranging for, any other child looked after by them to live outside England and Wales.

items.label: Looked after children - payments
items.description: Where a child is being looked after by a local authority the authority may make payments to a parent of the child; any person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him; or any relative, friend or other person connected with him, in respect of travelling, subsistence or other expenses incurred by that person in visiting the child.

items.label: Looked after children - personal adviser
items.description: A local authority shall arrange for each child whom they are looking after who is a eligible to have a personal adviser.

items.label: Looked after children - placement outside England and Wales
items.description: A local authority may only arrange for, or assist in arranging for, any child in their care to live outside England and Wales with the approval of the court.

items.label: Looked after children - promoting contact
items.description: Where a child is being looked after by a local authority Part 2 of Schedule 2 states: the authority shall, where appropriate, endeavour to promote contact between the child and his parents; any person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him; and any relative, friend or other person connected with him and keep them informed of where he is being accommodated.

items.label: Looked after children - prospective adopters
items.description: The local authority has a duty to consider fostering for adoption as part of the care planning process to achieve permanence for a looked after child

items.label: Looked after children - provision of accommodation
items.description: When a child is in the care of a local authority, it is their duty to provide the child with accommodation.

items.label: Looked after children - provision of accommodation and maintenance by local authority
items.description: It shall be the duty of any local authority looking after a child when he is in their care, to provide accommodation for him; and to maintain him in other respects apart from providing accommodation for him.

items.label: Looked after children - securing of sufficient accommodation
items.description: It is the general duty of a local authority to take steps that secure, so far as reasonably practicable, to provide the children with accommodation that is within the authority's area; and meets the needs of those children

items.label: Looked after children - visits
items.description: The LA’s representative must visit an unassessed accommodated child (in private) within 7 days of a notification under S.85(1) of the 1989 Act and at 6 monthly intervals (maximum) thereafter.  Where a child’s needs have been assessed within the 12 months up to the notification, the LA’s representative must visit the child within 3 months and at 6 monthly intervals (maximum) afterwards.  A LA’s representative must visit whenever reasonably requested by the child or if necessary to safeguard the child’ welfare and write a report of the visit containing prescribed information.

items.label: Looked after children - visits in detention
items.description: LAs must visit children who have ceased to be looked after by them as a result of prescribed circumstances (under section 23ZA of the 1989 Act) in the frequency and manner prescribed and provide a report on such visits.

items.label: Looked after children - visits in detention (Wales)
items.description: A LA must ensure that children who have ceased to be looked after by it and that are detained are visited by a representative of the LA in private within ten working days of the child first being detained and thereafter whenever reasonably requested to do so by specified persons, for example, the child and that they have access to advice, support and assistance. The representative must provide a report of each visit including prescribed details and provide a copy to the child

items.label: Looked after children - visits to, and contact with, looked after children and others
items.description: It is the duty of the local authority to ensure that a looked after child is visited by a representative of the authority; to arrange for appropriate advice, support and assistance to be available

items.label: Looked after children - ways to be accommodated and maintained
items.description: Where it is appropriate, the local authority must make arrangements for a looked after child to live with: a parent; a person with parental responsibility; or where a child is in the care of the local authority and there was a residence order in force immediately before the care order was made, a person in whose favour the residence order was made.

items.label: Looked after children - welfare after leaving care
items.description: It is the duty of the local authority looking after a child to advise, assist and befriend him with a view to promoting his welfare when they have ceased to look after him.

items.label: Looked after children and child welfare - provision of community homes
items.description: Every local authority shall make such arrangements as they consider appropriate for securing that community homes are available for the care and accommodation of children looked after by them; and for purposes connected with the welfare of children (whether or not looked after by them), and may do so jointly with one or more other local authorities.

items.label: Lord Lieutenant - appointment
items.description: Her majesty must appoint a Lord Lieutenant (or acting Lord Lieutenant) for every County in England and Wales.

items.label: Lord Lieutenant - appointment of clerk
items.description: A Lord Lieutenant shall appoint and may revoke the appointment of a clerk

items.label: Lord Lieutenant - appointment of deputy
items.description: A Lord Lieutenant must appoint one or more Deputy Lieutenants

items.label: Lord Lieutenant - appointment of Vice Lord Lieutenant
items.description: A Lord Lieutenant may with Her Majesty’s approval appoint a Vice Lord Lieutenant

items.label: Maintained school - intervention where school causing concern
items.description: The Governing Body of a maintained school must enter into arrangements if directed to do so by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Marine Conservation Zones - applications which may hinder MCZ objectives
items.description: Where the authority receives an application for authorisation of the doing of an act where there is or may be a significant risk of the act hindering the achievement of the conservation objectives stated for the MCZ, the authority must notify the appropriate statutory conservation body of that fact.

items.label: Marine Conservation Zones - failure to comply
items.description: A local authority must provide the appropriate statutory conservation body with an explanation for alleged failure to comply with duties.

items.label: Marine Conservation Zones - furthering conservation objectives
items.description: A local authority must exercise its functions in a way which the authority considers best furthers the conservation objectives stated for the Marine Conservation Zone or where it is not possible to exercise its functions in a manner which furthers those objectives, exercise them in the manner which the authority considers least hinders the achievement of those objectives.      If an authority considers that any of its functions is such that the exercise of the function would or might significantly hinder the achievement of the conservation objectives for an MCZ, it must inform the appropriate statutory conservation body of that fact.

items.label: Marine licensing - delegation of functions
items.description: A local authority must comply with any delegation of functions order in respect of marine licensing.

items.label: Marine planning - delegation of functions relating to marine plans
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from a Marine Planning Authority.

items.label: Marine policy - decisions in accordance with marine policy documents
items.description: A public authority must take any authorisation or enforcement decision in accordance with the appropriate marine policy documents, unless relevant considerations indicate otherwise.

items.label: Marine strategy
items.description: Each LA must, in exercising any functions so far as affecting the marine strategy area, have regard to any marine strategy developed under regulation 5.

items.label: Markets - appointment of times and charges
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances appoint times and charges for markets.

items.label: Markets - cold stores
items.description: A local authority may provide cold stores at markets

items.label: Markets - establishment or acquisition
items.description: A local authority may establish a market within [their area] or acquire by agreement (but not otherwise), either by purchase or on lease, the whole or any part of an existing market undertaking within [their area], and any rights enjoyed by any person within [their area] in respect of a market and of tolls, and, in either case, may provide a market place with convenient approaches to it; a market house and other buildings convenient for the holding of a market.

items.label: Markets - information from drivers of livestock vehicles
items.description: A local authority officer may obtain certain information from drivers of certain livestock vehicles.

items.label: Markets - market byelaws
items.description: A local authority who maintain a market, whether or not they are a market authority within the meaning of this Act, may make byelaws for regulating the use of the market place, and the buildings, stalls, pens and standings in that market place; for preventing nuisances or obstructions in the market place, or in the immediate approaches to it; for regulating porters and carriers resorting to the market, and fixing the charges to be made for carrying articles from the market within the district.

items.label: Markets - market days, hours and charging
items.description: A local authority may determine market days, hours; charge for certain items/services and recover unpaid charges.

items.label: Markets - weighing machines and scales
items.description: A local authority must provide weighing machines and scales in certain circumstances

items.label: Marriage - cancellation of registration of shared buildings
items.description: Local authorities (the Registrar General) must follow prescribed procedures for the cancellation of the registration of buildings which are shared by more than one religious organisation for the solemnization of marriages of same sex couples.

items.label: Marriage - conversion of civil partnership
items.description: Local authorities may provide secular services or ceremonies following conversions.

items.label: Marriage - registration and appointment for same sex marriage
items.description: Local authorities (the Registrar General and superintendent registrar) must follow the prescribed procedures on registration and cancellation of a building

items.label: Mayor of combined authority - disqualification due to sexual offences etc.
items.description: A person is disqualified from being elected or holding office as a Mayor in a combined authority in England if the person is subject to:(a)  any relevant notification requirements, or(b)  a relevant order.Where that notification or order is in relation to sexual offences etc. and is given or made on or after 28 June 2022.The terms applying to any disqualification are defined by Schedule 5B.

items.label: Meetings - providing live or later access to meetings
items.description: A local authority must comply with Regulations made by the Secretary of State in making provision for and in connection with allowing persons—(a) to film, photograph or make sound recordings of proceedings at a meeting of a body to which this section applies, or of a committee or sub-committee of such a body;(b) to use other means for enabling persons not present at such a meeting to see or hear proceedings at the meeting, as it takes place or later;(c) to report or provide commentary on the proceedings at such a meeting, orally or in writing, so that the report or commentary is available, as the meeting takes place or later, to persons not present at the meeting.

items.label: Meetings - religious observance
items.description: The business at a meeting of an English local authority or committee or subcommittee of that Authority may include time for—(a) prayers or other religious observance, or(b) observance connected with a religious or philosophical belief.

items.label: Members - allowances and expenses
items.description: A local authority may pay certain allowances and expenses to Members.

items.label: Members - declaration of office
items.description: Local authority members and elected mayors  must complete the prescribed declaration of office within two months of election for county, district and London borough.

items.label: Members - dispensation where pecuniary interest
items.description: An authority may in certain circumstances issue a dispensation allowing a member to take part in a debate or to vote where he or she has a pecuniary interest as per section 31(4) of the Localism Act 2011.

items.label: Members - disqualification due to sexual offences etc.
items.description: A person is disqualified for being elected or being a member of a local authority in England if the person is subject to:(a)  any relevant notification requirements, or(b)  a relevant order.Where that notification or order is given or made on or after 28 June 2022 in relation to sexual offences etc. as defined in section 81A.

items.label: Members - exercise of any function of a local authority
items.description: A local authority may authorise a councillor for a ward or division to discharge its functions (to the extent allowed) in respect of that ward or division.

items.label: Members - promote and maintain high standards of conduct
items.description: A relevant authority must promote and maintain high standards of conduct by members and co-opted members of the authority.    In discharging its duty as above a relevant authority must, in particular, adopt a code dealing with the conduct that is expected of members and co-opted members of the authority when they are acting in that capacity.

items.label: Members - provision about allowances
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding member's allowances.

items.label: Members - register of interests
items.description: The monitoring officer of a relevant authority must establish and maintain a register of interests of members and co-opted members of the authority.

items.label: Members - written record of decisions and actions
items.description: Where a member of a local authority discharges any function of the authority by virtue of arrangements made under section 236 of the Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007 (exercise of functions by local councillors in England), that member must—(a) ensure that a record is made in writing of any decision made or action taken in connection with the discharge of that function; and(b) within one month of the date on which the decision is made, or action taken, provide the record to the authority.The authority may also withdraw that exemption by notice.

items.label: Mental health - after-care services
items.description: It shall be the duty of the local social services authority to provide, in co-operation with relevant voluntary agencies, after-care services for any person to whom this section applies until such time as they are satisfied that the person concerned is no longer in need of such services

items.label: Mental health - application for guardianship
items.description: The person named as guardian in a guardianship application may be either a local social services authority or any other person but a guardianship application in which a person other than a local social services authority is named as guardian shall be of no effect unless it is accepted on behalf of that person by the local social services authority for the area in which he resides, and shall be accompanied by a statement in writing by that person that he is willing to act as guardian.

items.label: Mental health - applications for admission or guardianship by approved mental health professionals
items.description: If a local social services authority have reason to think that an application for admission to hospital or a guardianship application may need to be made in respect of a patient within their area, they shall make arrangements for an approved mental health professional to consider the patient's case on their behalf.

items.label: Mental health - approval by local social services authority
items.description: A local social services authority may approve a person to act as an approved mental health professional

items.label: Mental health - approved social workers
items.description: A local social services authority shall appoint a sufficient number of approved social workers for the purpose of discharging the functions referred to in the Act.

items.label: Mental health - arrangement of interview
items.description: A local social services authority must arrange for a person to be interviewed by a mental health professional in certain circumstances

items.label: Mental health - assessment of residency
items.description: A LA is responsible for determining within which local area an adult (who is a former user of secondary mental health services) resides, where there is a question about whether an adult's usual or most residence is situated within a particular LA area.However, where the local mental health partners for another LA area agree to act as the local mental health partners for an adult, then that adult is deemed to be usually resident within that other LA area

items.label: Mental health - availability of independent mental health advocates
items.description: A local social services authority shall make such arrangements as it considers reasonable to enable persons (independent mental health advocates) to be available to help qualifying patients.

items.label: Mental health - care co-ordination
items.description: Where a Local Health Board is responsible for providing a secondary mental health service to a relevant patient and a LA is also responsible for providing such a service, then the Local Health Board is the relevant mental health service provider for a relevant patient unless the patient is the subject of— a guardianship application or order, or, is under the age of eighteen years and—is looked after by a LA or is a relevant child or qualifies for advice and assistance or is admitted to a school in accordance with a statement of SEN that names the school in which case the LA is to act as the mental health service provider

items.label: Mental health - information about independent mental health advocates
items.description: The responsible person in relation to a qualifying patient shall take such steps as are practicable to ensure that the patient understands that help is available to him from an independent mental health advocate; and how he can obtain that help.

items.label: Mental health - prosecution by local authorities
items.description: A local social services authority may institute proceedings for any offence under this Part of this Act, but without prejudice to any provision of this Part of this Act requiring the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions for the institution of such proceedings.

items.label: Migrant children - compliance with transfer scheme
items.description: A local authority must, comply with a Scheme for the transfer of responsibility for relevant children prepared by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Migrant children - directed transfer of responsibility
items.description: A local authority must, when directed to do so by the Secretary of State, enter into arrangements under section 69 of the Act.

items.label: Migrant children - provision of information
items.description: A local authority must when directed to do so by the Secretary of State provide information to the Secretary of State relevant to the exercise of sections 69 or 72 of the Act.

items.label: Migrant children - transfer of responsibilities
items.description: A local authority may make arrangements with another authority for the transfer of certain responsibilities relating to migrant children.

items.label: Mineral workings - power to enter former mining land etc
items.description: Where a local authority have carried out, are carrying out or are considering whether to carry out works on any land under section 89(2) of the National Parks and Access to the Countryside Act 1949 (treatment of derelict land etc.) for the purpose of reclaiming or improving land under which relevant operations have been, but are no longer being, carried out an authorised person may at any reasonable time enter the land to carry out works; to survey the land for the purpose of ascertaining the effect on it of works carried out; or to survey the land for the purpose of ascertaining the location, extent and state of mine working produced by relevant operations, the state of the land, the risk of collapse of its surface, the likely extent of collapse, and the nature and extent of any works which may be necessary to prevent collapse or to deal with a collapse which has occurred.

items.label: Museums and galleries - admission charges
items.description: A local authority may charge for entry to museums and galleries in certain circumstances.

items.label: Museums and galleries - contribution towards expenses
items.description: A local authority may make contributions towards the expenses of running museums or galleries or provide advisory or other services there.

items.label: Museums and galleries - fund for purchase of exhibits
items.description: A local authority may establish a fund for the purchase of exhibits for its museums and galleries.

items.label: Museums and galleries - provision and maintenance
items.description: A local authority may provide and maintain museums and galleries in its area.

items.label: National Data Guardian - guidance
items.description: A local authority must have regard to guidance published by the National Data Guardian for Health and Social Care when processing health and adult social care data.

items.label: National Parks - improvements to waterways
items.description: A local authority whose area consists of or includes the whole or any part of a National Park may make improvements to waterways for the purposes of recreation.

items.label: National Parks - provision of facilities
items.description: A local authority whose area consists of or includes the whole or any part of a National Park may make arrangements for securing the provision of accommodation, meals and refreshments, camping sites and of parking places.

items.label: National Parks - regard to purposes when exercising functions
items.description: A local authority must In exercising or performing any functions in relation to land in a National Park, have regard to the purposes specified in subsection 5(1) the Act and, if it appears that there is a conflict between those purposes, shall attach greater weight to the purpose of conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the area comprised in the National Park

items.label: Natural environment - agreement to carry out a DEFRA function
items.description: A local authority may enter into an agreement with the Secretary of State to carry out a DEFRA function under the Act.

items.label: Natural environment - agreement with another body to carry out designated DEFRA function
items.description: A local authority may enter into an agreement with another designated body to carry out a function under the Act.

items.label: Nature reserves - establishment
items.description: A local authority may establish nature reserves and enter into certain agreements relating to the same.

items.label: New towns - overseeing development
items.description: Where the Secretary of State has by order appointed one or more local authorities to oversee the development of the area as a new town the local authority must exercise the functions of the Secretary of State in relation to the new town.

items.label: Noise - entry and seizure
items.description: Where a warning notice has been served and at any time in the period specified in the notice, noise emitted from the dwelling has exceeded the permitted level an officer of the local authority, or a person authorised by the authority for the purpose, may enter the dwelling from which the noise in question is being or has been emitted and may seize and remove any equipment which it appears to him is being or has been used in the emission of the noise.

items.label: Noise - evidence used in proceedings
items.description: Any evidence used in proceedings brought for an offence must comply with the requirements of section 7 of the Act.

items.label: Noise - fixed penalty notice
items.description: An officer authorised by a local authority may issue a fixed penalty notice in the prescribed form if he believes that an offence has been committed and has the power to request the offender to give his name and address.

items.label: Noise - investigation of complaints
items.description: An officer of a local authority may investigate certain complaints relating to noise at night emanating from private dwellings and certain other premises and may issue a warning notice.

items.label: Noise - loudspeakers in streets or roads
items.description: A local authority may resolve (which resolution must be published) that Schedule 2 (regulation the authorisation process for the operation of loud speakers in streets and roads) is to apply to its area and if it does so resolve, Schedule 2 shall come into force in its area on such date as may be specified for that purpose in the resolution.

items.label: Noise - warning notices
items.description: Any warning notice issued must comply with regulations.

items.label: Noise pollution - consent to excessive noise
items.description: A local authority may consent to noise being produced at a level above the permitted level in certain circumstances.

items.label: Noise pollution - construction sites
items.description: A local authority may, by notice or a consent, impose conditions upon the emanation of noise from a construction site.

items.label: Noise pollution - execution and costs of works
items.description: A local authority may recover costs for carrying out works required by a noise abatement order in certain circumstances.

items.label: Noise pollution - inspection for noise abatement areas
items.description: A local authority must cause its area to be inspected from time to time so it can decide how to use its noise abatement powers.

items.label: Noise pollution - measurement of noise levels
items.description: A local authority must in relation to an area which it has designated as a noise abatement zone, measure noise levels.

items.label: Noise pollution - noise abatement zones
items.description: A local authority may, by order, designate any part of its area a noise abatement zone.

items.label: Noise reduction - motor cycle silencer and exhaust systems
items.description: The local authority has the power to ensure compliance with schedule 3 and to enforce the act as necessary to prevent the supply of exhaust systems, silencers and components which are likely to result in motor cycles to which they are fitted emitting excessive noise.

items.label: Non domestic rating - levy payment
items.description: A local authority must make a levy payment to the Secretary of State in prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Non-domestic rates - chargeable amounts
items.description: A local authority must comply with the Regulations when making the calculations which fall within those Regulations

items.label: Non-domestic rates - exceptional billing calculations
items.description: Special provision for the relevant years beginning on 1st April 2021 and 1st April 2022.  This paragraph applies to a billing authority where, in the relevant year beginning on 1st April 2021, the exceptional balance the billing authority calculates in accordance with the schedule in Regulations is a negative amount.Where this paragraph applies for the relevant year beginning on 1st April 2021, a billing authority must: (a) include in the amount specified an amount equal to two thirds of the exceptional balance expressed as a positive amount;(b)for the relevant year beginning on 1st April 2022, a billing authority must include in the amount specified an amount equal to one third of the exceptional balance expressed as a positive amount.

items.label: Non-domestic rates - lists and appeals
items.description: A local authority must comply with the Regulations when making the calculations which fall within those Regulations

items.label: Non-domestic rates - relief for public lavatories
items.description: Where on the charging day for non-domestic rates a hereditament consists wholly or mainly of public lavatories the chargeable amount on the chargeable day is zero.  Liability to any business rate supplement is also zero.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - dates for submission of lists
items.description: The Local Government Finance Act 1988 is amended as follows.(2)  In section 41 (local non-domestic rating lists)—(a)  in subsection (2A) (date on which English local rating lists must be compiled), in paragraph (b), after "2017" insert ", on 1 April 2023";(b)  in subsection (5) (deadline for proposed list to be sent to billing authority), for "30 September" substitute "31 December".(3)  In section 52 (central non-domestic rating lists)—(a)  in subsection (2A) (date on which English central rating lists must be compiled), in paragraph (b), after "2017" insert ", on 1 April 2023";(b)  in subsection (5) (deadline for proposed list to be sent to Secretary of State or Welsh Ministers), for "30 September" substitute "31 December".(4)  In section 54A (postponement of compilation of Welsh lists for 2015 onwards)—(a)  in subsection (4)(b) (date on which Welsh local rating lists must be compiled), after "specified date" insert ", on 1 April 2023";(b)  in subsection (5)(b) (date on which Welsh central rating lists must be compiled), after "specified date" insert ", on 1 April 2023".

items.label: Non-domestic rating - determinations in respect of lists
items.description: Determinations made by a local authority in respect of certain non-domestic rating lists must take into account what is considered a relevant determination in this legislation when so doing.  The authority must take into account Coronavirus related matters when making their determination.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - disregarded income 2013
items.description: Local authorities (billing authorities) must disregard a prescribed proportion of the non-domestic rating income from certain prescribed calculations.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - disregarded income 2014
items.description: Local authorities (billing authorities) must disregard a prescribed proportion of the non-domestic rating income from certain prescribed calculations.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - levy and safety net payments assessment
items.description: A local authority may request that the Secretary of State calculate whether a safety net payment is likely to be required to be made to the authority in respect of the relevant year.  A local authority must make a levy payment to the Secretary of State in prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - local rating lists
items.description: The valuation officer for a billing authority shall compile, and then maintain, lists for the authority (to be called its local non-domestic rating lists).  As soon as is reasonably practicable after receiving the copy the authority shall deposit it at its principal office and take such steps as it thinks most suitable for giving notice of it.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - partly occupied hereditaments
items.description: Where a hereditament is shown in a billing authority's local non-domestic rating list and it appears to the authority that part of the hereditament is unoccupied but will remain so for a short time only the authority may require the valuation officer for the authority to apportion the rateable value of the hereditament between the occupied and unoccupied parts of the hereditament and to certify the apportionment to the authority.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - preparation and maintenance of lists
items.description: The billing authority shall, throughout the period of three months preceding the beginning of the first chargeable financial year for which a rural settlement list is to have effect, make available for inspection a draft of the list in the form in which the authority proposes that it should have effect for that year.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - rates retention
items.description: Local authorities (billing authorities) may deduct amounts as prescribed from the central share payable to the Secretary of State or to county councils, fire and rescue authorities in whose area the billing authority is and, for London authorities, the Greater London Authority as prescribed and as may be directed.  Provisions may be made in relation to costs, bad debts, reconciliation and for surplus or deficit calculations and according to prescribed time limits.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - reduction or remission of liability
items.description: A billing authority may reduce any amount a person is liable to pay for hereditaments or remit payment of the whole of any amount a person would otherwise be liable to pay if the ratepayer would sustain and it is reasonable for the authority to do so, having regard to the interests of persons liable to pay council tax set by it.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - renewable energy projects
items.description: A local authority (billing authority) may disregard an amount of non-domestic rating income in relation to designated classes of hereditaments for the purpose of certain calculations.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - rural settlement lists
items.description: Each billing authority shall compile and maintain, a list (to be called its rural settlement list).  It shall identify for each such year any settlements which are wholly or partly within the authority's area, appear to the authority to have had a population of not more than 3,000 on the last 31st December before the beginning of the chargeable financial year in question, and in that financial year are wholly or partly within an area designated by the Secretary of State by order as a rural area for the purposes of this section.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - small business relief
items.description: Billing authorities must have regard to the provisions relating to which hereditaments are excepted from the small business rate relief scheme including: a maximum rateable value of £12,000 for hereditaments which might be eligible for relief from non-domestic rates; prescribed conditions of eligibility for relief from non-domestic rates; a temporary rate relief scheme which commences on 1 April 2015 and ceases on 31 March 2016 and information to be included in the notice, the time within which such a notice is to be served and the method of service.

items.label: Non-domestic rating - transitional protection payments
items.description: Where a transitional relief scheme is in place a local authority (billing authority) must, on 31st January in the preceding year, estimate the amount of its deemed and actual ratings income for the relevant year (as prescribed) and notify the Secretary of State of the estimated amounts.  On or before 31st July in the year following a relevant year a billing authority must calculate the amount of its deemed and actual ratings income for the relevant year, arrange for the calculations and amounts to be certified and, if necessary, pay a reconciliation payment (calculated as prescribed).

items.label: Non-domestic rating Wales - local non-domestic rating lists for amalgamated authorities
items.description: A new billing authority receiving a copy of an amalgamated list (amalgamated list shall contain the information which was included in the local non-domestic rating lists complied on 1st April 1995 for the old billing authorities) shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable, deposit it at its principal office.

items.label: Norfolk and Suffolk Broads - general duty of public bodies
items.description: If undertaking work in the Broads, a relevant authority shall have regard to the purposes of conserving and enhancing the natural beauty, wildlife and cultural heritage of the Broads; promoting opportunities for the understanding and enjoyment of the special qualities of the Broads by the public; and protecting the interests of navigation.

items.label: Officers and members - indemnity from liability
items.description: A local authority must indemnify its officers and members from personal liability in certain circumstances.

items.label: Officers appointed as receivers or administrators - indemnities
items.description: A local authority may indemnify its officers in their role as receivers or administrators in certain circumstances.

items.label: Open data - re-use of public sector information
items.description: Local authorities (as public sector bodies) are under a general duty to permit re-use within prescribed timescales and if doing so, must act in accordance with regulations 11 to 16 and establish an internal complaints procedure to determine complaints arising under the Regulations. (Implementing Directive 2013/37/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 (O.J. No. L175/1, 27.6.2013), which amends Directive 2003/98/EC on the re-use of public sector information).

items.label: Open spaces - appropriation for enjoyment of the public
items.description: A local authority may use its land for the purposes of open spaces.

items.label: Open spaces - public walks and pleasure grounds
items.description: A local authority may acquire, lay out and maintain land to be used as public walks and pleasure grounds.

items.label: Open spaces - transfer to local authority
items.description: A local authority may accept that certain open spaces may be transferred into its possession.

items.label: Open spaces and burial grounds - acquisition of land
items.description: A local authority may acquire, manage and maintain land for the purposes of open spaces or burial grounds.

items.label: Open spaces and burial grounds - authorities acting jointly
items.description: Two or more local authorities may act jointly in exercising their powers under the Act and may defray each other expenses.

items.label: Open spaces and burial grounds - borrowing
items.description: A local authority may borrow for the purposes of the Act.

items.label: Open spaces and burial grounds - byelaws
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws to govern the use of the open spaces and burial grounds that it has acquired.

items.label: Open spaces and burial grounds - compensation
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances in relation to open spaces and burial grounds

items.label: Overseas assistance - advice and assistance
items.description: A local authority may provide non- financial advice and assistance as respects any matter in which they have skill and experience to a body engaged outside the United Kingdom in the carrying on of any of the activities of local government and must comply with any relevant Regulations and have regard to guidance when so doing.

items.label: Parish or community council - use of schoolroom etc.
items.description: A local authority must allow a parish or community council to use a room in a maintained school or other premises free of charge in certain circumstances.

items.label: Parks and gardens - additional facilities
items.description: A local authority may provide ice skating, infant play, sports, and recreational facilities and cafes in parks and gardens.

items.label: Parks and gardens - wardens
items.description: A local authority may appoint officers to serve as wardens for parks and gardens.

items.label: Parks and pleasure gardens - provision and byelaws
items.description: A local authority may purchase or take on lease lay out plant improve and maintain lands for the purpose of being used as public walks or pleasure grounds, and may support or contribute to the support of public walks or pleasure grounds provided by any person and make byelaws in respect of the same.

items.label: Parks and pleasure grounds - boating pools and lakes
items.description: A local authority may exercise certain powers relating to the provision and management of boating pools and lakes.

items.label: Parks and pleasure grounds - closing
items.description: A local authority may close parks and pleasure grounds at certain times.

items.label: Parks and pleasure grounds - hire of boats
items.description: An urban authority may either themselves provide and let for hire, or may license any person to let for hire, any pleasure boats on any lake or piece of water in any such park or pleasure ground, and may make byelaws for regulating the numbering and naming of such boats, the number of persons to be carried therein, the boathouses and mooring places for the same, and for fixing rates of hire and the qualifications of boatmen, and for securing their good and orderly conduct while in charge of any boat.

items.label: Parks and pleasure grounds - improvement of lands
items.description: A local authority may lay out plant and improve land forming part of a park or pleasure ground.

items.label: Parks and pleasure grounds - management
items.description: A local authority may, exercise certain powers regarding the management of parks and pleasure grounds.

items.label: Parks and pleasure grounds - temporary closure for shows
items.description: A local authority may temporarily close a park or pleasure ground, for payment or otherwise to any public charity or institution, or for any agricultural, horticultural, or other show, or any other public purpose.

items.label: Parks and recreation grounds - charges for sports
items.description: Where part of a park or recreation ground is set aside for sport a local authority may charge for use of the same.

items.label: Payments for restoration or continuation of supply of water, gas or electricity
items.description: A local authority may come to arrangements to enable the continuity or restoration of utility supplies to any premises in its area.

items.label: Performing animals - enforcement
items.description: A local authority may prosecute proceedings where any person commits an offence under the Act.

items.label: Performing animals - powers of entry
items.description: An officer duly authorised by a local authority may enter premises to inspect the animals kept there and to inspect the occupant's certificate

items.label: Performing animals - register
items.description: A local authority must keep a register (which must be available for inspection) for the purpose of this Act containing the details of any person who exhibits or trains animals who applies for registration in the prescribed form and on payment of such fee as appears to the local authority to be appropriate and give to the applicant a certificate of registration.

items.label: Personal property - Lost and uncollected property
items.description: A local Authority may take possession of lost and uncollected property in certain circumstances.

items.label: Persons in hospital - temporary protection of property
items.description: A local authority must provide for the temporary protection of property of certain persons admitted to hospital in certain circumstances.

items.label: Pest control - compliance with Ministerial order
items.description: A local authority must comply with an order made by the appropriate Minister utilising his default powers where he is satisfied that functions are not being satisfactorily performed by the authority.

items.label: Pest control - legal proceedings for offences regarding rats and mice
items.description: A local authority may institute legal proceedings or give consent for them being instituted.

items.label: Pest control - notice requiring destruction of rats and mice
items.description: A local authority may serve notice upon the occupier of land requiring the destruction of rats and mice on the land or otherwise for keeping the land free from rats and mice.

items.label: Pest control - power to carry out works to remove rats and mice
items.description: A local authority where a notice has been served under section 4 and not complied with, may carry out those works itself and recover certain expenses.

items.label: Pest control - powers of entry for inspection related to functions dealing with rats and mice
items.description: A person duly authorised by a local authority may enter land for the purpose of the authority's functions under the Act.

items.label: Pest control - rats and mice
items.description: A local authority must carry out inspections and take action to ensure that its area is kept free (as far as practicable) of rats and mice and to take action to ensure owners of other land comply with the Act.

items.label: Pest control - works on multiple premises to control rats and mice
items.description: A local authority may where there is an infestation of rats and mice in an area made up of several premises, enter land, carry out the work and recover certain expenses from the owners.

items.label: Pet shops - inspection
items.description: An officer or any veterinary surgeon or veterinary practitioner duly authorised by a local authority may enter a pet shop for the purposes of inspection.

items.label: Pet shops - licensing
items.description: A local authority may licence a pet shop, subject to conditions on payment of a fee.

items.label: Pet shops - prosecutions
items.description: A local authority may prosecute proceedings for any offence under the Act committed in the area of the authority.

items.label: Planning - acquisition of buildings of special interest by agreement
items.description: A local authority may acquire, by agreement, buildings of special architectural or historic interest and contiguous / adjacent land required for the preservation of, access to or management of the building.

items.label: Planning - acquisition of land by agreement
items.description: A local authority may acquire land by agreement in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - acquisition of land for exchange
items.description: A local authority may acquire land for exchange purposes in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - action notice for control of advertisements
items.description: A local authority may serve an action notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - advance of money in relation to blight notices
items.description: A local authority may advance money to any person in certain circumstances connected with blight notices.

items.label: Planning - alternative planning permission providers
items.description: A Local Authority must comply with regulations regarding the provision of information to alternate planning providers.

items.label: Planning - appeal against enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure for appeals with regard to enforcement notices.

items.label: Planning - appeals against listed buildings consent decision
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure regarding appeals on listed building consent decisions and the decision of the appeal.

items.label: Planning - appeals against listed buildings enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure regarding appeals relating to listed building enforcement notices and the outcome of that appeal.

items.label: Planning - appeals against planning decisions
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure for planning appeals.

items.label: Planning - appeals and hearings regarding hazardous substances consents
items.description: A local authority must comply with the appeals procedure and the determination of the Secretary of State.

items.label: Planning - appeals in Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSIs)
items.description: A local authority must, where acting as a planning authority utilise this Appeals procedure for SSIs as are laid down in these Regulations.

items.label: Planning - appeals regarding certificate of lawfulness for listed building
items.description: A local authority must comply with the appeals procedure with regard to certificates of lawfulness.

items.label: Planning - appeals to the Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority shall comply with procedures relating to appeals to the Secretary of State against refusal or failure to give decision on a planning application.

items.label: Planning - applications to Secretary of State where local authority is designated for not adequately performing function of determining applications
items.description: A designated local authority must comply with any requests made or directions given by the Secretary of State in relation to planning applications made to the Secretary of State in place of the local authority.

items.label: Planning - appropriation of common land
items.description: A local authority may with the consent of the Secretary of State appropriate part of the common land.

items.label: Planning - appropriation of land
items.description: A local authority may appropriate land in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - assessment of environmental effects in determination of applications
items.description: A local authority must have regard to prescribed environmental considerations when determining an application.

items.label: Planning - assurance regarding prosecution where enforcement notice served
