items.description: A local authority may issue and serve an assurance regarding prosecution in circumstances where it has served an enforcement notice.

items.label: Planning - availability of local documents
items.description: Where a planning authority is required to make documents available for inspection they must do so by either making the documents available at the offices of the local planning authority or placing the documents on the local planning authority web site for the period of time specified in regulations.

items.label: Planning - breach of conditions notice
items.description: A local authority may issue and serve a breach of conditions notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - brownfield land register
items.description: Each local planning authority must prepare, maintain and publish a register of previously developed land which is within their area and which meets the criteria defined in these regulations.The register is to be known as that local planning authority’s “Brownfield Land Register”The register must be published by 31st December 2017

items.label: Planning - buildings preservation notice
items.description: A local authority may serve in the prescribed form a building preservation notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - certificate of lawful use or development
items.description: A local authority shall provide a certificate of lawful use or development in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - certificate of lawfulness of proposed works to listed building
items.description: A local authority must issue a certificate of lawfulness of proposed works in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - certificates of lawfulness procedures
items.description: The local authority (planning authority) on receipt of an application for a certificate of lawfulness of proposed works must follow the prescribed procedure, including the period within which an application is to be determined; the procedures for appeals against refusal or failure to give a decision and for revoking a certificate.

items.label: Planning - CIL charging schedules
items.description: A local authority which proposes to charge the community infrastructure levy must issue a charging schedule that is subject to examination.

items.label: Planning - compensation for decisions on listed buildings
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - compensation for loss due to stop notice
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation where a stop notice has been served in certain circumstances

items.label: Planning - compensation for refusal or conditional grant of planning permission
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances relating to the refusal or conditional grant of planning permission and in certain circumstances recover those payments.

items.label: Planning - compensation for revocation or modification of hazardous substances consent
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances where an Order is made under section 14.

items.label: Planning - compensation for revocation or modification of planning permission
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances relating to the modification or revocation of planning permission and may in certain circumstances recover some or all of the compensation paid if development is subsequently carried out on the same land.

items.label: Planning - compensation for tree preservation orders
items.description: A local authority may, by regulations be placed under a duty to keep registers and pay compensation.

items.label: Planning - compensation on withdrawal of planning permission
items.description: When local authorities withdraw the development rights prescribed, compensation is only payable in respect of planning applications made within 12 months beginning on the date the directions took effect. They may use the mechanism prescribed for the permitted development rights to be withdrawn without compensation being payable, provided the prescribed procedures are followed as to the manner of withdrawal, the manner of publishing the withdrawal and the maximum period of notice that may be given in respect of withdrawal. Likewise regarding permitted development rights granted by a local development order, and in respect of neighbourhood development orders

items.label: Planning - completion notices for development
items.description: A local authority may serve a completion notice  stating that the planning permission will cease to have effect at the expiration of a further period specified in the notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - compulsory acquisition in connection with highways
items.description: A local authority may compulsory acquire land in connection with highway in certain circumstances and extinguish certain rights and rights of way.

items.label: Planning - compulsory acquisition of land
items.description: A local authority may acquire land for development and other planning purposes in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - compulsory acquisition of listed buildings
items.description: A local authority may acquire a listed building which is not being properly preserved where the Secretary of State authorises it do so.

items.label: Planning - compulsory purchase - damage compensation
items.description: Where a Local Authority entering and surveying land which it is acquiring by compulsory purchase causes damage it must pay compensation in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - compulsory purchase - entry of land
items.description: A Local Authority may enter and survey land which it is acquiring by compulsory purchase providing certain conditions are met.

items.label: Planning - conditional grant of planning permission
items.description: A local authority may attach conditions to a grant of planning permission.

items.label: Planning - conditions for hazardous substances consents
items.description: A local authority may impose conditions when granting a hazardous substance consent.

items.label: Planning - confirmation of tree preservation orders
items.description: A local authority may confirm a Tree Preservation Order in accordance with the prescribed provisions and must do so within 6 months and must adhere to the provisions regarding service, notice, publication and availability of copies, representations, variations, revocations and appeals of any Order and any compensation claims as prescribed.  Local authorities must keep a public register of applications, appeals and conditions.

items.label: Planning - conservation areas and listed buildings
items.description: A local authority must follow prescribed procedures for conservation area consent, for the variation or discharge of conditions attached to listed building or conservation area consents and for appeals in respect of these matters and other procedural matters relating to listed building and conservation area consents

items.label: Planning - consultation on development order
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the duty to consult in certain cases.

items.label: Planning - continuation of hazardous substances consents
items.description: A local authority must consider and determine application for the continuation of a hazardous substance consent and must pay compensation in certain circumstances..

items.label: Planning - contribution to preservation of listed buildings
items.description: A local authority may by grant or loan and subject to conditions, contribute towards the preservation of a listed building.

items.label: Planning - control of advertisements
items.description: A local authority must comply with and enforce regulations providing for the control of advertisements and pay compensation for their removal in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - control of demolition in conservation areas
items.description: A local authority may take certain actions in relation to dangerous structures in a conservation area.

items.label: Planning - Crown land
items.description: A local authority must comply with provisions relating to Crown land.

items.label: Planning - decision notices
items.description: A local authority must have regard to prescribed decision notices

items.label: Planning - defacement of premises
items.description: A local authority may serve notice and remedy the defacement or premises bus shelters or street furniture in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - designation of conservation areas
items.description: A local authority must determine which parts of their area are areas of special architectural or historic interest the character or appearance of which it is desirable to preserve or enhance, shall designate those areas as conservation areas, shall review that determination and shall comply with any directions from the Secretary of State.

items.label: Planning - determination by the Secretary of State to acquire land
items.description: A local authority must comply with a determination by the Secretary of State to require acquisition or development of land.

items.label: Planning - determination of an application to vary conditions
items.description: On an application for planning permission for development of land without complying with conditions subject to which a previous planning permission was granted, a local authority must determine an application for planning permission considering only the question of the conditions subject to which planning permission should be granted.

items.label: Planning - determination of procedure for listed buildings
items.description: A local authority must comply with procedures determined by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Planning - determination of relevant application
items.description: A local authority may decline to determine certain applications in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - development in enterprise zones
items.description: A local authority must comply with the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 in so far as it relates to enterprise zone schemes.

items.label: Planning - development management procedures
items.description: Local authorities (planning authorities) are required to follow procedures connected with planning applications, consultations in relation to planning applications, the determination of planning applications, appeals, local development orders, certificates of lawful use or development and the maintenance of registers of planning applications and related matters.

items.label: Planning - development of land
items.description: A local authority may develop land that has been acquired or appropriated by a local authority for planning purposes, and is for the time being held by the authority for the purposes for which it was so acquired or appropriated.

items.label: Planning - development orders for granting of planning permission
items.description: A local authority may grant planning permission pursuant to a development order, which may be subject to conditions or limitations.

items.label: Planning - development procedure
items.description: A local authority (planning authority) must follow prescribed procedures (including time limits) for planning applications (including planning permission), consultations in relation to planning applications, the determination of planning applications, appeals, local development orders, certificates of lawful use or development, the maintenance of registers of planning applications and other related matters.

items.label: Planning - directed stopping up or diversion of highway
items.description: A local authority must comply with an order made by the Secretary of State re the stopping up or diversion of highways

items.label: Planning - direction on local listed building consent orders
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions of the Secretary of State in relation to local listed building consent orders.

items.label: Planning - directions etc. as to method of dealing with applications
items.description: A local authority must comply with development orders and directions when dealing with planning applications including in relation to the discharge of planning conditions.

items.label: Planning - discretionary stopping up or diversion of highway
items.description: A local authority may authorise the stopping up or diversion of a highway for certain planning purposes.

items.label: Planning - disposal of appropriated or acquired land
items.description: A local authority may dispose of land appropriated or acquired for planning purposes by following certain procedures.

items.label: Planning - disposal of land
items.description: A local authority must take certain steps before disposing of certain types of land and must seek the best price when disposing of land.

items.label: Planning - duration of planning permission
items.description: A local authority must incorporate time limits for the commencement of authorised works or for approval of reserved matters into planning permissions and outline planning permissions.

items.label: Planning - emergency development
items.description: A local authority or a local health service body is permitted to develop on land owned, leased, occupied or maintained by it for the purposes of preventing an emergency, reducing, controlling or mitigating the effects of an emergency or taking other action in connection with an emergency.Any development undertaken must comply with the conditions of these regulations.

items.label: Planning - emergency works to preserve listed buildings
items.description: A local authority may carry out emergency works necessary for the preservation of a listed building and may recover the expenses involved in so doing.

items.label: Planning - enforcement of replacement of trees
items.description: A local authority may take action to enforce the replacement of trees in certain circumstances, including entering land, carrying out works and recovering expenses.

items.label: Planning - entry to land under warrant in relation to tree preservation orders
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority may enter land under a warrant issued by the magistrates' court for certain purposes.

items.label: Planning - entry to land without warrant in relation to tree preservation orders
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority may enter land without a warrant for certain purposes.

items.label: Planning - entry under warrant
items.description: A person duly authorised by a local authority may, at any reasonable hour, enter land with a warrant issued by magistrates for purposes connected to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

items.label: Planning - entry without warrant
items.description: A person duly authorised by a local authority may, at any reasonable hour, enter land without a warrant for purposes connected to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

items.label: Planning - environmental impact assessment
items.description: A planning authority shall not grant planning permission or subsequent consent unless they have first taken the environmental information into consideration and they shall state in their decision that they have done so.  A local authority must follow specified procedures concerning screening opinions, applications, environmental statements, notifications, unauthorised development and other miscellaneous developments.

items.label: Planning - Environmental Impact Assessment consideration
items.description: A local authority must not grant consent to an application made in pursuance of a requirement imposed by an order granted development consent for nationally significant infrastructure unless it has first taken the environmental information into consideration, and it must state in its decision that it has done so and in doing so must follow the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Planning - established use certificates
items.description: A local authority shall comply with procedures relating to established use certificates.

items.label: Planning - execution and cost of works for proper maintenance of land
items.description: A local authority may enter land, carry out works and recover expenses in respect of a notice requiring proper maintenance of land in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - execution and cost of works required by enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority may enter land and carry out works required by an enforcement notice in certain circumstances and recover reasonable expenses for doing so.

items.label: Planning - execution of works required by listed building enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority may in certain circumstances where an enforcement notice has not been complied with, enter premises, carry out works and recover the expenses involved in doing so.

items.label: Planning - exercise of planning functions in conservation areas
items.description: A local authority must pay special attention to the desirability of preserving or enhancing the character or appearance of a conservation area when exercising planning functions with respect to any buildings or other land in a conservation area.

items.label: Planning - expenses of county councils
items.description: The council of a county may direct that any expenses incurred by them under the provisions specified in Parts I and II of Schedule 16 shall be treated as special expenses of a county council chargeable upon such part of the county as may be specified in the directions.

items.label: Planning - extinguishment of rights of way over highway
items.description: A local authority may extinguish rights of way over a highway in certain circumstances having followed a particular procedure.

items.label: Planning - fees
items.description: A local authority must forward any fee received in respect of a planning application to the planning authority who are to determine the application and refund any fee where an application is rejected or an authority fails to determine relevant applications in time.  A LA may decide that a fee does not apply when it is satisfied that various prescribed reasons are established.

items.label: Planning - fees for planning applications etc.
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations made regarding the fees it should charge for exercising certain planning functions and other costs and contributions.

items.label: Planning - form of applications for planning permission
items.description: A local authority may require that a planning application must include such particulars and evidence as the authority thinks necessary.

items.label: Planning - general considerations for determination of applications
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the development plan and any other material considerations and consult when dealing with an application for planning permission.

items.label: Planning - general permitted development
items.description: Local authorities (Planning authorities) may grant planning permission for certain prescribed classes of development without the requirement for a planning application to be made under Part 3 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances consent application fees
items.description: A local authority must charge prescribed fees for certain applications.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances consents
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding hazardous substance applications and consents and their determination.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances contravention notice
items.description: A local authority may issue, serve, vary or withdraw (in the prescribed manner) a hazardous substances contravention notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances established presence
items.description: A local authority must take certain steps when established presence is claimed in relation to a hazardous substance consent.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances injunctions
items.description: A local authority may apply to the high court or the primary court for any actual or apprehended contravention of hazardous substances control to be restrained by injunction

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances new consent
items.description: A local authority must take certain steps with regard to a new request for consent without the conditions attached to a previous consent.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances on Crown land
items.description: A local authority must comply with provisions relating to hazardous substances on Crown Land.

items.label: Planning - hazardous substances temporary exemptions directions
items.description: A local authority must comply with a temporary exemption direction.

items.label: Planning - heritage partnership agreements
items.description: A local authority may enter into a heritage partnership agreement with prescribed legal individuals, which may contain prescribed conditions and/or measures.

items.label: Planning - heritage partnership agreements procedures
items.description: The local authority (local planning authority) must follow the prescribed procedures for heritage partnership agreements. In particular, the local authority must publicise its intention to make a heritage partnership agreement granting listed building consent and consult English Heritage in prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Planning - information as to interests in Crown land
items.description: A local authority must provide the Secretary of State with information regarding interests in Crown land for certain purposes connected with the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

items.label: Planning - information regarding interests in land
items.description: A local authority may by notice in writing require the occupier of any premises and any person who, either directly or indirectly, receives rent in respect of any premises to give in writing certain information.

items.label: Planning - injunctions for breach of tree preservation orders
items.description: A local authority may apply for an injunction to prevent a breach of this part of the Act.

items.label: Planning - injunctions for enforcement of listed buildings consent
items.description: A local authority may apply to the high or county courts for injunctive relief in certain circumstances connected to enforcement.

items.label: Planning - injunctions restraining breaches of planning control
items.description: A local authority may seek an injunction in the county or high courts to enforce planning control.

items.label: Planning - issue of certificate that building not intended to be listed
items.description: A local authority may not serve a building preservation notice for the period during which a certificate from the Secretary of State (or Welsh Ministers) that the building is not intended to be listed is in force.

items.label: Planning - issue of enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority may issue and serve an enforcement notice where it appears to them that there has been a breach of planning control and that it is expedient to issue the notice having regard to the development plan and any other material considerations.

items.label: Planning - land compensation (England)
items.description: A local authority must follow the prescribed procedure for issuing certificates under section 17 of the Land Compensation Act 1961 and send copies to other prescribed planning authorities.

items.label: Planning - land compensation (Wales)
items.description: A local authority must follow the prescribed procedure when issuing certificates under section 17 of the Land Compensation Act 1961.

items.label: Planning - list of buildings of special architectural or historical interest
items.description: A local authority must be guided by the list of buildings of special architectural or historical interest approved by the Secretary of State when carrying out its functions under the Act and must where applicable make a list of such buildings within its area available for inspection.

items.label: Planning - listed building consent orders
items.description: Local authorities must follow prescribed procedures for local listed building consent orders regarding their preparation and revocation and for notice, publicity, public inspection and consultation.  LAs must also have regard to prescribed matters in relation to compensation for withdrawal.

items.label: Planning - listed buildings consent
items.description: A local authority may award listed buildings consent for the alteration, extension or demolition of a listed building in the manner prescribed and subject to conditions.

items.label: Planning - listed buildings enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority may issue, serve, amend, vary or withdraw a listed building enforcement notice in the prescribed manner in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - listed buildings in Greater London
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding directions from the Historic Buildings and Monuments Commission for any application for planning permission for any development in Greater London which would, in the opinion of the local planning authority to which the application is made, involve the demolition, in whole or in part, or a material alteration, of a listed building.

items.label: Planning - listed buildings purchase notices
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure relating to listed building purchase notices.

items.label: Planning - local listed building consent orders
items.description: A local authority may grant listed building consent for works by means of a local listed building consent order.

items.label: Planning - local plans
items.description: Local authorities must comply with the prescribed procedures in relation to local plans and supplementary planning documents and procedures regarding publication of the local plan or supplementary planning document, consultation on those documents and consideration of representations made and their subsequent adoption or withdrawal.  Further with requirements and procedures regarding submission to or intervention by the Secretary of State, independent examination of the local plan and publication of the recommendations of the person appointed to examine the local plan.   An LA must also have regard to procedures relating to joint development documents, availability of documents and the monitoring reports which they must prepare.

items.label: Planning - London spatial development availability of documents
items.description: The Mayor of London must make copies of the London Spatial Development Strategy available for public inspection.

items.label: Planning - major infrastructure projects
items.description: A local authority must refer certain planning applications to the Secretary of State for determination if the Secretary of State thinks that the development to which the application relates is of national or regional importance and so directs.

items.label: Planning - management and disposal of acquired listed buildings
items.description: A local authority may manage and disposal of any buildings acquired under sections 47 or 52 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990.

items.label: Planning - neighbourhood area designation
items.description: A local authority must follow the procedure regarding applications for designation of a neighbourhood area or forum; for making neighbourhood development plans and in relation to neighbourhood development orders and the EIA Directive

items.label: Planning - neighbourhood area referendums
items.description: An LA must conduct a referendum in accordance with the Neighbourhood Planning Referendums Rules and other electoral legislation and these regulations including using the form of words prescribed, publish further information not fewer than 28 days before the date it is held and comply with the various specified restrictions.

items.label: Planning - neighbourhood development orders
items.description: A local authority must, in certain circumstances, make a Neighbourhood Development Order.

items.label: Planning - non-material changes to planning permission
items.description: A local authority may make non-material changes to planning permissions.

items.label: Planning - notice of applications for planning permission
items.description: A local authority must not entertain an application for planning permission unless notice requirements have been complied with.

items.label: Planning - notice requiring proper maintenance of land
items.description: A local authority may serve a notice requiring a person to properly maintain land and must comply with the appeals procedure.

items.label: Planning - orders for discontinuance, alterations or removals etc.
items.description: A local authority may (subject to confirmation by the Secretary of State) make orders, with regard to planning permissions, requiring continuance, discontinuance, alterations or removals etc. and recover expenses in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - override of easements
items.description: Local authorities may override easements and other rights which would otherwise restrict their use of land that has been acquired or appropriated for planning purposes. They can do this only if the use is in accordance with planning permission.

items.label: Planning - permission for development already carried out
items.description: A local authority may grant planning permission for development already carried out.

items.label: Planning - permitted development - use of land for market
items.description: The use of any land for the purposes of holding a market by or on behalf of a local authority and the provision on the land of any moveable structure for the permitted use at any time during the period when these regulations apply.Such development is not permitted if the land is, or is within, a site of special scientific interest.

items.label: Planning - planning contravention notice
items.description: A local authority may issue a planning contravention notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - planning enforcement order
items.description: A local authority may apply to the Magistrates' Court for a planning enforcement order in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - planning obligations
items.description: A local authority may enter into, modify or discharge planning obligations in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - planning permission for listed buildings
items.description: A local authority considering whether to grant planning permission for development which affects a listed building or its setting, shall have special regard to the desirability of preserving the building or its setting or any features of special architectural or historic interest which it possesses.

items.label: Planning - power to decline to determine applications
items.description: A local authority may decline to determine applications in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - powers of entry for listed buildings and conservation areas
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may for certain purposes under the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 enter land for those purposes.

items.label: Planning - procedure for certain proceedings and local inquiries
items.description: A local authority must comply with certain procedures and inquiries relating to the planning process.  A determination must provide for the proceedings to be considered in whichever of the following ways appears to the Secretary of State to be most appropriate at a local inquiry,  at a hearing or on the basis of representations in writing.

items.label: Planning - proposals for preservation and enhancement of conservation areas
items.description: A local authority must formulate and publicise proposals for the preservation and enhancement of conservation areas.

items.label: Planning - provision for preservation and planting of trees
items.description: A local authority shall ensure that in granting planning permission for any development, adequate provision is made, by the imposition of conditions, for the preservation or planting of trees

items.label: Planning - publication for development of nationally significant infrastructure
items.description: Where a developer has made an application for a development of nationally significant infrastructure publicity for the proposed application, notice of the accepted application (where this applies) and publicising of the acceptance notice must all be done in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Planning - publicity for applications affecting conservation areas
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State with regard to publicity to be given to planning applications affecting conservation areas.

items.label: Planning - publicity for applications affecting listed buildings
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding publicity for applications for planning permissions which may affect listed buildings.

items.label: Planning - purchase notices
items.description: A local authority must comply with a purchase notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - purchase of blighted land notice
items.description: A local authority must comply with a purchase of blighted land notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - recovery of compensation
items.description: A local authority must pay amounts equivalent to compensation paid to the Secretary of State in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - referral of applications for hazardous substances consents
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions requiring the referral of certain applications to the Secretary of State.

items.label: Planning - referral of applications to the Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the referral of planning applications to the Secretary of State.

items.label: Planning - register of applications etc.
items.description: A local authority must keep, maintain and make available a register of planning related matters.

items.label: Planning - register of enforcement and stop notices
items.description: A local authority shall, in the manner prescribed keep a register of enforcement and stop notices and other enforcement action.

items.label: Planning - register of hazardous substances applications and consents
items.description: A local authority must compile, maintain and make available a register with the prescribed content relating to hazardous substances.

items.label: Planning - register of land
items.description: A local authority must comply with Regulations requiring it to prepare and maintain a register of certain types of land.

items.label: Planning - register of notices of contraventions of tree preservation orders
items.description: It shall be the duty of a local planning authority to compile and keep available for public inspection free of charge at all reasonable hours and at a convenient place a register containing such particulars as the Secretary of State may determine of notices of intended acts affecting protected trees in their area.

items.label: Planning - removal of placards and posters
items.description: A local authority may remove or obliterate placards and posters and remove structures used for unauthorised display (England only) in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - review of simplified planning zone schemes
items.description: A local authority must keep the question of simplified planning zone schemes for their area under review.

items.label: Planning - reviews of old minerals permissions
items.description: A local authority must, where acting as planning authority, comply with the requirements therein.

items.label: Planning - revocation and modification of listed buildings consent
items.description: A local authority may revoke or modify listed buildings consent.

items.label: Planning - revocation or modification of hazardous substances consents
items.description: A local authority may by order (which must be confirmed) revoke or modify hazardous substance consents in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - revocation or modification of planning permission
items.description: A local authority may revoke or modify planning permissions.

items.label: Planning - right of entry on land with hazardous substances
items.description: A person authorised in writing by a local authority may with or without a warrant enter land in certain circumstances for the purpose of surveying in connection with any application for hazardous substances consent or any proposal to issue a hazardous substances contravention notice.

items.label: Planning - right of entry to Crown land for hazardous substances surveying
items.description: A person authorised in writing by a local authority may enter Crown land in certain circumstances for the purpose of surveying the same, but only after having first obtained the appropriate authority.

items.label: Planning - rights of entry to land
items.description: A person authorised in writing by a local authority may enter land for certain purposes connected with the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

items.label: Planning - simplified planning zones
items.description: A local authority may make or alter a simplified planning zone scheme.

items.label: Planning - spatial development availability of documents
items.description: The combined authority must make the spatial development strategy documents available for public inspection.

items.label: Planning - stop notice
items.description: A local authority may issue and serve a stop notice prohibiting the carrying out a relevant activity on the land to which the enforcement notice relates, or any part of that land specified in the stop notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - street vote development orders
items.description: A local authority must comply with the procedure and outcome relating to Street Vote Developments Orders and associated referenda.

items.label: Planning - temporary stop notice
items.description: A local authority may issue a temporary stop notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - temporary stopping up of highway for mineral workings
items.description: A local authority may temporarily stop up a highway for mineral working purposes.

items.label: Planning - time period for appeals
items.description: A local authority must, where acting as planning authority, comply with the time period set out in the Town and Country Planning (Determination of Appeal Procedure) (Prescribed Period) (England) Regulations 2009/454.

items.label: Planning - town scheme agreements
items.description: A local authority may enter into a town scheme agreement in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning - tree preservation orders
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances, make tree preservation orders and provisional orders in the case of Welsh authorities.

items.label: Planning - use of appropriated or acquired land
items.description: A local authority may use land appropriated or acquired for planning purposes for certain other purposes.

items.label: Planning - variation or discharge of conditions attached to listed buildings consent
items.description: A local authority may vary or discharge conditions attached to a listed Buildings Consent to the extent permitted.

items.label: Planning - variation or revocation of local listed building consent orders
items.description: A local authority may vary or revoke a local listed building consent order.

items.label: Planning - variation or withdrawal of enforcement notice
items.description: A local authority may vary or withdraw an enforcement notice.

items.label: Planning - written representations for appeals
items.description: A local authority must, where acting as planning authority, comply with the procedure for dealing with written representations.

items.label: Planning and development - adoption of local development documents
items.description: The local planning authority may adopt a local development document (other than a development plan document) either as originally prepared or as modified to take account of any representations made in relation to the document  or any other matter they think is relevant.

items.label: Planning and development - co-operation in relation to sustainable development
items.description: Local authorities must co-operate in relation to the planning of sustainable development.

items.label: Planning and development - discretionary joint committees
items.description: One or more local authorities may agree with one or more county councils in relation to any area of such a council for which there is also a district council to establish a joint committee to be the local planning authority

items.label: Planning and development - discretionary revision of local development documents
items.description: The local planning authority may at any time prepare a revision of a local development document.

items.label: Planning and development - expenditure of Assembly
items.description: A local authority must pay the expenditure of the Assembly if the Assembly prepares, revises or approves a local development plan in circumstances where the Assembly does so because it thinks the local authority is failing to do anything necessary in connection with the preparation, revision or adoption of the plan.

items.label: Planning and development - joint local development documents
items.description: Two or more local authorities may agree to prepare joint local development documents and may request the Secretary of State's involvement to enable continued examination of a document if a local authority withdraws from such an agreement.

items.label: Planning and development - local development monitoring reports
items.description: Local authorities must prepare and make available monitoring reports on local development as directed.

items.label: Planning and development - local development schemes
items.description: A local authority must prepare, maintain and revise a scheme to be known as their local development scheme, and revise it if directed by the Secretary of State or the Mayor of London (if the authority is a London Borough), and must make the up-to-date text of the scheme available to the public (together with a copy of amendments).

items.label: Planning and development - mandatory joint committees
items.description: Local authorities must comply with the Secretary of State's direction to establish or to revoke a joint committee.

items.label: Planning and development - mandatory revision of local development documents
items.description: The authority must prepare a revision of a local development document if the Secretary of State directs them to do so, and in accordance with such timetable as he directs.

items.label: Planning and development - minerals and waste development scheme
items.description: A county council in respect of so much of their area for which there is a district council must prepare and maintain a scheme to be known as their minerals and waste development scheme

items.label: Planning and development - neighbourhood development plans
items.description: Local authorities must prepare a neighbourhood development plan in certain circumstances

items.label: Planning and development - preparation of local development documents
items.description: A local authority must prepare and submit development plan documents in accordance with the local development scheme.

items.label: Planning and development - regard to Secretary of State's guidance
items.description: Local authorities must have regard to the Secretary of State's guidance when exercising their functions with relation to local development.

items.label: Planning and development - reimbursement of costs to Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must pay the costs of the Secretary of State where he utilises his default power  if he thinks that a local planning authority are failing or omitting to do anything it is necessary for them to do in connection with the preparation, revision or adoption of a development plan document.

items.label: Planning and development - statement of community involvement
items.description: A local authority must prepare a statement of community involvement.

items.label: Planning and development - survey of area in England
items.description: A local authority must keep under review the matters which may be expected to affect the development of their area or the planning of its development.

items.label: Planning and development - survey of area related to county matters
items.description: A county council in respect of so much of their area for which there is a district council must keep under review the matters which may be expected to affect development of that area or the planning of its development in so far as the development relates to a county matter.

items.label: Planning and development - sustainable development
items.description: A local authority must exercise various functions under the Act with a view to achieving sustainable development.

items.label: Planning and development - withdrawal of local development documents
items.description: A local authority may withdraw local development documents at any time before adoption.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - adoption of local development plan
items.description: A local authority may adopt a local development plan in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - annual monitoring report
items.description: A local authority must prepare an annual monitoring report to the Assembly in the manner directed.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - direction from Assembly
items.description: Two or more bodies must prepare a joint development plan when directed to do so by the Assembly

items.label: Planning and development Wales - intervention by Assembly
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the Assembly.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - local development plan
items.description: A local authority must prepare and appraise a local development plan as directed.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - regard to guidance from Assembly
items.description: A local authority must in exercising any function under Part 6 of the Act have regard to Guidance from the Assembly.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - review of local development plan
items.description: A local authority must review a local development plan if they think the plan should be reviewed and at such others times as prescribed by Welsh Ministers, and must report to the Assembly on the findings of their review.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - revision of local development plan
items.description: A local authority must revise a local development plan in certain circumstances.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - revocation of local development plan
items.description: A local authority may request the Assembly to revoke a local development plan.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - survey of area in Wales
items.description: A local authority must keep under review the matters which may be expected to affect the development of their area or the planning of its development.

items.label: Planning and development Wales - withdrawal of local development plan
items.description: A local authority may withdraw a local development plan at any time before it is adopted.

items.label: Planning and land - assessment of development land
items.description: If the Secretary of State directs an authority to do so, it shall make an assessment of land which is in its area and which is in its opinion available and suitable for development for residential purposes.

items.label: Planning and land - public access to register of land held by public bodies
items.description: Registers sent to the local authority by the Secretary of State shall be available at the council's principal office for inspection by any member of the public at all reasonable hours.

items.label: Planning and land - publication of information
items.description: A local authority must as prescribed publish information about the discharge of its functions and other related matters in accordance with a code of practice that may be issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Planning Data – Compliance with Regulations
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the management of its planning data and approved data standards where applicable.

items.label: Planning Data – Duty to make certain planning data publicly available
items.description: A local authority must make planning data publicly available where required to do so by Regulations.

items.label: Planning Data – Provision of Planning Data from third parties
items.description: A local authority may by publishing a notice require a person, or persons of a particular description, to provide to the authority such planning data as is specified or described in planning data regulations.

items.label: Planning Data – Use of planning data software
items.description: A local authority must use planning data software where required to do so by Regulations.

items.label: Plant health - publication of orders
items.description: A local authority must publish certain orders when required to do so.

items.label: Plant health - removal or destruction of crop, seed or plant
items.description: A local authority must comply with certain directions and pay compensation in certain circumstances in respect of any crop, or any seed, plant or part thereof, which is removed or destroyed in pursuance of any order.

items.label: Platforms - safety for use on public occasions
items.description: A local authority must check the safety of every roof of a building, and every platform, balcony, or other structure or part thereof let or used or intended to be let or used for the purpose of affording sitting or standing accommodation for a number of persons used on the occasion of any show, entertainment, public procession, open-air meeting, or other like occasion.

items.label: Pleasure boats - licensing
items.description: A local authority may grant, amend or revoke licences for pleasure boats.

items.label: Policy - charging for discretionary services
items.description: A local authority may charge the service recipient for certain discretionary services.

items.label: Policy - Chief Officer remuneration
items.description: The authority must comply with its pay policy statement for the financial year in making the determination of  the remuneration of or other terms and conditions applying to a chief officer of the authority

items.label: Policy - direction to prepare and submit draft multi-area agreement
items.description: Local Authorities must prepare a multi-area agreement when directed to do so by the Secretary of State and must consult before so doing.

items.label: Policy - housing finance strategies and statements Wales
items.description: A local authority must prepare such housing strategies and statements as may be required.

items.label: Policy - local area agreement
items.description: A local authority when directed to do so by the Secretary of State must prepare a draft local area agreement and should consult with partner authorities and such other persons as appear to it to be appropriate in so doing.

items.label: Policy - pay policy statement
items.description: Local authority must prepare a pay policy statement, annually and have regard to Guidance when doing so.

items.label: Policy - power of general competence
items.description: A local authority may do anything that an individual can do providing it is not otherwise prevented from doing so by statute.

items.label: Policy - proposal for multi-area agreement
items.description: The local authorities for an area proposed to be covered by a multi-area agreement (the proposed area) may request the Secretary of State to give a direction under section 125 for the preparation and submission of a draft multi-area agreement for the proposed area.

items.label: Policy - proposals for single tier of local government
items.description: A local authority may respond to an invitation from the Secretary of State to bring forward a proposal regarding the establishment of a single tier of local government for the area

items.label: Policy - provision of information to Boundary Committee
items.description: A local authority must if requested by the Boundary Committee to do so provide the Boundary Committee, by such date as the Boundary Committee may specify, with any information that the Boundary Committee may reasonably require in connection with any of their functions.

items.label: Policy - publication of information about multi-area agreement
items.description: A Local Authority must publish information about multi-area agreements or revised multi-area agreements.

items.label: Policy - regard to guidance by Secretary of State for combined authority
items.description: A local authority must have regard to guidance prepared by the Secretary of State with regard to anything done under Part VI of the Act.

items.label: Policy - regard to local improvement targets in local area agreement
items.description: A local authority must have regard to local improvement targets in its local area agreement when exercising its functions.

items.label: Policy - review by Boundary Committee of local government areas
items.description: A local authority may request the Boundary Committee to conduct a review of local government areas.

items.label: Policy - revision and amendment of targets in local area agreement
items.description: Any local improvement target other than a designated target for the time being specified in a local area agreement may be amended, or  removed from the local area agreement,by the responsible local authority with the agreement of any partner authority to which the target relates and after consulting each other person to whom it relates.    The responsible local authority may, with the consent of each person to whom the target in question is to relate, specify a new local improvement target in a local area agreement.  Designated targets may only be amended following consultation with the Secretary of State.

items.label: Policy - revision proposals for multi-area agreement
items.description: A Local Authority may or must if directed to do so by the Secretary of State prepare a proposal for a revised multi-area agreement and consult as required.

items.label: Policy - structural and boundary changes
items.description: A local authority may make agreements about incidental matters regarding the subject matter of orders issued under sections 7 and 10 of the Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007.

items.label: Policy - submission of existing multi-area agreement
items.description: Local Authorities must when preparing a multi-area agreement other than in accordance with section 125 comply with the requirements of section 128 and consult when so doing.

items.label: Policy - trading in function-related activities through a company
items.description: A local authority may as authorised by regulations trade in function related activities through a company.

items.label: Policy - transfer of responsibility in multi-area agreement
items.description: The local authorities to which the targets specified in a multi-area agreement relate may request the Secretary of State to agree to another one of those authorities becoming the responsible authority in relation to the agreement.

items.label: Pollution control - default powers where authority failed to perform functions
items.description: A local authority must comply with the directions of the Secretary of State when utilising his default powers under the Act.

items.label: Pollution control - detergents in water
items.description: LAs in England and Wales are enforcement authorities with powers to appoint authorised officers who must enforce contraventions of the Regulations in their area by serving notices, imposing requirements, using powers of entry and seizure and disposing of controlled product

items.label: Pollution control - emissions register
items.description: Each local authority must maintain a register containing information concerning emissions from premises which has been obtained by the authority under section 35 of the Clean Air Act and information concerning certain appeals against section 36 notices.

items.label: Pollution control - environment permits
items.description: Where a specified regulated facility is or will be operated in a LA’s area, a LA may carry out various functions in relation to that facility including granting, varying, transferring and requiring surrender of permits and take actions relating to the enforcement and prevention of pollution

items.label: Pollution control - power to obtain information
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances, serve a notice requiring the provision of information.

items.label: Pollution control - powers of entry
items.description: An officer duly authorised by a local authority may enter any land or vessel for the purposes of inspections, measurements or tests required by the Act.

items.label: Pollution control - volatile organic compounds
items.description: A LA must enforce the regulations which implement Directive 2004/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on the limitation of emissions of volatile organic compounds due to the use of organic solvents in certain paints, varnishes and vehicle refinishing products (the VOCs in Paints Directive).

items.label: Pollution control - water quality
items.description: LAs must make such arrangements with the specified relevant supplier as will secure that the authority is notified as required by the regulations and may take and analyse, by a person designated by them in writing, such samples of the water supplied to premises in their area as they may reasonably require

items.label: Postponed elections - duties of registration officer
items.description: Where notice of an election or referendum was required to be published before 6th April 2020 and the poll was not held on the date specified the relevant registration officer must:(a)retain the documents forwarded to the officer in accordance with regulation 4(4) for the period of one year, and(b)after that period, cause those documents to be destroyed, unless otherwise directed by an order of a county court, a Crown Court or a magistrates’ court.A person must not be allowed to inspect any of the documents in the possession of the relevant registration officer, except in accordance with an order made by a court for the inspection or production of any document for the purpose of instituting or maintaining a prosecution for an offence in relation to ballot papers.

items.label: Postponed elections - London Mayor or assembly and councillor by-elections
items.description: The authority must comply with these regulations in relation to any candidates for the postponed election for the Mayor of London and London Assembly due to be held on 7th May 2020 and any postponed by-election to fill a vacancy in the office of councillor for any principal area in England.

items.label: Postponed elections - parish council by-elections
items.description: A local authority must observe the following. A person (“P”) who became a candidate at a relevant by-election to fill a casual vacancy in the office of parish councillor on or before 6th April 2020 is no longer a candidate, and is treated as not having been a candidate before the coming into force of this regulation. Nothing in paragraph 1 above affects whether or not P is a candidate at the postponed poll for such an election.

items.label: Postponed elections - police and crime commissioner elections
items.description: A returning officer for a relevant PCC election may recover charges in respect of expenses incurred for or in connection with that election, notwithstanding that the election was not held, if the expenses were necessarily incurred for the efficient and effective conduct of the election. The amount of any charges recoverable is to be paid by the Minister on an account being submitted to the Minister.

items.label: Postponed elections and referendums - postal ballots
items.description: Where a local authority makes arrangements for the election of a councillor for any local government area in England to fill a casual vacancy; or a referendum, the poll for which is conducted in accordance with Schedule 3 or 5 to the 2012 Regulations (neighbourhood planning referendums).In circumstances where notice of election or (as the case may be) notice of the referendum was required to be published on or before 6th April 2020, and the poll for that election or referendum was not held on the date required to be stated in that notice as a result of the Local Government and Police and Crime Commissioner (Coronavirus) (Postponement of Elections and Referendums) (England and Wales) Regulations 2020(1).A postal ballot paper which was returned by a postal voter has no effect for the purpose of the postponed poll.

items.label: Postponed elections and referendums - treatment of postal ballot documents
items.description: Where notice of an election or referendum was required to be published on or before 6th April 2020 and the poll for that election or referendum was not held on the date required the returning officer must comply with regulations concerning the opening of and disposal of postal ballots.

items.label: Powers of entry for surveying, measuring etc.
items.description: A local authority may enter land for certain purposes connected with the Act.

items.label: Premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance - closure notice
items.description: A local authority may apply for a closure notice with regard to premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance and enforce that notice or apply for its extension or discharge (with rights to appeal).

items.label: Premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance - reimbursement of costs
items.description: A local authority may apply to have the cost of cleaning, securing or maintaining premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance.

items.label: Premises closure notice - closure order
items.description: A local authority may apply to a magistrate’s court for a closure order or an extension of a closure order where a closure notice has been made and served.

items.label: Premises closure notice - closure order appeal
items.description: A local authority may appeal to the Crown Court against various types of decision by the magistrate’s court relating to a closure order.

items.label: Premises closure notice - closure order enforcement
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority person may enter premises in respect of which a closure order is in force, do anything necessary to secure the premises against entry.A person acting under subsection (1) may use reasonable force. A person seeking to enter premises under subsection (1) must, if required to do so by or on behalf of the owner, occupier or other person in charge of the premises, produce evidence of his or her identity and authority before entering the premises.An authorised person may also enter premises in respect of which a closure order is in force to carry out essential maintenance or repairs to the premises.

items.label: Premises closure notice - closure order guidance
items.description: A local authority must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State when considering taking action in relation to a closure notice or closure order.

items.label: Premises closure notice - closure order reimbursement of costs
items.description: A local authority that incurs expenditure for the purpose of clearing, securing or maintaining premises in respect of which a closure order is in force may apply to the court that made the order for an order for those costs.

items.label: Premises closure notice - discharge of closure order
items.description: A local authority may apply to a magistrate’s court for the discharge of a closure order.

items.label: Premises closure notice - issue and duration
items.description: A local authority may issue a closure notice if satisfied on reasonable grounds—that the use of particular premises has resulted, or (if the notice is not issued) is likely soon to result, in nuisance to members of the public, orthat there has been, or (if the notice is not issued) is likely soon to be, disorder near those premises associated with the use of those premises,and that the notice is necessary to prevent the nuisance or disorder from continuing, recurring or occurring.

items.label: Premises closure notice - variation and discharge
items.description: A local authority may vary and cancel a premises closure notice

items.label: Private fostering - actions on notification of child privately fostered
items.description: Where a local authority have received a notification about a child being fostered privately they must arrange for an officer of the authority within seven working days or as soon as is reasonably practicable visit the premises where the child is being cared for, visit and speak to the private foster carer and family, visit and speak to the child and ensure that all matters relating to the welfare of the child have been considered.Having made the visits the officer should make a written report to the authority.

items.label: Private fostering - actions on notification of proposal to foster
items.description: Where a local authority have received notification of a proposal to foster a child privately they must arrange for an officer of the authority within seven working days or as soon as is reasonably practicable, to visit the proposed foster home, proposed foster carer and family, the child and every parent or person with parental responsibility for the child.Having completed the visits the officer should prepare a written report to the authority.

items.label: Private fostering - monitoring the discharge of functions
items.description: Each local authority must monitor the way in which they discharge their functions under Part 9 of the Act and must appoint an officer of the authority for that purpose.

items.label: Private fostering - subsequent visits to children
items.description: Each local authority must arrange for an officer of the authority to visit every child who is being fostered privately in their area:(a)in the first year of the private fostering arrangement, where reasonably practicable, at intervals of not more than six weeks(b)in any second or subsequent year, where reasonably practicable, at intervals of not more than 12 weeks.The authority must also arrange for every child who is fostered privately in their area to be visited by an officer when reasonably requested to do so by the child, the private foster carer, a parent of the child or any other person with parental responsibility for the child.Visits and matters considered during visits must be in accordance with regulations and the officer should make a written report of the visit.

items.label: Private hire vehicles - licensing
items.description: Subject to the provisions of this legislation, a council may on the receipt of an application from the proprietor of any vehicle for the grant in respect of such vehicle of a licence to use the vehicle as a private hire vehicle, grant in respect thereof a vehicle licence and may attach conditions to the grant of any such licence.

items.label: Procurement - exclusion of non-commercial considerations from contracts
items.description: It is the duty of every public authority in relation to its public supply or works contracts, to exclude non-commercial considerations.

items.label: Procurement - explanation of procurement decisions
items.description: Public authorities have a duty to give reasons for certain contract decisions to the person concerned.  This includes decisions regarding approved suppliers, contract awards and existing contracts.

items.label: Procurement - implied power to enter into contracts
items.description: Any statutory provision imposing a function upon a local authority confers a power for that authority to enter into a contract for the purpose of carrying out that function.

items.label: Procurement - review of approved supplier list
items.description: It is the duty of a public authority which maintains an approved list to consider whether persons have been included in or excluded from the list by reference to non-commercial matters, and if it appears to the authority that that is the case to compile the list afresh.

items.label: Procurement - valuation of contracts
items.description: The "estimated value" of a contract is its value for the time being estimated by a contracting authority.A contracting authority that estimates the value of a contract must do so in accordance with Schedule 3 of the Procurement Act 2023.A contracting authority must not exercise a discretion in connection with estimating the value of a contract with a view to securing that any requirement of this Act does not apply in relation to the contract.

items.label: Procurement investigations
items.description: A contracting authority must comply with an investigation by an appropriate authority relating to the relevant contracting authority's compliance with requirements of this Act.The relevant contracting authority must comply with a notice from the appropriate authority before the end of—(a)  the period specified in the notice (which must be at least 30 days beginning with the day on which the notice is given), or(b)  such longer period as the appropriate authority may agree to.In this section—"procurement investigation"  means an investigation under section 108(1);"relevant contracting authority"  means a contracting authority other than—(a)  a Minister of the Crown or a government department;(b)  the Welsh Ministers;(c)  a Northern Ireland department;(d)  the Corporate Officer of the House of Commons;(e)  the Corporate Officer of the House of Lords;(f)  the Senedd Commission;(g)  the Northern Ireland Assembly Commission;(h)  a private utility;"relevant documents"  means documents or other information that—(a)  are specified or described in a notice, and(b)  are in the possession or control of the relevant contracting authority to which the notice is given.

items.label: Procurement investigations recommendations
items.description: In considering how to comply with the requirements of this Act, a relevant contracting authority must have regard to a section 109 recommendation issued to it.A relevant contracting authority to which a section 109 recommendation has been issued must, where the recommendation so specifies, submit a progress report to the appropriate authority at such intervals as may be specified.A "progress report"  is a report setting out—(a)  what action (if any) the relevant contracting authority has taken as a result of the recommendation, or(b)  if the authority has taken no such action, a statement to that effect.Where the relevant contracting authority has taken no action as a result of the section 109 recommendation, or has taken different action to that recommended, the progress report must also include the authority's reasons for doing so.The contracting authority must also have regard to Guidance published under section 110.

items.label: Procurement termination notices
items.description: This section applies if, after publishing a tender or transparency notice in respect of a public contract, a contracting authority decides not to award the contract.As soon as reasonably practicable after making the decision, the contracting authority must give notice to that effect.This section does not apply to private utilities.

items.label: Procurement –  technical specifications
items.description: This section applies in relation to—(a)  a competitive tendering procedure;(b)  an award of a public contract in accordance with a framework;(c)  a process to become a member of a dynamic market.The procurement documents may not refer to design, a particular licensing model or a description of characteristics in circumstances where they could appropriately refer to performance or functional requirements.he procurement documents may not refer to a United Kingdom standard unless—(a)  the standard adopts an internationally-recognised equivalent, or(b)  there is no internationally-recognised equivalent.If the procurement documents refer to a United Kingdom standard, they must provide that tenders, proposals or applications that the contracting authority considers satisfy an equivalent standard from another state, territory or organisation of states or territories will be treated as having satisfied the United Kingdom standard.In considering whether a standard is equivalent to a United Kingdom standard for the purposes of the above, a contracting authority may have regard to the authority's purpose in referring to the standard.A contracting authority may require certification, or other evidence, for the purpose of satisfying itself that a standard is satisfied or equivalent.Unless the contracting authority considers it necessary in order to make its requirements understood, the procurement documents may not refer to a particular—(a)  trademark, trade name, patent, design or type,(b)  place of origin, or(c)  producer or supplier.If these matters are referred to, the procurement documents must also provide that tenders, proposals or applications demonstrating equivalent quality or performance will not be disadvantaged.In this section—"procurement documents"  means—(a)  the tender notice or associated tender documents, including any requirements of a competitive tendering procedure, conditions of participation or award criteria;(b)  documents inviting suppliers to participate in a competitive selection process under a framework, including details of the process, any conditions of participation or criteria for the award of the contract;(c)  documents inviting suppliers to apply for membership of a dynamic market, including any conditions for membership;"United Kingdom standard"  means a standard that is—(a)  set by the British Standards Institution, or(b)  primarily developed for use in the United Kingdom, or part of the United Kingdom.

items.label: Procurement – automatic suspension of the entry into or modification of contracts
items.description: A contracting authority may not enter into a public contract, or modify a public contract or a convertible contract, if during any applicable standstill period—(a)  proceedings under this Part are commenced in relation to the contract, and(b)  the contracting authority is notified of that fact.The court may lift or modify this restriction by order under section 102.The above restriction does not apply if—(a)  the proceedings at first instance have been determined, discontinued or otherwise disposed of, and(b)  the court has not made an order to extend the restriction.In this section "convertible contract"  has the meaning given in section 74.See sections 51 and 76 for provision about standstill periods.

items.label: Procurement – award criteria
items.description: “Award criteria"  means criteria set in accordance with this section against which tenders may be assessed for the purpose of awarding a public contract under section 19 (award following competitive tendering procedure).In setting award criteria, a contracting authority must be satisfied that they—(a)  relate to the subject-matter of the contract,(b)  are sufficiently clear, measurable and specific,(c)  do not break the rules on technical specifications in section 56, and(d)  are a proportionate means of assessing tenders, having regard to the nature, complexity and cost of the contract.In setting award criteria, a contracting authority must—(a)  describe how tenders are to be assessed by reference to them and, in particular, specify whether failure to meet one or more criteria would disqualify a tender (the "assessment methodology"), and(b)  if there is more than one criterion, indicate their relative importance by—(i)  weighting each as representing a percentage of total importance,(ii)  ranking them in order of importance, or(iii)  describing it in another way.In setting award criteria for the assessment of tenders by reference to lots, a contracting authority—(a)  may limit the number of lots that may be awarded to any one supplier, and(b)  in doing so, must provide an objective mechanism for supplier selection in circumstances where a supplier would otherwise exceed the limit.The reference to the subject-matter of a contract includes a reference to—(a)  the goods, services or works to be supplied under the contract, including in respect of any aspect of their production, trading or other stage in their life-cycle;(b)  how or when those goods, services or works are to be supplied;(c)  the qualifications, experience, ability, management or organisation of staff where those factors are likely to make a material difference to the quality of goods, services or works being supplied;(d)  price, other costs or value for money in all the circumstances.In the case of a light touch contract, the reference to the subject-matter of the contract also includes a reference to—(a)  the views of an individual for whose benefit the services are to be supplied (a "service recipient"), or of a person providing care to a service recipient, in relation to—(i)  who should supply the services, and(ii)  how and when they should be supplied;(b)  the different needs of different service recipients;(c)  the importance of proximity between the supplier and service recipients for the effective and efficient supply of the services.

items.label: Procurement – award of contracts following a competitive tendering procedure
