items.description: Before inviting the submission of tenders in relation to the award of a regulated below-threshold contract, a contracting authority must—(a)  have regard to the fact that small and medium-sized enterprises may face particular barriers in competing for a contract, and(b)  consider whether such barriers can be removed or reduced.This does not apply in relation to the award of a contract in accordance with a framework.

items.label: Procurement – regulated below-threshold contracts: implied payment terms
items.description: The terms below are implied into every regulated below- threshold contract entered into by a contracting authority.Any sum due to be paid under the contract by the contracting authority must be paid before the end of the period of 30 days beginning with—(a)  the day on which an invoice is received by the contracting authority in respect of the sum, or(b)  if later, the day on which the sum first became due in accordance with the invoice.The term above does not apply if the contracting authority—(a)  considers the invoice invalid, or(b)  disputes the invoice.On receiving an invoice from a payee, the contracting authority must notify the payee without undue delay if—(a)  it considers the invoice invalid, or(b)  it disputes the invoice.A contracting authority may rely on a payment made by a third party to satisfy the term above only with the agreement of the payee.For these purposes an invoice is valid if it sets out the minimum required information and meets any other requirement set out in the contract.The minimum required information is—(a)  the name of the invoicing party,(b)  a description of the goods, services or works supplied,(c)  the sum requested, and(d)  a unique identification number.These terms are also implied into any contract that is wholly or substantially for the purpose of performing (or contributing to the performance of) all or any part of the contract referred to above, but for these purposes, references in those terms to the contracting authority are to be read as references to the person to whom goods, services or works are supplied for the purpose of performing (or contributing to the performance of) all or any part of the contract referred to above.Any term purporting to restrict or override the terms implied by this section is without effect.Nothing in this section prohibits the parties to a contract from agreeing that a sum due under the contract must be paid earlier than would be required by this section.A Minister of the Crown or the Welsh Ministers may by regulations amend this section for the purpose of changing the number of days referred to above, but the number of days may not be more than 30 days.In this section—(a)  "payee"  means the person due to be paid under the invoice concerned;(b)  a reference to a contracting authority receiving an invoice includes a reference to an invoice being delivered to an address specified in the contract for the purpose.

items.label: Procurement – regulated below-threshold contracts: notices
items.description: A contracting authority may not advertise for the purpose of inviting tenders in relation to the award of a notifiable below-threshold contract without first publishing a below-threshold tender notice.The above does not apply if a contracting authority advertises only for the purpose of inviting tenders from particular or pre-selected suppliers.As soon as reasonably practicable after entering into a notifiable below- threshold contract, a contracting authority must publish a contract details notice.A "notifiable below-threshold contract" is a regulated below-threshold contract with an estimated value of—(a)  in the case of a contract to be awarded by—(i)  a central government authority that is not a devolved Welsh authority, not less than £12,000;(ii)  a central government authority that is a devolved Welsh authority, not less than £30,000, or(b)  otherwise, not less than £30,000.A "below-threshold tender notice" is a notice setting out—(a)  that the contracting authority intends to award a contract, and(b)  any other information specified in regulations under section 95.Any time limits provided for in a below-threshold tender notice must be—(a)  reasonable, and(b)  the same for each supplier.A Minister of the Crown or the Welsh Ministers may by regulations amend this section for the purpose of amending the financial thresholds.

items.label: Procurement – regulated below-threshold contracts: procedure
items.description: If a contracting authority invites the submission of tenders in relation to the award of a regulated below-threshold contract, the authority may not restrict the submission of tenders by reference to an assessment of a supplier's suitability to perform the contract.The reference to a supplier's suitability to perform the contract includes a reference to a supplier's—(a)  legal and financial capacity;(b)  technical ability.The above does not apply in relation to a works contract if the contract has an estimated value of—(a)  in the case of a contract to be awarded by a central government authority, not less than £138,760, or(b)  otherwise, not less than £213,477.A Minister of the Crown may by regulations amend this section for the purpose of amending the financial thresholds.This section does not apply in relation to—(a)  the award of a contract by a devolved Welsh authority, unless it is awarded under a reserved procurement arrangement,(b)  the award of a contract under a devolved Welsh procurement arrangement, or(c)  the award of a contract in accordance with a framework.

items.label: Procurement – reserving contracts to public service mutuals
items.description: A This section applies in relation to the award of a public contract under section 19 if the contract—(a)  is for reservable light touch services, and(b)  has a maximum term of five years or less.A competitive flexible procedure may provide for suppliers that are not qualifying public service mutuals to be excluded from participating in, or progressing as part of, the procedure.The following applies in relation to the award of a public contract under section 19 if the competitive flexible procedure provides for suppliers to be excluded.In assessing tenders under section 19, a contracting authority must disregard any tender from a supplier that is not a qualifying public service mutual.A "qualifying public service mutual"  means a public service mutual that has not entered into a comparable contract during the period of three years ending with the day on which the contract referred to above is awarded.A "public service mutual"  means a body that—(a)  operates for the purpose of delivering public services and mainly for the purpose of delivering one or more reservable light touch services,(b)  is run on a not-for-profit basis or provides for the distribution of profits only to members, and(c)  is under the management and control of its employees.In this section—"comparable contract"  means a contract that was—(a)  a contract for the same kind of services,(b)  awarded by the same contracting authority, and(c)  awarded in reliance on this section;"reservable light touch services"  means services of a kind specified in regulations.

items.label: Procurement – reserving contracts to supported employment providers
items.description: A competitive flexible procedure may provide for suppliers that are not supported employment providers to be excluded from participating in, or progressing as part of, the procedure.The following applies in relation to the award of a public contract under section 19 if the competitive flexible procedure provides for suppliers to be excluded as set out above.In assessing tenders under section 19, a contracting authority must disregard any tender from a supplier that is not a supported employment provider.A "supported employment provider"  means an organisation that operates wholly or partly for the purpose of providing employment, or employment- related support, to disabled or disadvantaged individuals where—(a)  disabled or disadvantaged individuals represent at least 30 per cent of the workforce of the organisation,(b)  if a particular part of the organisation is to perform the contract, disabled or disadvantaged individuals represent at least 30 per cent of the workforce of that part of the organisation, or(c)  if more than one organisation is to perform the contract, disabled or disadvantaged individuals represent at least 30 per cent of the combined workforce of—(i)  those organisations,(ii)  where a particular part of each organisation is to perform the contract, those parts, or(iii)  where a combination of organisations and parts is to perform the contract, those organisations and parts.

items.label: Procurement – standstill periods on the award of contracts
items.description: A contracting authority may not enter into a public contract before—(a)  the end of the mandatory standstill period, or(b)  if later, the end of another standstill period provided for in the contract award notice.The "mandatory standstill period"  is the period of eight working days beginning with the day on which a contract award notice is published in respect of the contract.This does not apply in relation to a contract that is—(a)  awarded under section 41 by reference to paragraph 13 of Schedule 5 (direct award: extreme and unavoidable urgency);(b)  awarded under section 41 by reference to regulations under section 42 (direct award to protect life, etc);(c)  awarded under section 41 or 43 (direct award and switching to direct award) by a private utility;(d)  awarded in accordance with a framework;(e)  awarded by reference to a dynamic market;(f)  a light touch contract.If a contract is of a kind described above, a contracting authority may not enter into the contract before the end of any standstill period (a "voluntary standstill period") provided for in the contract award notice.A voluntary standstill period may not be less than a period of eight working days beginning with the day on which the contract award notice is published.

items.label: Procurement – sub contracting specifications
items.description: If a contracting authority considers that the authority could award a contract for the supply of certain goods, services or works to a particular supplier under section 41 (direct award in special cases); in awarding a contract that is wholly or partly for the supply of those goods, services or works under section 19 (award following competitive tendering procedure), the contracting authority may require that a supplier sub-contracts the supply of those goods, services or works to the particular supplier.

items.label: Procurement – sub-contracting directions
items.description: This section applies in relation to a supplier if—(a)  a contracting authority, as a condition of awarding a public contract, required that the supplier sub-contract the supply of certain goods, services or works to another supplier, or(b)  the supplier—(i)  indicated to a contracting authority that it intended to sub- contract all or part of a public contract to another supplier, and(ii)  relied on that other supplier to satisfy any conditions of participation (see section 22(8)).The contracting authority may direct that the supplier enter into a legally binding arrangement with the other supplier for the purpose of that supplier performing all or part of the contract (as required or indicated).If a supplier fails to enter into a legally binding arrangement as directed by the contracting authority, the contracting authority may—(a)  choose not to enter into the contract with the supplier,(b)  direct the supplier to enter into a legally binding arrangement with another appropriate supplier, or(c)  if the contract has already been entered into, terminate the contract.an "appropriate supplier"  means a supplier that—(a)  is not an excluded supplier, and(b)  could have been relied on in place of the supplier referred to in subsection (1)(b)(ii).The reference to a condition of award includes, in the case of a direct award, any condition attaching to the award of a contract.A supplier is not to be treated as having relied on another supplier to satisfy conditions of participation if the conditions were satisfied by the first supplier alone.

items.label: Procurement – switching to Direct Award
items.description: A contracting authority may award a public contract directly to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier if—(a)  the authority has invited suppliers to submit tenders as part of, or requests to participate in, a competitive tendering procedure in respect of the contract,(b)  it has not received any suitable tenders or requests in response, and(c)  it considers that award under section 19 is not possible in the circumstances.A tender or request is not suitable if the contracting authority considers that—(a)  it would be disregarded in an assessment of tenders under section 19(3)(a), (b) or (c);(b)  it does not satisfy the contracting authority's requirements or the award criteria when assessed by reference to the assessment methodology and the relative importance of the criteria indicated under section 23(3);(c)  there is evidence of corruption or collusion between suppliers or between suppliers and contracting authorities;(d)  it materially breaches a procedural requirement in the tender notice or associated tender documents.A reference to a tender breaching a procedural requirement includes a reference to a supplier breaching a procedural requirement in relation to the tender.A breach is material if the contracting authority considers that ignoring it would put the tender at an unfair advantage.A contracting authority may carry out a selection process or take such other preliminary steps as it considers appropriate for the purpose of awarding a contract by direct award.Before awarding a contract to a supplier under this section, a contracting authority must consider whether the supplier—(a)  is an excludable supplier, or(b)  submitted an unsuitable tender or request in response to the invitation.

items.label: Procurement – Tender notices and associated tender documents
items.description: A contracting authority must publish a tender notice for the purpose of—(a)  inviting suppliers to submit a tender as part of an open procedure, or(b)  in the case of a competitive flexible procedure—(i)  inviting suppliers to submit a request to participate in the procedure, or(ii)  where no such invitation is made, inviting suppliers to submit their first, or only, tender as part of the procedure.A "tender notice"  means a notice setting out—(a)  that a contracting authority intends to award a public contract under section 19, and(b)  any other information specified in regulations under section 95.A contracting authority must provide any associated tender documents in accordance with the tender notice."Associated tender document"  means, in relation to a tender notice, a document setting out information specified in regulations under section 95 that supplements that set out in the tender notice.A contracting authority may not invite suppliers to submit a tender as part of a competitive tendering procedure unless it is satisfied that the tender notice or associated tender documents contain—(a)  information sufficient to allow suppliers to prepare such a tender, and(b)  in particular, details of the goods, services or works required by the contracting authority.(6)  In detailing its requirements, a contracting authority must be satisfied that they—(a)  are sufficiently clear and specific, and(b)  do not break the rules on technical specifications in section 56.See section 40 for an exception to the duty in subsection (1) for contracts awarded by reference to suppliers' membership of certain utilities dynamic markets.

items.label: Procurement – terminating public contracts: national security
items.description: A relevant contracting authority may not terminate a contract by reference to the implied term in section 78 on the basis of the discretionary exclusion ground in paragraph 14 of Schedule 7 (threat to national security) unless—(a)  the authority has notified a Minister of the Crown of its intention, and(b)  the Minister considers that—(i)  the supplier or sub-contractor is an excludable supplier by reference to paragraph 14 of Schedule 7, and(ii)  the contract should be terminated.A relevant contracting authority may not terminate a contract by reference to the implied term in section 78 on the basis of the mandatory exclusion ground in paragraph 35 of Schedule 6 (threat to national security) unless the authority has notified a Minister of the Crown of its intention.In this section, a "relevant contracting authority"  means a contracting authority other than—(a)  a Minister of the Crown or a government department,(b)  the Corporate Officer of the House of Commons, or(c)  the Corporate Officer of the House of Lords.

items.label: Procurement – The National Procurement Policy Statement
items.description: A contracting authority must have regard to the national procurement policy statement.The above does not apply—(a)  to private utilities;(b)  in relation to the award of a contract—(i)  in accordance with a framework, or(ii)  by reference to suppliers' membership of a dynamic market;(c)  in relation to procurement under a devolved Welsh procurement arrangement or transferred Northern Ireland procurement arrangement;(d)  to a devolved Welsh authority or transferred Northern Ireland authority, except in relation to procurement under a reserved procurement arrangement (but not an arrangement of a kind mentioned in paragraph (b)).

items.label: Procurement – The Welsh Procurement Policy Statement
items.description: The following contracting authorities must have regard to the Wales procurement policy statement—(a)  a devolved Welsh authority, except in relation to procurement under a reserved procurement arrangement or transferred Northern Ireland procurement arrangement;(b)  a contracting authority other than a devolved Welsh authority in relation to procurement under a devolved Welsh procurement arrangement. But the above) does not apply—(a)  to private utilities;(b)  in relation to the award of a contract—(i)  in accordance with a framework, or(ii)  by reference to suppliers' membership of a dynamic market.

items.label: Procurement – time limits
items.description: In setting time limits for the purposes of this Part, a contracting authority must, where relevant, have regard to—(a)  the nature and complexity of the contract being awarded;(b)  the need for site visits, physical inspections and other practical steps;(c)  the need for sub-contracting;(d)  the nature and complexity of any modification of the tender notice or any associated tender documents;(e)  the importance of avoiding unnecessary delay.Time limits set for the purposes of this Part must be the same for each supplier.A participation period and tendering period must equal or exceed the shortest minimum period specified in the tables shown in full in the section.

items.label: Procurement – transparency notices
items.description: Before awarding a contract under section 41 or 43 a contracting authority must publish a transparency notice. A "transparency notice"  means a notice setting out—(a)  that a contracting authority intends to award a contract directly, and(b)  any other information specified in regulations under section 95. This section does not apply in relation to the award of a contract under section 41 by virtue of paragraph 15 of Schedule 5 (direct award: user choice contracts).

items.label: Procurement – Treaty state suppliers: non-discrimination
items.description: A contracting authority may not, in carrying out a procurement, discriminate against a treaty state supplier.A contracting authority discriminates against a treaty state supplier if it treats the supplier less favourably than it treats, or would treat, a United Kingdom supplier or other treaty state supplier because of—(a)  the supplier's association with the supplier's treaty state, or(b)  the supplier's lack of association with—(i)  the United Kingdom, or(ii)  another treaty state.On a comparison of cases for the above purposes, there must be no material difference between the circumstances relating to each case.In this section, a reference to a supplier's association with a state includes a reference to the fact that the state is the place of origin of goods, services or works supplied by the supplier.In this section, a "treaty state"  means a state, territory or organisation of states or territories that is party to an international agreement specified in Schedule 9, other than the United Kingdom.And, in (a) above, a treaty state is a supplier's treaty state if the supplier is entitled to the benefits of such an international agreement by reference to that treaty state being party to the agreement.In this Act, "United Kingdom supplier"  means a supplier that is—(a)  established in, or controlled or mainly funded from, the United Kingdom, a British Overseas Territory or a Crown Dependency, and(b)  is not a treaty state supplier.

items.label: Procurement – voluntary standstill period on the modification of contracts
items.description: A contracting authority may not modify a public contract or a convertible contract before the end of any standstill period ("a voluntary standstill period") provided for in a contract change notice in respect of the contract. A voluntary standstill period may not be less than a period of eight working days beginning with the day on which the contract change notice is published.

items.label: Product compliance and safety - medical devices
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to medical devices sold directly to the public.

items.label: Product labelling - footwear
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Regulations relating to footwear labelling.

items.label: Product labelling - Olympic Symbol protection
items.description: The local authority may take action against anyone who uses the Olympic symbol or other controlled representation on goods or packaging or who has or makes an article specifically designed or adapted for making copies of a controlled representation.

items.label: Product Regulation and Metrology – Enforcement of Metrology Regulations
items.description: A local authority must, if ordered to do so by Regulations, enforce metrology Regulations made under the Act.

items.label: Product Regulation and Metrology – Enforcement of Product Regulations
items.description: A local authority must, if ordered to do so by Regulations, enforce product Regulations made under the Act.

items.label: Product Regulation and Metrology – Fees and Costs
items.description: A local authority impose and recover fees and costs for carrying out work under the Act to the extent allowed for by Regulations.

items.label: Product Regulation and Metrology – Sharing of Data
items.description: A local authority may share data referred to in Regulations regarding product regulation and metrology regulation to the extent allowed for by Regulations.

items.label: Product safety - brake linings on road vehicles
items.description: The local authority may initiate proceedings against a person who attempts to supply or to fit to a vehicle brake linings which do not conform to the regulations.

items.label: Product safety - electromagnetic compatibility
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce Regulations and to carry out Market Surveillance relating to the ability of equipment to function satisfactorily in its electromagnetic environment without introducing intolerable electromagnetic disturbances to other equipment in that environment.

items.label: Product safety - entry, investigation and test purchases
items.description: An enforcement authority shall have power to issue suspension, withdrawal or recall notices where there is a potential health and safety risk.  In order to investigate the authority has the power to enter premises and to make test purchases.

items.label: Product safety - gas appliances
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Regulations relating to gas appliances

items.label: Product safety - general enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and enforce regulations relating to general product safety.

items.label: Product safety - issue of notices for gas appliances
items.description: A local authority may serve a compliance notice, a withdrawal notice or a recall notice on a relevant economic operator in respect of an appliance or fitting if the authority has reasonable grounds for believing that there is non-compliance with regulations

items.label: Product safety - nightwear
items.description: The local authority has the power to seize and test goods to ensure compliance with regulations relating to nightwear safety.

items.label: Product safety - oil heaters
items.description: The local authority may test oil heaters to ensure compliance with safety regulations

items.label: Product safety - pedal bicycles
items.description: The local authority has the power to institute proceedings against anyone who fails to comply with regulations relating to the supply of either assembled bicycles or bicycles with unassembled parts.

items.label: Product safety - pressure equipment
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the safety of pressure equipment and assemblies of pressure equipment.

items.label: Product safety - pyrotechnic articles
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce the regulations relating to the safety of pyrotechnic articles as defined in the regulations.

items.label: Product safety - REACH enforcement
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to REACH (the registration, evaluation, authorisation and restriction of chemicals)

items.label: Product safety - recreational craft
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to recreational craft.

items.label: Product safety - simple pressure vessels
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the safety of simple pressure vessels

items.label: Product safety - supply of machinery
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the safety of supplied machinery

items.label: Protection of freedom - surveillance cameras
items.description: Local authorities must have regard to the Code of Practice issued under section 29(1) of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 when exercising any functions to which the Code relates.

items.label: Provision of garage accommodation
items.description: A local authority may provide, maintain and repair garage facilities.

items.label: Provision of recreational facilities
items.description: A local authority may provide, grant loans or charge for recreational facilities.

items.label: Provision of sanitary appliances at places of entertainment
items.description: A local authority may by notice require the owner or occupier of a place of entertainment to provide sanitary appliances.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - enforcement of access provisions
items.description: A person authorised  by a local authority may—enter premises in respect of which an access prohibition is in effect (see section 22(6)); anddo anything necessary to secure the premises against entry.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - entry or search of premises
items.description: A local authority may apply to a Magistrate’s court for a warrant to enter and search premises in certain circumstances

items.label: Psychoactive substances - entry, search and seizure – reasonable force
items.description: A local authority officer may use reasonable force in exercising the powers of entry, search and seizure under the Act

items.label: Psychoactive substances - examination, testing and taking samples
items.description: A local authority officer to whom a warrant under section 39 has been issued may examine, test and take samples of substances found on the premises

items.label: Psychoactive substances - forfeiture of seized items
items.description: A local authority may apply to a court for the forfeiture of seized items.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - premises notice
items.description: A local authority may issues a premises notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - production of documents
items.description: A local authority officer to whom a warrant under section 39 has been issued may require the production of documents

items.label: Psychoactive substances - prohibition notices
items.description: A local authority may issues a prohibition notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - prohibition or premises order
items.description: A local authority may apply for a Prohibition or Premises Order in certain circumstances

items.label: Psychoactive substances - recovery of costs
items.description: A local authority may apply to a court to recover its costs expended in enforcing access provisions.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - return or disposal of seized items
items.description: A local authority must comply with its duty to return or dispose of items seized under the Act

items.label: Psychoactive substances - seizure and detention of items, notices and records
items.description: A local authority officer who has seized items using powers under the Act must comply with the requirements under the Act relating to the giving of notices and keeping records

items.label: Psychoactive substances - seizure of items or documents
items.description: A local authority officer to whom a warrant under section 39 has been issued may seize and/or detain items and take copies of documents or records.

items.label: Psychoactive substances - variation or discharge of prohibition or premises orders
items.description: A local authority may apply for the variation or discharge of a Prohibition or Premises Order in certain circumstances

items.label: Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 Provision of Information
items.description: A local authority must, provide the Minister with information when presented with a valid Information Notice.

items.label: Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 Provision of Information - Review
items.description: A local authority may apply to the Minister to review the issue of the Information Notice.

items.label: Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 Recovery of proceeds – Sharing
items.description: A local authority may share proceeds recovered where the Minister has recovered sums on its behalf with the Minister.

items.label: Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 – General Duty
items.description: A local authority must, co-operate with an investigation by the Cabinet Office Minister into fraud and must pay any fees incurred by the Minister.

items.label: Public clocks - provision
items.description: Any urban authority may from time to time provide such clocks as they consider necessary, and cause them to be fixed on or against any public building, or, with the consent of the owner or occupier, on or against any private building the situation of which may be convenient for that purpose, and may cause the dials thereof to be lighted at night, and may from time to time alter and remove any such clocks to such other like situation as they may consider expedient.

items.label: Public clocks - repairing, maintaining, winding up, and lighting
items.description: A local authority may repair, maintain, wind up and light up a public clock.

items.label: Public health - animals
items.description: LAs have the powers along with the Secretary of State and the Food Standards Agency to appoint inspectors, who have powers of entry and inspection

items.label: Public health - application of legislation to Crown property
items.description: A local authority may enter into an agreement regarding the application of the Act to Crown property.

items.label: Public health - appointment of Director of Public Health
items.description: Each local authority must, acting jointly with the Secretary of State, appoint an individual to have responsibility for public health functions within the authority area.

items.label: Public health - appointment of directors
items.description: A local authority must, acting jointly with the Secretary of State, appoint a director of public health.  A local authority must have regard to any guidance given by the Secretary of State in relation to its director of public health, including guidance as to appointment and termination of appointment, terms and conditions and management.

items.label: Public health - arbitration of water rights
items.description: A local authority may refer certain disputes relating to water rights to arbitration.

items.label: Public health - arrangements between local authorities and NHS bodies
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations made by the Welsh ministers regarding co-operation between them and NHS bodies in Wales.

items.label: Public health - arrangements between NHS bodies and local authorities
items.description: A local authority must have regard to regulations regarding joint arrangements between the NHS and the local authority for carrying out prescribed arrangements for the discharge of prescribed functions concerning exercise of its health function.

items.label: Public health - authority actions where child excluded from school
items.description: Where a local authority has required that a child is kept away from school for public health reasons the authority must as soon as reasonably practicable after serving such notice inform the headteacher of the child's school that it has served the notice and of the contents of the notice.The authority must review the notice within 5 working days beginning with the day on which the request is made where the child's parent is requesting a review in respect of that notice for the first time and must inform the parent and the headteacher of the child's school of the outcome of the review.A local authority must inform the child's parent and the headteacher of the child's school as soon as reasonably practicable where a notice has expired and no further notice is to be served.

items.label: Public health - bathing huts
items.description: A local authority may provide bathing huts or conveniences and charge for the use of the same.

items.label: Public health - byelaws
items.description: A local authority may pass byelaws under the Act.

items.label: Public health - byelaws concerning pleasure fairs and roller skating
items.description: A local authority may pass bye laws to regulate pleasure fairs and roller skating to ensure public safety.

items.label: Public health - byelaws for privately run swimming baths and pools
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws regulation the use of swimming baths and swimming pools whether open or covered not under local authority control.

items.label: Public health - byelaws for tents, vans and sheds used for human habitation
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws for promoting cleanliness in, and the habitable conditions of, tents, vans, sheds and similar structures used for human habitation and generally for the prevention of nuisances in connection therewith.

items.label: Public health - byelaws for the prevention of nuisances
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws to prevent the occurrence of nuisances from snow, filth, dust, ashes and rubbish, the keeping of animals so as to be prejudicial to health and the movement through streets of offensive matter or liquids.

items.label: Public health - byelaws regulating hop and fruit pickers
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws regulating the provision of accommodation for hop, fruit, vegetable, flower or bulb pickers.

items.label: Public health - byelaws to regulate public bathing
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws to regulate public bathing including specifying the times and places where public bathing is permitted or prohibiting bathing where it may be dangerous.

items.label: Public health - canal boats
items.description: A local authority shall enforce any regulations regarding canal boats in respect of those boats present in it's area.

items.label: Public health - cleaning of common courts and passages
items.description: A local authority may sweep, clean and remove rubbish from common courts and passages and recover the expense of doing the same.

items.label: Public health - cleansing of premises
items.description: A local authority may issue a notice requiring the cleansing of filthy or verminous premises and if that notice is not complied with it may carry out the work itself and recover the expenses involved in doing so.

items.label: Public health - cleansing stations
items.description: A local authority may provide cleansing stations to enable it to discharge its functions under the Act.

items.label: Public health - closure of public baths during winter months
items.description: A local authority may temporarily close a public bath between 1 October and 31 March to allow its use for other purposes.

items.label: Public health - co-operation between NHS bodies and authorities
items.description: In exercising their respective functions NHS bodies (on the one hand) and local authorities (on the other) must co-operate with one another in order to secure and advance the health and welfare of the people of England and Wales.

items.label: Public health - co-operation between NHS bodies and local authorities
items.description: In exercising their respective functions NHS bodies (on the one hand) and local authorities (on the other) must co-operate with one another in order to secure and advance the health and welfare of the people of England and Wales.Local Authorities must also have regard to any guidance published by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Public health - compensation
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation to a person or body who suffers any direct pecuniary loss in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public health - complaints about exercise of public health functions
items.description: A local authority must have regard to regulations made in relation to complaints concerning exercise of its health functions.

items.label: Public health - conducting water to baths and wash-houses
items.description: A local authority may lay pipes and apparatus for the purpose of conducting water to baths and wash-houses.

items.label: Public health - contribution of expenses for works on watercourses
items.description: A local authority may defray the costs of works relating to certain watercourses.

items.label: Public health - control of certain diseases
items.description: A local authority shall, where stipulated, comply with regulations for the control of certain diseases.

items.label: Public health - cost of Ministerial orders
items.description: A local authority must pay the cost of Ministerial orders in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public health - court order for cleansing ponds, pools, ditches and gutters
items.description: A local authority may apply for a court order requiring a neighbouring local authority to carry out works in respect of ponds, pools, ditches and gutters lying near to, or forming, boundary of district.

items.label: Public health - culverting for building works
items.description: A local authority may by notice require or allow the owner of land to culvert certain water courses in connection with building works.

items.label: Public health - defective lavatories in buildings
items.description: A local authority may issue a notice requiring the repair of a defective closet (lavatory).

items.label: Public health - dental public health
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding its dental public health function.

items.label: Public health - directed mortuaries and post-mortem rooms
items.description: A local authority must provide mortuaries and post-mortem rooms if required to do so by the Minister and may make byelaws and charge for the use of the same.

items.label: Public health - directed partnership arrangements in England
items.description: A local authority must comply with any directions made by the Secretary of State in respect of directed partnership arrangements for a failing body.

items.label: Public health - directed partnership arrangements in Wales
items.description: A local authority must enter into directed partnership arrangements when directed by the Welsh ministers.

items.label: Public health - discretionary mortuaries and post-mortem rooms.
items.description: A local authority may provide mortuaries and post-mortem rooms, may make byelaws and charge for the use of the same

items.label: Public health - enforcement of byelaws for hairdressers and barbers
items.description: A local authority must enforce byelaws made under section 77 to regulate hairdressers and barbers.

items.label: Public health - entry of premises in connection with Public Health Act
items.description: An officer duly authorised by a local authority may enter premises to ascertain compliance with byelaws and building regulations.

items.label: Public health - equipment and facilities
items.description: A local authority may make equipment and facilities available to other authorities and accommodation available to certain local authority officers.

items.label: Public health - establishment of a care trust
items.description: A local authority must publish proposals, inform and consult in the prescribed manner before establishing a care trust.

items.label: Public health - examination and testing of drains
items.description: A local authority may examine and test any sanitary convenience, drain, private sewer or cesspool believed to be defective.

items.label: Public health - execution of works on sewers and drains
items.description: A local authority may with the agreement of a third party carry out certain works on sewers and drains on his behalf and at his expense.

items.label: Public health - exercise by local authorities of certain public health functions
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding its public health function.

items.label: Public health - expenses of joint boards
items.description: A local authority must  pay towards the expenses of joint boards created under the Act.

items.label: Public health - expenses payable by instalments
items.description: A local authority may determine that certain expenses will be payable by instalment

items.label: Public health - fencing of land adjoining streets
items.description: A local authority may in certain circumstances issue a notice requiring an owner of land adjoining streets to fence off that land and if that work is not done, carry it out itself and recover the cost as a civil debt.

items.label: Public health - filthy or verminous articles
items.description: A local authority may remove filthy or verminous articles from premises and cleanse or destroy them in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public health - general functions
items.description: A local authority has the functions specified in relation to public health (including dental health) and must have regard to any document published by the Secretary of State in the exercise of prescribed functions and must make arrangements for the handling and recording of complaints.  An LA must ensure arrangements made by Local Healthwatch organisations with other persons include certain provisions about procedures, decision-making and the use of a trade mark.  An overview and scrutiny committee of a LA must acknowledge receipt of a referral of a social care matter by a Local Healthwatch organisation contractor within 20 working days

items.label: Public health - guidance from Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must have regard to any document published by the Secretary of State when exercising health functions.

items.label: Public health - Health and Wellbeing Board
items.description: A local authority must establish a Health and Wellbeing Board for its area.The Health and Wellbeing Board is to consist of—at least one councillor of the local authority, nominated in accordance with regulations,- the director of adult social services for the local authority,- the director of children’s services for the local authority,- the director of public health for the local authority,- a representative of the Local Healthwatch organisation for the area of the local authority,- a representative of each relevant clinical commissioning group- such other persons, or representatives of such other persons, as the local authority thinks appropriate.

items.label: Public health - health and wellbeing strategies
items.description: A local authority must formulate and implement a health and wellbeing strategy in accordance with regulations from the Welsh ministers.

items.label: Public health - improving health of people in local area
items.description: A local authority must take steps it considers appropriate to improve the health of people living within its area.

items.label: Public health - indemnity of members and officers
items.description: A local authority must indemnify members and officers in certain circumstances in relation to certain actions taken under the Act.

items.label: Public health - infection and contamination control
items.description: LAs in Wales have discretionary powers to prevent, protect against, control or provide a public health response to the incidence or spread of infection or contamination which presents or could present significant harm to human health. LAs can require that a child is kept away from school; a head teacher provide it with the names and contact details of the pupils at the school; disinfect or decontaminate things or premises on request from the owner or tenant; request specified things for health protection purposes and offer compensation or expenses in relation to a request; restrict contact with, and access to, a dead body and take action to relocate a dead body.

items.label: Public health - inspection of derelict petrol tanks
items.description: An officer authorised by a local authority may inspect derelict petrol tanks to ensure their compliance with the Act.

items.label: Public health - Integrated Care Partnerships
items.description: An integrated care board and each responsible local authority whose area coincides with or falls wholly or partly within the board's area must establish a joint committee for the board's area, with one member appointed by each responsible local authority.

items.label: Public health - joint boards
items.description: Certain local authorities may set up joint boards in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public health - joint committees with NHS Bodies and pooled funds
items.description: Where a function is exercisable jointly (by virtue of section 65Z5 or otherwise) by a relevant NHS Body and any  local authority or a combined authority, those bodies may—(a)  arrange for the function to be exercised by a joint committee of theirs;(b)  arrange for one or more of the bodies, or a joint committee of the bodies, to establish and maintain a pooled fund.Arrangements under this section may be made on such terms as may be agreed between the parties, including terms as to payment.

items.label: Public health - joint Local Health and Wellbeing Strategies
items.description: Where a local authority receives an integrated care strategy under section 116ZB(7)(b) of the Act, the responsible local authority must prepare a strategy ("a joint local health and wellbeing strategy") setting out how the assessed needs in relation to the responsible local authority's area are to be met if required.In preparing a strategy the local authority must, in particular, consider the extent to which the  assessed needs could be met more effectively by the making of arrangements under section 75 of the National Health Service Act 2006.When preparing a strategy under this section, the  local authority must have regard to the integrated care strategy prepared under section 116ZB,  the mandate published by the Secretary of State under section 13A of the National Health Service Act 2006, any guidance issued by the Secretary of State; and must  involve the Local Healthwatch organisation for the area of the local authority, and involve the people who live or work in that area.The local authority must publish each strategy prepared by it under this section.

items.label: Public health - joint overview and scrutiny committee
items.description: A local authority may set up a joint overview and scrutiny committee with other local authorities in relation to health services in accordance with Regulations.

items.label: Public health - joint working and delegation arrangements with NHS bodies
items.description: A local authority may agree with any relevant NHS body for any functions exercisable by the NHS body be exercised by or jointly with a local authority.

items.label: Public health - joint working with prison service
items.description: A local authority must in carrying out its public health function co-operate with the prison service in making arrangements to improve the health of prisoners.

items.label: Public health - life saving appliances.
items.description: A local authority may provide life- saving appliances at any place.

items.label: Public health - Ministerial default powers
items.description: A local authority which has failed to discharge their functions must comply with the Minister when exercising his default powers and pay any expenses incurred by the Minister in so doing.

items.label: Public health - monitoring of risks
items.description: It is the duty of the relevant local authority to carry out the function of monitoring of public health risks, and imposing or enabling the imposition of restrictions or requirements on or in relation to persons, things or premises in the event of, or in response to, a threat to public health in the authority area.

items.label: Public health - moveable dwellings licensing
items.description: A local authority may licence the use of land for moveable dwellings which includes any tent, any van or other conveyance whether on wheels or not, and, subject as hereinafter provided, any shed or similar structure, being a tent, conveyance or structure which is used either regularly, or at certain seasons only, or intermittently, for human habitation

items.label: Public health - nuisances
items.description: A local authority may take action against certain nuisances arising outside its district.

items.label: Public health - overflowing and leaking cesspools
items.description: A local authority may by notice require the repair of or other works to an overflowing or leaking cesspool.

items.label: Public health - overview and scrutiny committees
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the review and scrutiny of health services within its area.

items.label: Public health - Part 2a orders (England)
items.description: LAs in England must make reasonable enquiries of and give notice to prescribed persons of an application for a Part 2A order under the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 and may impose reasonable charges to recover the costs of actions taken where an order is in relation things and premises.   An LA must provide information to the person subject to the order and have regard to the impact of the order on the welfare of that person or any, where an order is for detention, isolation or quarantine. It must also report details of applications, orders and variations or revocations of orders to the Health Protection Agency

items.label: Public health - Part 2a orders (Wales)
items.description: LAs in Wales must make reasonable enquiries of and give notice to prescribed persons of an application for a Part 2A order under the Public Health (Control of Disease) Act 1984 and may impose reasonable charges to recover the costs of actions taken where an order is in relation things and premises.   An LA must provide information to the person subject to the order and have regard to the impact of the order on the welfare of that person or any, where an order is for detention, isolation or quarantine. It must also report details of applications, orders and variations or revocations of orders to the Welsh Ministers

items.label: Public health - payment of compensation for damages
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances to people who have suffered loss as a result of the exercise of its powers under the Act.

items.label: Public health - payments to board or commissioning group in Wales
items.description: A local authority may make payments to a Strategic Health Authority, a Primary Care Trust or a Local Health Board towards expenditure incurred or to be incurred by the body in connection with the performance by it of prescribed functions. in accordance with directions made by the Welsh ministers.

items.label: Public health - payments to boards and commissioning groups in England
items.description: A local authority may make payments to various boards and commissioning groups in connection with the exercise of its health function and must have regard to directions prescribed by the Secretary of State when so doing.

items.label: Public health - polluted water supplies
items.description: A local authority may close or restrict use from certain polluted water supplies.

items.label: Public health - ponds, pools, ditches and gutters
items.description: A local authority may carry out works in respect of ponds, pools, ditches and gutters or contribute towards the expenses of others doing the same.

items.label: Public health - prevention, care and aftercare
items.description: A local authority may to the extent directed by the Secretary of State and with his approval make arrangements for provide prevention, care and aftercare in relation to its health function.

items.label: Public health - prohibition of sale of verminous articles
items.description: A local authority may, in accordance with the prescribed procedure, require the removal of and destroy verminous household articles prepared or offered for sale and may recover certain expenses

items.label: Public health - prosecution of offences
items.description: A local authority may prosecute relevant offences under the Act.

items.label: Public health - protection of buildings
items.description: Where it appears to a local authority that any building in their area is unoccupied; or that the occupier of a building in their area is temporarily absent from it and it is not effectively secured against unauthorised entry; or is likely to become a danger to public health, the local authority may undertake works in connection with the building for the purpose of preventing unauthorised entry to it, or, as the case may be, for the purpose of preventing it becoming a danger to public health.

items.label: Public health - provision for the care of mothers
items.description: A local authority may make provision for the care of mothers, prevention, care and after-care, home help and laundry facilities,

items.label: Public health - provision of premises, equipment or accommodation
items.description: A local authority may provide premises, equipment or accommodation for certain purposes.

items.label: Public health - public baths and wash-houses
items.description: A local authority may provide public baths and wash houses, may issue byelaws in respect of the same and make charges for use.

items.label: Public health - public conveniences
items.description: A local authority may provide public conveniences in certain circumstances, may make byelaws charges for the same or let them out for rent

items.label: Public health - public pumps, wells, cisterns, reservoirs, conduits
items.description: A local authority may utilise or close public pumps, wells, cisterns, reservoirs and conduits used for the free supply of water.

items.label: Public health - reduction of pigeons and other birds
items.description: A local authority may take any steps for the purpose of abating or mitigating any nuisance, annoyance or damage caused by the congregation in any built-up area of house doves or pigeons or of starlings or sparrows.

items.label: Public health - regulation of hairdressers and barbers
items.description: A local authority may make byelaws for the purpose of securing the cleanliness of premises on which a hairdresser's or barber's business is carried on and of the instruments, towels, materials and equipment used therein, and the cleanliness of the hairdressers or barbers working in such premises in regard to both themselves and their clothing.

items.label: Public health - regulation of seaside pleasure boats
items.description: For the prevention of danger, obstruction or annoyance to persons bathing in the sea or using the seashore, a local authority may make byelaws regulating the speed of pleasure boats, regulating the use of pleasure boats so as to prevent their navigation in a dangerous manner or without due care and attention or without reasonable consideration for other persons and requiring the use of effectual silencers on pleasure boats propelled by internal combustion engines.

items.label: Public health - removal of accumulations of rubbish
items.description: A local authority may, in accordance with the prescribed procedure remove accumulations of rubbish.

items.label: Public health - removal of manure from a stables or mews
items.description: A local authority may serve a notice to requiring the removal of manure from stables or mews in an urban district in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public health - removal of noxious matter
items.description: A local authority may serve a notice to require an occupier to remove certain noxious matter in certain circumstances, remove the noxious substance itself and recover expenses.

items.label: Public health - repair and cleansing of culverts
items.description: A local authority may by notice require the owner of land to repair or cleanse culverts.

items.label: Public health - repair of drains, private sewers and waste pipes
items.description: A local authority may repair or cleanse drains, private sewers and waste pipes in certain circumstances and may recover certain expenses.

items.label: Public health - requirement to keep a child away from school
items.description: Where a local authority is satisfied that a child may be infected or contaminated, that the infection or contamination is one which presents or could present significant harm to human health, that there is a risk that the child might infect or contaminate others, that it is necessary to keep the child away from school in order to remove or reduce that risk and that keeping the child away from school is a proportionate response to the risk to others presented by the child, the authority may by serving notice on the child's parent require that the parent keep the child away from school.The content of the notice should be as detailed in regulations.The local authority may review the notice if they receive a request to do so (other than the first request from the child's parents).The local authority may vary or revoke such a notice.

items.label: Public health - sale of waste materials from street works
items.description: A local authority may sell certain waste materials arising from certain street works and after deducting its proper expenses must pay the balance of the monies to the owner of the materials.

items.label: Public health - seats, drinking fountains and cattle troughs
items.description: A local authority may erect or allow others to erect, subject to conditions, seats, drinking fountains or cattle troughs

items.label: Public health - temporary closure of public baths
items.description: A local authority may temporarily close a public bath to allow its use for swimming competitions and may make charges for that use.

items.label: Public health - vacation of building for fumigation
items.description: A local authority may, in accordance with the prescribed procedure, require the vacation of a building for the purposes of fumigation and may recover certain expenses.

items.label: Public health - verminous persons
items.description: A local authority may on request or with consent cleanse a verminous individual or his or her clothing.

items.label: Public health - water fluoridation schemes
items.description: Local authorities are required to follow procedural requirements in the exercise of their functions in relation to the consideration of proposals for new fluoridation schemes, variation or termination of existing fluoridation schemes, or the maintenance of existing fluoridation schemes.

items.label: Public health - weighing and measuring of children
items.description: Where a local authority carries out a weighing and measuring exercise it must comply with prescribed conditions and may process the resulting information, including personal information relating to the children concerned, and disclose it to prescribed persons. It may also process it for the purposes of research, monitoring, audit or the planning of services or for any purpose connected with public health as prescribed and must have regard to guidance issued by the Secretary of State.Local authorities have powers to discharge health scrutiny functions by:  overview and scrutiny committees and must discharge prescribed duties in so doing; or a joint committee and must do so in prescribed circumstances.  A local authority may make reports and recommendations to providers of health services on matters reviewed or scrutinised by it and must take steps to try to reach agreement in relation to any recommendations it has made.  A local authority may report relevant proposals to the Secretary of State in prescribed circumstances.

items.label: Public health -FGM protection order
items.description: A local authority is specified as a Third Party for the purposes of applying for an FGM protection order under paragraph 2 of Part 1 of Schedule 2 to the Female Genital Mutilation Act 2003 and as such can apply to the court for an FGM protection order without the leave of the court.

items.label: Public lavatories - abolition of turnstiles
items.description: A local authority must ensure that there are no turnstiles at public lavatories controlled or managed by a local authority.

items.label: Public meetings and assemblies - provision of room
items.description: A local authority may acquire or provide and furnish halls, offices and other buildings, whether within or without the area of the authority, for use for public meetings and assemblies.

items.label: Public order - prohibiting trespassory assemblies
items.description: If the chief officer of police reasonably believes that an assembly is intended to be held in a place which the public has no right to access or and that the assembly is likely to be held without the permission of the occupier of the land, and may result in serious disruption to the life of the community, or where the land, or a building or monument on it, is of historical, architectural, archaeological or scientific importance, in significant damage to the land, building or monument, he may apply to the council of the district for an order prohibiting for a specified period the holding of all trespassory assemblies in the district or a part of it, as specified.    On receiving such an application, a council may and Wales, with the consent of the Secretary of State make an order either in the terms of the application or with such modifications as may be approved by the Secretary of State

items.label: Public performance licence - person under 16
items.description: A local authority may issue a public performance licence to a person aged under 16 in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public performance licence - variation or revocation for person under 16
items.description: A local authority may vary or revoke a performance licence issued to a person aged under 16 in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public performance licence person under 14
items.description: A local authority may issue a public performance licence to a person aged under 14 in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public performance training licence for person 12 to 16 - issue, variation or revocation
items.description: A local authority may issue, vary or revoke a performance training licence for performances of a dangerous nature for persons aged 12 to 16 in certain circumstances.

items.label: Public safety - co-operation to assess and manage risk from offenders
items.description: The local authority has a duty to co-operate with the responsible authority (ie. police, prisons and probation acting jointly) on MAPPA (multi-agency public protection arrangements) to assess and manage the risks posed in that area by relevant sexual and violent offenders, and other persons who are considered by the responsible authority to be persons who may cause serious harm to the public, to the extent that such co-operation is compatible with the exercise by the local authority of its functions under any other enactment.

items.label: Public safety - collaboration to reduce and prevent serious violence
items.description: Local authorities must consult with certain stakeholders and collaborate with the police and with stakeholders in order to plan to prevent and reduce serious violence. Including a duty to plan together to exercise their functions so as to prevent and reduce serious violence in the area.In particular, the specified authorities for a local government area must:(a)  identify the kinds of serious violence that occur in the area,(b)  identify the causes of serious violence in the area, so far as it is possible to do so, and(c)  prepare and implement a strategy for exercising their functions to prevent and reduce serious violence in the area.

items.label: Public safety - consultation when preparing a strategy for serious violence
items.description: Local authorities must consult with:- each educational authority for the area- each prison authority for the area;- each youth custody authority for the area when preparing a strategy for exercising their functions to prevent and reduce serious violence in the area.In addition where two or more specified authorities have chosen to collaborate (see section 9) they must also consult every other specified authority for the area.

items.label: Public safety - decision to collaborate to prevent and reduce serious violence
items.description: Two or more specified authorities may collaborate with each other to prevent and reduce serious violence in a relevant area, providing they consult stakeholders as required when doing so.

items.label: Public safety - regard to guidance when collaborating on serious violence
items.description: Local authorities must have regard to Guidance issued by the Secretary of State, when exercising its powers and duties relating to collaborating and planning to prevent or reduce serious violence.

items.label: Public safety - strategy to prevent and reduce serious violence
items.description: Once a strategy to prevent or reduce serious violence has been prepared for a local government area, the specified authorities for the area must:(a)  publish the strategy,(b)  keep the strategy under review, and(c)  from time to time prepare and implement a revised strategy.

items.label: Public service delivery - disclosure to improve provision
items.description: A local authority may disclose information to improve public service delivery in certain circumstances and must have regard to any code of practice when so doing.

items.label: Public service delivery - disclosure to water and sewage undertakers
items.description: A local authority may disclose information to water and sewage undertakers in certain circumstances and must have regard to any code of practice when so doing.

items.label: Public Spaces Protection Order - breach of prohibition on consuming alcohol
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority may, where a person is or has been consuming alcohol in breach of a prohibition in a public spaces protection order, or intends to consume alcohol in circumstances in which doing so would be a breach of such a prohibition, (upon showing his identity) require that person not to consume, in breach of the order, alcohol or anything which the authorised person reasonably believes to be alcohol; or to surrender anything in that person’s possession which is, or which the authorised person reasonably believes to be, alcohol or a container for alcohol (and dispose of the same).  If the person fails to co-operate he commits a criminal offence.

items.label: Public Spaces Protection Order - fixed penalty notice
items.description: A person authorised by a local authority may issue a fixed penalty notice to anyone he or she has reason to believe has committed an offence under sections 63 or 67 in relation to a public spaces protection order.

items.label: Public Spaces Protection Order - guidance
items.description: A person authorised must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State when exercising its powers in relation to public spaces protection orders.

items.label: Public Spaces Protection Order - making and duration
items.description: A local authority may make a public spaces protection order if satisfied on reasonable grounds that activities carried on in a public place within the authority's area have had a detrimental effect on the quality of life of those in the locality, or it is likely that activities will be carried on in a public place within that area and that they will have such an effect; and that the effect, or likely effect, of the activities is, or is likely to be, of a persistent or continuing nature, is, or is likely to be, such as to make the activities unreasonable, and justifies the restrictions imposed by the notice.

items.label: Public Spaces Protection Order - restriction of right of way over highway
items.description: A local authority must take certain matters into account and take certain steps before making a public spaces protection order which restricts public right of way over a highway.

items.label: Public Spaces Protection Order - varying and discharge
items.description: A local authority may vary and discharge a public spaces protection order in accordance with regulations.  Where an order is varied or discharged details of the variation or discharge must be published in accordance with regulations made by the Secretary of State..

items.label: Public transport - accounts
items.description: Where a local authority run public service vehicles under this Part of this Act they shall in the accounts relating to their transport undertakings distinguish, so far as may be practicable receipts and expenditure relating to their public service vehicles from receipts and expenditure relating to any other transport undertaking, and in the receipts and expenditure relating to their public service vehicles shall further distinguish receipts and expenditure on capital account from receipts and expenditure upon revenue account.

items.label: Public transport - agreements for management of services
items.description: A local authority authorised to run public service vehicles under the Act may enter into agreements for the management and maintenance of such services with others.

items.label: Public transport - borrowing
items.description: A local authority authorised to run public service may borrow money with the consent of the Minister.

items.label: Public transport - byelaws and street furniture for waiting
items.description: A local authority may pass byelaws to regulate waiting for public vehicles and erect street furniture in support of those byelaws.

items.label: Public transport - charging for passengers and parcels
items.description: A local authority authorised to run public service vehicles under the Act may demand and take for passengers and small parcels carried on such vehicles such fares and charges as they may think fit.

items.label: Public transport - outside of area
items.description: A local authority who under any local Act or Order are operating a tramway, light railway, trolley vehicle, or omnibus undertaking, may as part of that undertaking run public service vehicles on any road inside or outside their district.

items.label: Public transport - prohibition on forming bus company
items.description: A relevant authority may not, in exercise of any of its powers, form a company for the purpose of providing a local service.

items.label: Public transport - purchase and maintenance of vehicles
items.description: A local authority may purchase and maintain vehicles for use in its public transport service and may purchase by agreement, take on lease, and hold lands and may on any lands so purchased by or leased to them or any lands lawfully appropriated by them for the purpose erect such buildings, sheds, and conveniences and may provide such plant and appliances as may be requisite or expedient for the establishment, running, equipment, maintenance and repair of their public service vehicles.

items.label: Public transport - quality contract schemes
items.description: A local authority which is also a transport authority and is proposing a quality contract scheme for bus services in its area must comply with and where relevant enforce the following Regulations.

items.label: Public transport facilities - capital expenditure
items.description: A local authority may make payments towards capital expenditure for public transport facilities in certain circumstances

items.label: Publication of information - local area agreement
items.description: A local authority must publish information regarding its Local Area Agreement.

items.label: Pupil referral units - management committee
items.description: Local authorities must establish management committees to run pupil referral units (PRUs) in their area, and make provision for the constitution and procedures of such committees.Local authorities must delegate some of their functions in relation to pupil referral units to the management committee but must not delegate functions in relation to staffing and finance of the unit, health and safety issues, control of premises and a reserve power in relation to prevention of a breakdown of discipline.

items.label: Recycling - charging for use of recycling sites
items.description: Best value authorities must not (by the disapplication of section 93(1) of the Local Government Act 2003) use the discretionary power to charge residents to deposit household waste at a household waste recycling centre.

items.label: Recycling - monitoring of compliance with battery recycling scheme
items.description: A local authority must monitor compliance with the scheme and accuracy of producer information

items.label: Recycling - publishing of information regarding waste batteries
items.description: A local authority must share and publish the prescribed information in the prescribed format in accordance with the Regulations.

items.label: Recycling - records and information
items.description: A local authority must collect information and maintain records about municipal waste and submit returns using the Waste Data Flow system.  It is liable to a penalty under the Measure of £200 per tonne by which it falls short of the target amount and £1000 when it fails to maintain records, submit a return or fails to comply with the requirements of any  notice served by the Welsh ministers or the monitoring authority in accordance with the Regulations and pay interest on late payment.

items.label: Recycling - register of battery producers
items.description: A local authority must prepare, maintain and make available a register of producers and publish applications for inclusion in the register the prescribed form.

items.label: Recycling - sharing of information regarding battery recycling schemes
items.description: A local authority may share certain information with certain bodies for certain purposes in accordance with the Regulations.

items.label: Recycling - waste batteries and accumulators
items.description: A local authority must comply with its general duties

items.label: Refuse disposal - acquisition of land
items.description: A local authority may acquire land for the purposes of refuse disposal in accordance with legislation.

items.label: Refuse disposal - powers of entry
items.description: An officer authorised by a local authority may enter land for certain purposes under the Act.

items.label: Registrars - appointment of deputy
items.description: A local authority may employ a deputy superintendent registrars or deputy registrar of births and deaths.

items.label: Registrars - appointment of officers
items.description: A local authority must employ (interim) superintendent registrars and registrars of births and deaths.

items.label: Registration - marriage and civil partnership referrals
items.description: A superintendent registrar or a registration authority must make a referral as prescribed to the Secretary of State and give the information prescribed in regulations 17 and 18 to the parties for the purposes of section 28H(5)(c)(i) and (ii) of the 1949 Marriage Act and section 12A(5)(c)(i) and (ii) of the 2004 Civil Partnership Act.

items.label: Registration - marriage/civil partnership gender recognition register
items.description: Local authorities (the Registrar General) must maintain a Gender Recognition Marriage Register, and a Gender Recognition Civil Partnership Register, which must not be open for public inspection or search.  The Registrar General must register the marriage and create a link (which is not to be open to public inspection) between the original marriage register entry and the new entry in the Gender Recognition Marriage Register and maintain the details in the registers as prescribed.

items.label: Registration - wedding venue licence
items.description: The local authority may grant a licence for a premises to act as a venue for marriages and civil partnerships in accordance with condition set out in Regulations.

items.label: Registration -marriages
items.description: Superintendent Registrars are required to follow the procedures prescribed relating to the registration of marriages.

items.label: Registration of births - within three months of the date of birth
items.description: Where the relevant registrar receives from any qualified informant before the expiration of three months from the date of the birth of a child information of the particulars required by Regulation 7(1) he shall forthwith register the birth and the particulars, if not previously registered, in the presence of the informant.

items.label: Registration of death - provision of information concerning death
