items.label: Special educational needs - continued provision where EHC plan maintained
items.description: This section applies where, immediately before a child in need reaches the age of 18—a local authority in England is providing services for the child in the exercise of functions conferred by section 17, andan EHC plan is maintained for the child.The local authority may continue to provide services for the child in the exercise of those functions after the child reaches the age of 18, but may not continue to do so after the EHC plan has ceased to be maintained.In this section “EHC plan” means a plan within section 37(2) of the Children and Families Act 2014.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - compliance with tribunal
items.description: Where a First-tier tribunal makes an order requiring an authority to take action the authority must:- If the order requires a home authority to make a detained person's EHC needs assessment, the home authority within 2 weeks of the order being made must notify the appropriate person that it must make the assessment.- Following the needs assessment send the results to designated persons within the proscribed timescales- Reconsider where the order directs it to do so within the proscribed timescalesIf the order requires the home authority to amend the name of the school or other institution or the type of school or other institution specified in the EHC plan, the home authority must issue the amended EHC plan within 2 weeks of the order being made.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - decision not to secure EHC plan
items.description: Where, following a detained person's EHC needs assessment, a home authority decides that it is not necessary for special educational provision to be made for the detained person in accordance with an EHC plan, the appropriate person must be notified as soon as practicable, and in any event within 16 weeks of the home authority receiving a request for a detained person's EHC needs assessment, or the date on which the detained person has been brought or comes to the attention of the authority.The home authority must also notify persons specified in Regulations.(3)  When notifying the appropriate person the home authority must also notify them of:(a)  their right to appeal that decision,(b)  the time limits for doing so,(c)  the information concerning mediation, set out in regulation 18, and(d)  the availability of information and advice relating to the special educational needs of children and young people.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - decision on EHC needs assessment
items.description: The home authority must notify the appropriate person and the person in charge of the relevant youth accommodation where the detained person is detained of its decision whether or not it is necessary to secure a detained person's EHC needs assessment as soon as practicable and in any event within 6 weeks of either receiving a request to secure a detained person's EHC needs assessment or  the date on which the detained person has been brought or comes to the attention of the authority. The home authority must also notify the persons who were notified in accordance with regulation 4(2) of its decision.(3)  When notifying the appropriate person of its decision that it is not necessary to secure a detained person's EHC needs assessment, it must also notify them of:(a)  their right to appeal that decision,(b)  the time limits for doing so,(c)  the information concerning mediation, (d)  the availability of information and advice in connection with a detained person's EHC needs assessment.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - determination of need for SEN provision
items.description: Where a home authority determines that it is not necessary for special educational provision to be made for the detained person in accordance with an EHC plan on release from detention it must:- Notify the appropriate person and the person in charge of the relevant youth accommodation where the detained person is detained, as soon as practicable, but in any event within 6 weeks of either receiving a request to secure a detained person's EHC needs assessment or the date on which the detained person has been brought or comes to the attention of the authority.- Where the home authority is considering securing a detained person's EHC needs assessment it must also notify relevant parties as identified in this regulation.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - disclosure of EHC plan
items.description: When an authority becomes responsible for keeping an EHC plan for a detained person it must send a copy of the plan to designated persons within 5 days.The EHC Plan must not be disclosed without the permission of the detained person except where specified by this legislation.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - incomplete assessment
items.description: Where an EHC plan for a person leaving detention or as a consequence of a detention order was started but is not completed the authority must ensure:(a) any EHC plan is finalised within 20 weeks;(b) any decision not to secure an EHC plan is finalised within 16 weeks;(c)a decision whether or not to secure an EHC needs assessment is made within 6 weeks;

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - mediation
items.description: Where the appropriate person has informed the mediation adviser that he or she wishes to pursue mediation, the home authority must arrange for mediation between it and the appropriate person, within 30 days from the date on which the mediation adviser was informed by the appropriate person that he or she wishes to pursue mediation.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - steps following mediation
items.description: Where mediation has resulted in an agreement such agreement must be documented in writing.  Where the issues are such that there is a right of appeal the authority must comply with time limits.  Where the issues do not allow the right of appeal the authority must take action within 2 weeks of the mediation agreement.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - timescales for EHC plans
items.description: When a home authority sends a draft plan to the appropriate person it must:(a)  give them at least 15 days, beginning with the day on which the draft plan was served, in which to—(i)  make representations about the content of the draft plan, and to request that a particular school or other institution be named in the plan, and(ii)  require the home authority to arrange a meeting between them and an officer of the home authority at which the draft plan can be discussed, and(b)  advise them where they can find information about the schools and colleges that are available for the detained person to attend on release from detention. The final plan must be sent to persons specified in Regulations as soon as practicable, and in any event within 20 weeks of the home authority receiving a request for an EHC needs assessment, or on the date which the detained person has been brought or comes to the attention of the authority.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - transfer of EHC plan
items.description: Where a detained person with an EHC plan is to be released the EHC plan must be disclosed to relevant parties within 5 days of the date of release.  Where the new authority receives a request to carry out an EHC assessment or to review the plan from the commissioning authority it must comply with the request.

items.label: Special educational needs - detained persons - unopposed appeals
items.description: Where the detained person has appealed to the First-tier Tribunal and the home authority notifies the First-tier Tribunal that it does not oppose the appeal before it submits a response the home authority must:- within 2 weeks of the date it notified the First-tier Tribunal under paragraph (1), notify the appropriate person that it must make a detained person's EHC needs assessment.- inform relevant. parties of its decision regarding the need for an EHC plan within specified time limits (subject to exceptions described in regulations)- issue draft and final EHC plans to relevant persons within the time limits specified (unless exceptional circumstances defined in regulations apply)- issue the amended EHC plan within 2 weeks of the date it notified the First-tier Tribunal.

items.label: Special educational needs - dispute resolution procedure in England
items.description: A local authority must prepare and publish a dispute resolution procedure relating to SEN matters and must have regard to guidance from the Secretary of State when so doing.

items.label: Special educational needs - dispute resolution procedure in Wales
items.description: A local authority must prepare and publish a dispute resolution procedure relating to SEN matters and must have regard to guidance from Welsh ministers when so doing.

items.label: Special educational needs - duties of governing body or local education authority
items.description: A local authority and the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with certain general duties regarding SEN provision

items.label: Special educational needs - education in mainstream school
items.description: A local authority must educate a child with SEN in a mainstream school unless it is incompatible with the wishes of his parent, or the provision of efficient education for other children.

items.label: Special educational needs - education in non-mainstream school
items.description: A local authority may educate a child with SEN in a non-mainstream school in certain circumstances.

items.label: Special educational needs - encouragement to remain in education or training
items.description: A local authority must make available to young people and relevant young adults such services as they consider appropriate to encourage, enable or assist them to engage and remain in education or training. The services are currently known as Connexions services. Local authorities can fulfil the duty to make services available either by providing them itself or by making arrangements with others which could include other local authorities.

items.label: Special educational needs - giving notice to or serving documents upon child
items.description: A local authority must give notice to or serve documents relating to a SEN appeal upon the child in certain circumstances.

items.label: Special educational needs - identification and assessment of needs
items.description: A local authority has a general duty to identify and assess SEN provision for the children for whom they are responsible.

items.label: Special educational needs - independent advocacy services
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements for the provision of independent advocacy services (relating to SEN) in their area, publicise the same and must have regard to guidance from Welsh Ministers when so doing.

items.label: Special educational needs - informing parent of SEN provision
items.description: A local authority in the case of a pupil referral unit or the governing body of a school maintained by the local authority must inform a parent when SEN provision is made.

items.label: Special educational needs - notice of no statement
items.description: A local authority must where it decides not to make a statement of SEN give the parent a notice in writing explaining the right to appeal.

items.label: Special educational needs - parental notification of assessment
items.description: Where an authority believes a child for whom they are responsible may have special educational needs they must notify the parents that they are considering an assessment and of the procedure for doing so.

items.label: Special educational needs - parental request for assessment
items.description: A local authority must assess a child's SEN at its parent's request in certain circumstances and comply with the appeals procedure and the outcome of any appeal.

items.label: Special educational needs - payment and assistance to city colleges
items.description: A local education authority may pay all or any part of the cost incurred and may provide any other assistance in respect of securing that the statemented provision for a relevant child is made.

items.label: Special educational needs - provision of goods and services
items.description: A local authority may provide goods and services to the governing body of a maintained school in connection with SEN provision.

items.label: Special educational needs - provision otherwise than in schools
items.description: A local authority must consult the parent where it proposes to make SEN provision otherwise than at school.

items.label: Special educational needs - provision outside England and Wales
items.description: A local authority may make SEN provision outside England and Wales in certain circumstances.

items.label: Special educational needs - publication of information
items.description: A local education authority shall publish information about  special educational provision for children with special educational needs (but without statements) in accordance with these regulations.  Information to be published is detailed in the Schedule to these RegulationsThe authority should keep that information under review, and where there is a significant change in any of that information, revise the information accordingly and publish the revised information in accordance with regulations.

items.label: Special educational needs - review and assessment on request of responsible body
items.description: A local authority must review or assess a child's SEN at the request of the responsible body in certain circumstances and comply with the appeals procedure and the outcome of any appeal.

items.label: Special educational needs - review of arrangements
items.description: A local authority must keep under review its SEN provision and consult with others as it thinks necessary or desirable.

items.label: Special educational needs - review of city college arrangements
items.description: A local education authority shall keep under review the arrangements made under these Regulations and in doing so shall consult the governing bodies of any city college in the authority’s area; and in any neighbouring local education authority’s area to which the authority makes any payment, supplies any goods and services or provides any assistance under these Regulations.

items.label: Special educational needs - reviews of educational needs
items.description: A local authority must comply with the prescribed process for reviewing SEN provision and the appeals procedure.

items.label: Special educational needs - statement
items.description: If in the light of an assessment of any child's educational needs and of any representations made by the child's parent it is necessary for the local education authority to, determine the special educational provision which any learning difficulty he may have calls for, the authority shall make and maintain a statement of his special educational needs.

items.label: Special educational needs and disability - compliance with SEN provision
items.description: Where a local authority maintains an EHC plan for a child the authority must secure the specified special educational provision for the child or young person.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - admittance to school
items.description: Where an EHC plan has been drawn up for a child with special educational needs or a disability and the plan names a school or other educational institution the governing body, proprietor or principal of the school or other institution must admit the child or young person for whom the plan is maintained.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - advice and information for families
items.description: A local authority must arrange for children and young people for whom it is responsible, and the parents of children for whom it is responsible, to be provided with advice and information about matters relating to the special educational needs or disabilities of the children or young people concerned.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - advice and information for others
items.description: A local authority may arrange for persons other than children and young people for whom it is responsible, and the parents of children for whom it is responsible, to be provided with advice and information about matters relating to the special educational needs or disabilities of the children or young people concerned.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - amendment of EHC plan following review
items.description: Where a review of an EHC plan has been carried out the authority must act in accordance with regulations and within specified time scales when considering amending an EHC plan or when deciding not to amend an EHC plan.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - appeal mediation
items.description: A local authority must inform the parent or young person of the right to mediation and participate in the same and notify other relevant bodies where appropriate.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - appeals pilot scheme
items.description: A local authority must comply with a pilot scheme for its area enabling child to appeal.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - appointment of SEN co-ordinator
items.description: The appropriate authority in mainstream schools and maintained nursery schools must designate a member of staff at the school (to be known as the “SEN co-ordinator”) as having responsibility for co-ordinating the provision for pupils with special educational needs.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - arrangements for resolving disagreements
items.description: A local authority must make arrangements for resolving disagreements between certain bodies in certain circumstances regarding and EHC plan.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - arrangements outside England and Wales
items.description: A local authority may arrange for the delivery of an EHC plan outside of England or Wales.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - cessation of EHC plan
items.description: A local authority may cease to maintain an EHC plan for a child or young person only if—(a) the authority is no longer responsible for the child or young person, or(b) the authority determines that it is no longer necessary for the plan to be maintained.The circumstances in which it is no longer necessary for an EHC plan to be maintained for a child or young person include where the child or young person no longer requires the special educational provision specified in the plan.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - co-operation with governing bodies
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with governing bodies of academic institutions and each governing body must co-operate with the authority, in the exercise of the authority's functions in relation to special educational needs.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - co-operation with partners
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with each of its local partners, and each local partner must co-operate with the authority, in the exercise of the authority's functions under Part 3.The authority must also make arrangements for ensuring co-operation between the officers of the authority.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - Code of Practice
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the Secretary of State’s Code of Practice regarding special educational needs and disabilities.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - discretionary re-assessment of EHC plan
items.description: A local authority may re-assess the educational, health care and social care needs of a child or young person for whom it maintains an EHC plan at any time and must consult as required.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - draft EHC plan
items.description: A local authority must where it is required to secure that an EHC plan is prepared for a child or young person, consult the child's parent or the young person about the content of the plan during the preparation of a draft of the plan.The local authority must then—(a) send the draft plan to the child's parent or the young person, and(b) give the parent or young person notice of his or her right to—(i) make representations about the content of the draft plan, and(ii) request the authority to secure that a particular school or other institution is named in the plan

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - EHC assessment
items.description: A local authority must make an EHC (Education, Health and Care) assessment for a qualifying child or young person. The authority must take into account the views of that child, young person or parent and must notify the child, young person and parents of the outcome with reasons.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - EHC plan
items.description: Where, in the light of an EHC needs assessment, it is necessary for special educational provision to be made for a child or young person in accordance with an EHC plan—(a)the local authority must secure that an EHC plan is prepared for the child or young person, and(b)once an EHC plan has been prepared, it must maintain the plan.A local authority must send the finalised EHC plan to—(a)  the child's parent or to the young person;(b)  the governing body, proprietor or principal of any school, other institution or provider of relevant early years education named in the EHC plan; and(c)  to the responsible commissioning body, as soon as practicable, and in any event within 20 weeks of the local authority receiving a request for an EHC needs assessment in accordance with section 36(1) of the Act, or of the local authority becoming responsible for the child in accordance with section 24 of the Act.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - EHC plan after 25th birthday
items.description: A local authority may continue to maintain an EHC plan for a young person until the end of the academic year during which the young person attains the age of 25.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - EHC plan appeals
items.description: A local authority must comply with the appeals process regarding EHC plans

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - EHC plan in relation to higher education
items.description: When a young person is intending to undertake a course of higher education, the local authority must disclose a copy of that young person’s EHC plan to: - any person in connection with the young person’s application for a disabled student’s allowance in accordance with chapter 3 of part 5 of the Education (Student Support) Regulations 2011(1)- the principal (or equivalent position) of the institution at which it has been confirmed that the young person has a place to undertake a course of higher education,within 15 working days of being asked to do so by the young person.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - general duties
items.description: When exercising function under Part 3 of the Act in the case of a child or young person, a local authority in England must have regard to certain general matters relating to inclusion and to sharing information with both parent(s) and the child/ young person

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - identification of children and young people with needs
items.description: A local authority in England must exercise its functions with a view to securing that it identifies—(a) all the children and young people in its area who have or may have special educational needs, and(b) all the children and young people in its area who have a disability.A local authority in England is responsible for a child or young person if he or she is in the authority’s area and has been identified by the authority as someone who has or may have special educational needs, or brought to the authority’s attention by any person as someone who has or may have special educational needs.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - information regarding provision
items.description: If special educational provision is made for a child or young person at a maintained school, a maintained nursery school, or a pupil referral unit, and no EHC plan is maintained for the child or young person.  The appropriate authority for the school must inform the child's parent or the young person that special educational provision is being made for the child or young person.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - inspection of institution
items.description: Where a local authority maintains an EHC plan for a child or young person, a person authorised by the authority is entitled to have access at any reasonable time to the premises of a school, post-16 institution or other institution at which education or training is provided in pursuance of the plan, for the purpose of monitoring the education or training.This power does not apply to the premises of a mainstream post-16 institution in Wales.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - integration of services
items.description: A local authority in England must exercise its functions with a view to ensuring the integration of educational provision and training provision with health care provision and social care provision, where it thinks that this would—(a) promote the well-being of children or young people in its area who have special educational needs or a disability, or(b) improve the quality of special educational provision.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - joint commissioning arrangements
items.description: A local authority and its partner commissioning bodies must make arrangements (“joint commissioning arrangements”) about the education, health and care provision to be secured for—(a) children and young people for whom the authority is responsible who have special educational needs, and(b) children and young people in the authority's area who have a disability.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - local offer
items.description: A local authority is responsible for providing  children and young people with special educationalneeds or disabilities and their families information about what supportservices the local authority think will be available in their local area (known as the 'local offer') and for makingsure the local offer is available for everyone to see.  The authority must consult with all parties specified in these Regulations when compiling the local offer and must involve children, their parents and young people in preparation and review of local offer.The authority must seek comments on the local offer from children and young people with special educational needs or a disability, and the parents of children with special educational needs or a disability must publish comments and the authority's response (in a form that does not enable any individual to be identified) together with the local offer on its website at least annually.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - mainstream schooling with EHC plan
items.description: A local authority must secure that the EHC plan provides for the child or young person to be educated in a maintained nursery school, mainstream school or mainstream post-16 institution, unless that is incompatible with —(a) the wishes of the child's parent or the young person, or(b) the provision of efficient education for others

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - mainstream schooling without EHC plan
items.description: A local authority must secure that the child or young person to be educated in a maintained nursery school, mainstream school or mainstream post-16 institution, unless certain exceptions laid down in the section apply.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - maintenance of EHC plan on release from detention
items.description: Where a child or young person who has been subject to a detention order is released,(b) on the release date, a local authority becomes responsible for him or her, and(c) an EHC plan was—(i) maintained for him or her immediately before the start of the detention, or(ii) kept for him or her under  section 74 during the detention.(2) The local authority must—(a) maintain the plan, and(b) review the plan as soon as reasonably practicable after the release date.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - meeting special educational needs
items.description: If a registered pupil or a student at a school or other institution has special educational needs, the appropriate authority must, in exercising its functions in relation to the school or other institution, use its best endeavours to secure that the special educational provision called for by the pupil's or student's special educational needs is made.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - no institution requested
items.description: Where a local authority is not requested to name a particular institution in the EHC plan it must name an institution that is suitable for the age, ability, aptitude or special educational needs of the child or young person concerned. It must after consultation with the governing body or proprietor of that institution name that institution in the EHC.The local authority must then forward a copy of the final EHC plan to the child’s parents or young person and to the institution named.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - nursery and mainstream schooling
items.description: Where a child with special educational needs is being educated in a maintained nursery school or a mainstream school those concerned with making special educational provision for the child must secure that the child engages in the activities of the school together with children who do not have special educational needs, subject to it being reasonably practicable and compatible with—(a) the child receiving the special educational provision called for by his or her special educational needs,(b) the provision of efficient education for the children with whom he or she will be educated, and(c) the efficient use of resources.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - payment of fees
items.description: A local authority must pay the fees (including board and lodging) of the institution concerned where it maintains an EHC plan for a child or young person under which special educational provision in respect of the child or young person is made at a school, post-16 institution or place at which relevant early years education is provided, and that school, institution or place is named in the EHC plan.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - personal budgets
items.description: A local authority that maintains an EHC plan, or is securing the preparation of an EHC plan, for a child or young person must prepare a personal budget for him or her if asked to do so by the child's parent or the young person.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - provision at other institution
items.description: A local authority may arrange for any special educational provision that it has decided is necessary for a child or young person for whom it is responsible to be made otherwise than in a school or post-16 institution or a place at which relevant early years education is provided.An authority may do so only if satisfied that it would be inappropriate for the provision to be made in a school or post-16 institution or at such a place.Before doing so, the authority must consult the child's parent or the young person.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - publication of local offer
items.description: A local authority must publish information about—(a) the provision it expects to be available in its area at the time of publication for children and young people who have special educational needs or a disability, and(b) the provision that it expects to be available outside its area.The local offer should include information about all the areas specified in Schedule 2 of the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014The local offer should be published on the authority's website.  The authority should also publish arrangements for enabling those without access to the internet to get information

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - report containing SEN information
items.description: If special educational provision is made for a child or young person at a maintained school, a maintained nursery school, or a pupil referral unit, and no EHC plan is maintained for the child or young person.  The appropriate authority for the school must inform the child's parent or the young person that special educational provision is being made for the child or young person.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - request for co-operation
items.description: A local authority may require the co-operation of certain bodies in certain circumstances in connection with its functions in relation to Special Educational Needs.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - requested institution
items.description: Where a local authority is requested to name a particular institution in the EHC it must after consultation with the governing body or proprietor of that institution name that institution in the EHC unless the school or other institution requested is unsuitable for the age, ability, aptitude or special educational needs of the child or young person concerned, or the attendance of the child or young person at the requested school or other institution would be incompatible with  the provision of efficient education for others, or the efficient use of resources. In which case after consultation a further institution must be named. The local authority must then forward a copy of the final EHC plan to the child’s parents or young person and to the institution named.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - requested re-assessment of EHC plan
items.description: A local authority must secure a re-assessment of the educational, health care and social care needs of a child or young person for whom it maintains an EHC plan if a request is made to it by—(a) the child's parent or the young person, or(b) the governing body, proprietor or principal of the school, post-16 institution or other institution which the child or young person attends.and must consult as required.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - review of educational, training and social care provision
items.description: A local authority must keep under review and consult where required  regarding the educational, training provision and social care provision made in its area for children and young people who have special educational needs or a disability, and(b) the educational provision, training provision and social care provision made outside its area for—(i) children and young people for whom it is responsible who have special educational needs, and(ii) children and young people in its area who have a disability.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - review of EHC plan
items.description: A local authority must review an EHC plan that it maintains—in the period of 12 months starting with the date on which the plan was first made, andin each subsequent period of 12 months starting with the date on which the plan was last reviewed under this section.and must consult as required.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - supply of goods or services
items.description: A local authority may supply goods and services to—the governing body of a maintained school or maintained nursery school in England; orthe proprietor of an Academy; orthe governing body of an institution within the further education sector that the authority thinks is or is to be attended by a young person for whom the authority maintains an EHC plan, in connection with the provision of special educational needs on such terms and conditions as it thinks fit including payment.

items.label: Special educational needs or disability - transfer of EHC plan
items.description: A local authority must comply with Regulations regarding the transfer of an EHC plan.

items.label: Sports grounds - amendment or replacement of safety certificates
items.description: A local authority may amend or replace a safety certificate in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Sports grounds - appeals against determinations on safety certificates
items.description: A local authority must comply with the appeals procedure concerning safety certificates.

items.label: Sports grounds - entry and inspection
items.description: An officer authorised by a local authority may enter a sports ground for the purpose of inspection and take a copy of certain records.

items.label: Sports grounds - inspection and enforcement
items.description: A local authority must arrange for the periodical inspection of sports grounds.

items.label: Sports grounds - issue, amendment, transfer and cancellation of safety certificates
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the issue, amendment, transfer and cancellation of safety certificates.

items.label: Sports grounds - prohibition notices
items.description: A local authority may issue or withdraw a prohibition notice in certain circumstances.

items.label: Sports grounds - safety certificates
items.description: A local authority must consider applications for safety certificates for qualifying sports grounds and comply with the prescribed procedure for so doing.

items.label: Staff - establishment of staff commission
items.description: A local authority must comply with Secretary of State's directions regarding co-operation with and the payment of expenses to a staff commission.

items.label: Staff - family absence
items.description: Local authorities must maintain a record of all notifications made by members of periods of family absence; the periods of family absence taken and keep them for at least 10 years.LAs have duties to inform, regarding cancellation of family absence, complaints and standing orders relating to members whilst taking a period of family absence.

items.label: Staff - superannuation of persons employed in local government service
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations made under the Act providing for pension schemes for its employees.

items.label: Staff pensions - discretionary payments
items.description: A LA who is a Local Government Pension Scheme employer may make discretionary payments to employees who in the course of carrying out their work sustain an injury or contract a disease and must publish its policy regarding the exercise of its powers.

items.label: Statistics - disclosure to to the Statistics and Registration Service Board
items.description: A local authority may, subject to the provisions of this section, disclose to the Statistics and Registration Service Board any information held by the authority in connection with its functions.

items.label: Statistics and registration - disclosure of information
items.description: A local authority must disclose certain information to the Statistics and Information Service in certain circumstances

items.label: Statues and monuments - erection, maintenance and removal
items.description: A local authority may provide, maintain and, remove statues and monuments in their district.

items.label: Statutory nuisances - criminal and civil proceedings for breach of abatement notice
items.description: A local authority may bring criminal and criminal proceedings in the case of a breach of an abatement notice.

items.label: Statutory nuisances - inspection and investigation
items.description: A local authority must inspect its area from time to time to identify statutory nuisances and must investigate complaints about statutory nuisance.

items.label: Statutory nuisances - notice to recover expenses
items.description: A local authority may serve a notice to recover expenses in certain circumstances which will become a charge on premises.

items.label: Statutory nuisances - proceedings
items.description: A local authority must commence proceedings for statutory nuisance in certain circumstances.

items.label: Stray dogs - appointment and actions by officer
items.description: A local authority must appoint an officer to discharge the functions of seizing, serving notices regarding, disposing of or returning stray dogs and may charge for certain expenses for so doing.

items.label: Street cleaning - non-highway
items.description: A local authority may, with the agreement of the owner or occupier, carry out street cleaning on land which does not form part of the highway.

items.label: Street cleaning - prohibition of parking
items.description: A local authority may by notice prevent parking upon streets upon which street cleaning is  to be carried out

items.label: Street collections - regulations
items.description: A local authority may make regulations, subject to the approval of the relevant Minister, governing street collections of money for charitable or other purposes.

items.label: Street furniture - civil debt for recovery of damage
items.description: A local authority may recover damage caused by negligence to certain items of street furniture as a civil debt.

items.label: Street lighting - affixing to buildings
items.description: A local authority may, with the agreement of a building's owner, affix street lighting to buildings.

items.label: Street names - alteration
items.description: A local authority may with the consent of two thirds of the relevant council tax payers change a street name and mark the same.

items.label: Street names - naming or alteration
items.description: A local authority may name or alter the name of a street in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Street names - objection
items.description: A local authority may object to a proposed street name in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Street names - placement of street nameplates
items.description: A local authority must mark or place the name of a street on the street and renew it in certain circumstances.

items.label: Street trading - regulation
items.description: A local authority may adopt schedule 4 of the Act to enable it to Regulate street trading.

items.label: Street works - advance notice
items.description: A local authority may prescribe requirements when given an advance notice by an undertaker proposing to execute street works.

items.label: Street works - co-ordination of street works
items.description: A local authority must use its best endeavours to coordinate the execution of works of all kinds.

items.label: Street works - cost sharing for major road works and apparatus
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding cost sharing in certain circumstances.

items.label: Street works - directions as to placing of apparatus
items.description: A local authority may give directions as to the placing of apparatus in connection with street works.

items.label: Street works - directions as to timing
items.description: If it appears to the authority that proposed street works are likely to cause serious disruption to traffic, and that the disruption would be avoided or reduced if the works were carried out only at certain times, the authority may give the undertaker such directions as may be appropriate as to the times when the works may or may not be carried out.

items.label: Street works - maintenance of apparatus
items.description: A local authority must take certain steps relating to the maintenance of apparatus as regards the safety and convenience of persons using the street (having regard, in particular, to the needs of people with a disability), the structure of the street and the integrity of apparatus of the authority in the street.

items.label: Street works - major road works and apparatus
items.description: A local authority must co-operate with others and the owners of apparatus in certain information regarding certain major road works.

items.label: Street works - notice restricting works following substantial road works
items.description: A local authority may give notice restricting street works following substantial road works.

items.label: Street works - protected streets
items.description: A local authority may give its consent for the placing of apparatus in protected streets and may charge fees for so doing.

items.label: Street works - reinstatement
items.description: A local authority may investigate the reinstatement of a road, require the undertaker to repair and in certain circumstances carry out the repairs itself and charge the undertaker for so doing.

items.label: Street works - road works and apparatus.
items.description: A local authority must provide the owners of apparatus with certain information regarding certain road works in certain circumstances.  This section applies to works for road purposes other than major highway works.

items.label: Street works - safety measures
items.description: A local authority may give directions as to safety measures to an undertaker of street works in their area.

items.label: Street works - streets with special engineering difficulties
items.description: A local authority must consider designating street as a street with special engineering difficulties when requested to do so.

items.label: Street works - temporary traffic regulation
items.description: Where by reason of street works the traffic authority makes an order or issues a notice under section 14 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 (temporary prohibition or restriction of traffic), the authority may recover from the undertaker the whole of the costs incurred by them in connection with or in consequence of the order or notice.

items.label: Street works - traffic sensitive streets
items.description: A local authority may make a limited designation order in relation to traffic sensitive streets in certain circumstances.

items.label: Street works - undertaken by street authority or district council
items.description: A street authority or district council may enter into an agreement with an undertaker for the execution by the authority or council on behalf of the undertaker of any street works.

items.label: Street works - unreasonable delay or obstruction
items.description: A local authority may issue a notice to prevent unreasonable delay and obstruction and may recover certain costs.

items.label: Street works - unreasonably prolonged works
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations relating to unreasonably prolonged works.

items.label: Street works licence
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances, grant a street works licence permitting a person to place, or to retain, apparatus in the street and thereafter to inspect, maintain, adjust, repair, alter or renew the apparatus, change its position or remove it and to execute for those purposes any works required.

items.label: Street works register
items.description: A local authority must maintain and make available a street works register which must comply with prescribed conditions.

items.label: Streets - naming streets and house numbering
items.description: A local authority must name streets and number houses.

items.label: Subsidy control - compliance with regulations made by Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must comply with Regulations made by the Secretary of State regarding information to be included on the subsidy database.

items.label: Subsidy control - consideration of principles
items.description: A local authority(a)  must consider the subsidy control principles before deciding to give a subsidy, and(b)  must not give the subsidy unless it is of the view that the subsidy is consistent with those principles.

items.label: Subsidy control - consideration of when subsidy control does not apply
items.description: A local authority should have regard to circumstances in which the subsidy control requirements do not apply to the giving of a subsidy.Where the subsidy control requirements do not apply to the giving of a subsidy, those requirements are to be taken as not applying to the making of a subsidy scheme so far as it provides for the giving of such a subsidy.

items.label: Subsidy control - energy and environment principles
items.description: A local authority(a)  must consider the energy and environment principles before deciding to give a subsidy in relation to energy and environment, and(b)  must not give the subsidy unless it is of the view that the subsidy is consistent with those principles.

items.label: Subsidy control - energy and environment principles for schemes
items.description: A local authority(a)  must consider the energy and environment principles before making a subsidy scheme that provides for the giving of subsidies in relation to energy and environment, and(b)  must not make the scheme unless it is of the view that the subsidies provided for by the scheme will be consistent with those principles.

items.label: Subsidy control - inclusion of information in subsidy database
items.description: A local authority must ensure that an entry in the subsidy database is made in respect of (a)  a subsidy given by the authority, and(b)  a subsidy scheme made by the authority.The above does not apply to a subsidy if(a)  it is given under a subsidy scheme,(b)  an entry is made in the subsidy database in respect of the scheme, and(c)  the amount of the subsidy is no more than £100,000.When doing so the local authority must comply with specified time limits and with any Regulations made by the Secretary of State supplementing or modifying the above.

items.label: Subsidy control - mandatory referral to CMA
items.description: A local authority must request a report from the CMA: (a)  before giving a subsidy, or making a subsidy scheme, of particular interest, or(b)  where directed to do so by the Secretary of State under section 55.The request must(a)  include the information in relation to the subsidy or subsidy scheme that would be required under section 34, if the subsidy or scheme were to be given or made,(b)  provide such other information as is specified in regulations under subsection (3)(a),(c)  explain, in the case of a request under subsection (1)(a), why the public authority considers that the subsidy or subsidy scheme would meet the criteria for being a subsidy, or subsidy scheme, of particular interest,(d)  include an assessment by the public authority as to whether the subsidy or scheme would comply with the requirements of Chapters 1 and 2 of Part 2, and the reasons for that conclusion, and(e)  include any evidence relevant to that assessment.The request must also comply with Regulations issue by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Subsidy control - pre-action information for potential review
items.description: Where a local authority receives a request for pre-action information in relation to a potential review of a subsidy decision, the authority must provide such information as would enable, or assist in, the making of a determination as to whether the subsidy was given, or the scheme was made, in accordance with the requirements of Chapters 1 and 2 of Part 2.The information must be provided by the public authority(a)  in writing, and(b)  within 28 days of receiving the request for information.In providing information, a public authority may impose such restrictions as it considers proportionate in order to protect(a)  commercially sensitive information,(b)  confidential information,(c)  information subject to legal privilege, or(d)  information, the disclosure of which would be contrary to the public interest.Information provided in response to a request made under this section may be used only(a)  for the purpose for which it was requested, and(b)  in accordance with any restrictions imposed by the public authority.

items.label: Subsidy control - prohibitions and requirements
items.description: A local authority must comply with any prohibitions determined by legislation when giving certain subsidies, and meet any requirements stipulated in relation to the giving of certain other subsidies.

items.label: Subsidy control - recovery of misused subsidy
items.description: A local authority which has given a subsidy has the right to recover from the beneficiary the whole or part of its amount to the extent that the subsidy is used for a purpose other than the purpose for which it was given.This right is enforceable as if created by contract between the public authority and the beneficiary.Nothing in this section affects any other remedy that the authority may have in connection with the giving of the subsidy.

items.label: Subsidy control - regard to guidance
items.description: A public authority must have regard to guidance issued by the Secretary of State (so far as applicable to the authority and the circumstances of the case) when giving a subsidy or making a subsidy scheme.

items.label: Subsidy control - request for report from CMA
items.description: A local authority may request a report from the CMA before giving a subsidy, or making a subsidy scheme, of interest.The request must(a)  include the information in relation to the subsidy or subsidy scheme that would be required under section 34, if the subsidy or scheme were to be given or made,(b)  provide such other information as is specified in regulations under subsection (3)(a),(c)  explain why the public authority considers that the subsidy or subsidy scheme would meet the criteria for being a subsidy, or subsidy scheme, of interest,(d)  include an assessment by the public authority as to whether the subsidy or scheme would comply with the requirements of Chapters 1 and 2 of Part 2, and the reasons for that conclusion, and(e)  include any evidence relevant to that assessment.The request must comply with any Regulations issued by the Secretary of State.

items.label: Subsidy control - subsidy schemes
items.description: A local authority(a)  must consider the subsidy control principles before making a subsidy scheme, and(b)  must not make the scheme unless it is of the view that the subsidies provided for by the scheme will be consistent with those principles.

items.label: Taxation - decision on taxable status
items.description: If a local authority enters into a contract to which Section 61M applies, If the contract is entered into on or after 6 April 2017, the duty under subsection (1) must be complied with-(a)     on or before the time of entry into the contract, or(b)     if the services begin to be performed at a later time, before that later time.If the contract is entered into before 6 April 2017, the duty under subsection (1) must be complied with on or before the date of the first payment made under the contract on or after 6 April 2017

items.label: Taxation - information to establish taxable status
items.description: If a local authority enters into a contract to which Section 61M applies, the local authority may ask the person such questions as it requires to enable it to comply with its duty under Section 61T.

items.label: Taxation - self employed persons contracted to local authority
items.description: If a local authority contracts with a third party for a person to carry out work for it and that person would be considered to be an employee if engaged directly by the local authority then the local authority must treat that person as an employee for the purposes of tax and national insurance.

items.label: Taxi and private hire licences - acting on reported concerns
items.description: Where an English licensing authority ("authority A"):(a)  receives information from another licensing authority ("authority B") relating to a person who has driven in authority B's area in reliance on a driver's licence granted by authority A, or(b)  receives information of a similar nature from a relevant authority ("authority C") relating to a person who has driven in authority C's area in reliance on a driver's licence granted by authority A.(2)  Before the end of the period of 20 working days beginning with the date on which authority A becomes aware of the information, authority A must:(a)  consider whether to suspend or revoke the person's driver's licence in reliance on(i)  the information, and(ii)  any other information available to authority A, and(b)  inform authority B or authority C (as the case may be) in writing(i)  whether or not it has suspended or revoked, or intends to suspend or revoke, the person's driver's licence, and(ii)  the reasons for that action or intended action.

items.label: Taxi and private hire licences - provision of information
items.description: Where:(a)  an English licensing authority ("the first authority") becomes aware of relevant information relating to a person who has driven in the first authority's area in reliance on a driver's licence or a relevant licence (one issued in Scotland or in Wales) granted by another licensing authority or a relevant authority ("the second authority"),(b)  the information relates to the person's conduct in the first authority's area, and(c)  the first authority is satisfied that, had it granted the licence, it would have considered suspending or revoking it in reliance on the information.(2)  The first authority must provide to the second authority:(a)  the relevant information, and(b)  any other information of which it is aware which is relevant to identifying the person,before the end of the period of 10 working days beginning with the day on which the first authority became aware of the relevant information relating to the person's conduct in its area.

items.label: Taxi and private hire licences - recording of licensing decisions
items.description: In certain circumstances relating to the refusal, revocation or suspension of a taxi or private hire licence a local authority must:(a)  make an entry recording the decision, and prescribed information, in the licensing information database,(b)  ensure (whether by amending, removing or reinstating it) that the entry is kept up-to-date so as to reflect any subsequent change made to the decision(i)  by the authority,(ii)  on appeal against the authority's decision, or(iii)  on any subsequent appeal,during the period of 11 years beginning with the day on which the entry is first made, and(c)  keep a record of the relevant information and the decision until the end of the period referred to in paragraph (b).This must be done within 5 working days of the local authority notifying the person of their decision.

items.label: Taxi and private hire licences - regard to guidance
items.description: A licensing authority must have regard to guidance issued to licensing authorities in connection with their functions under this Act.

items.label: Television services - enforcement
items.description: The relevant local authority may enforce the requirements of these Regulations and has the power to make test purchases, search, seize, test and detain equipment (and relevant documentation with regard to seizure) and to apply for forfeiture of equipment.

items.label: Temporary road traffic order for Coronavirus - notice of intent
items.description: Where a traffic authority is satisfied that an order should be made for purposes connected to coronavirus the traffic authority must, not less than 7 days before making an order, publish notice of its intention to make the order using such arrangements as the traffic authority considers appropriate for the purpose of informing persons likely to be affected by its provisions.

items.label: Temporary road traffic order for Coronavirus - notice of order
items.description: The traffic authority must, on or before the day on which the order is made, give notice of the order to:(a) the chief officer of police of any police area in which any road to which the order relates is situated(b)where the traffic authority is not the fire authority for the area in which any road to which the order relates is situated, to the chief officer of the fire authority for that area(c)where the order would be likely to have direct effect on traffic, or any class of traffic, on any road for the maintenance of which another traffic authority is responsible, to that other traffic authority(d)the concessionaire where the order is likely to have a direct effect on traffic, or any class of traffic, on a road which is subject to a concession or a road in respect of which an assignation has been granted under section 28(1) of the 1991 Act.

items.label: Temporary road traffic order for Coronavirus - publication of order
items.description: Within 14 days after making the order the traffic authority must publish a notice of the making of the order in one or more newspapers, whether in print or online, circulating in the area in which any road to which the order relates is situated.Where the traffic authority considers that it is not reasonably practicable to comply with these requirements for reasons connected to the effects of coronavirus, including restrictions on movement, the traffic authority must publish a notice of the making of the order using such alternative arrangements as the traffic authority considers appropriate for the purpose of informing persons likely to be affected by its provisions.

items.label: Tenant fees - assistance in civil recovery
items.description: A local authority may assist a person who has made an unlawful payment in breach of sections 1 or 2 or Schedule 2, to recover that amount by way of an application to a first-tier tribunal.

items.label: Tenant fees - duty to enforce prohibitions applying to landlords
items.description: A local weights and measures authority must enforce legislation relating to prohibitions which apply to landlords as detailed in Section 1 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019

items.label: Tenant fees - duty to enforce prohibitions applying to letting agents
items.description: A local weights and measures authority must enforce prohibitions applying to letting agents as detailed in Section 2 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019

items.label: Tenant fees - financial penalties
items.description: A local authority being satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that a person has breached section 1 or 2 or Schedule 2 of the Act, may impose a financial penalty on the person in respect of the breach (subject to restrictions and limitations imposed by the Act).

items.label: Tenant fees - notification of enforcement
items.description: A local authority (subject to certain limitations  imposed by the Act) taking enforcement action must notify another local authority of enforcement action taking place in the area of that second authority and certain other prescribed matters.

items.label: Tenant fees - power to enforce prohibitions applying to landlords
items.description: A district council which is not a local weights and measures authority may enforce legislation relating to prohibitions which apply to landlords as detailed in Section 1 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019

items.label: Tenant fees - power to enforce prohibitions applying to letting agents
items.description: A district council which is not a local weights and measures authority may enforce prohibitions applying to letting agents as detailed in Section 2 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019

items.label: Tenant fees - repayment of amount improperly paid
items.description: A local authority may, subject to certain limitations imposed by the Act, require the person responsible to repay the amount improperly paid in breach of section 1 or 2 or Schedule 2 of the Act and may require the person responsible to pay interest on that amount.

items.label: Tobacco purchasing - prohibition of purchase by adult for consumption by child
items.description: A local authority must enforce this criminal offence in its role as weights and measures authority.

items.label: Tourism - visitor and conference facilities
items.description: A local authority may encourage visitors and provide conference facilities or make contributions to others providing the same.

items.label: Town development - appropriation of land for planning purposes
items.description: A local authority may appropriate land, if authorised to do so by the Minister for the purposes of town development.

items.label: Town development - conditions of payment of Exchequer contributions
items.description: A local authority must comply with conditions attached to any exchequer contributions towards the cost of town development.

items.label: Town development - contributions to expenses of land drainage works
items.description: The council of a receiving district or an authority eligible to participate may contribute towards expenses incurred by the National Rivers Authority or by an internal drainage board in the execution of works rendered necessary by the carrying out of development which, in the opinion of the authority making the contribution, is town development within the meaning of this Act.

items.label: Town development - contributions to receiving district
items.description: A local authority which will benefit from town development in another district may make financial contributions to that district.

items.label: Town development - extension of powers of receiving district
items.description: A local authority which will benefit from town development may take certain actions that relate to another district.

items.label: Town development - Ministerial approval for acquisition of land
items.description: A local authority may, with ministerial approval, acquire land compulsorily for the purposes of the Act.

items.label: Town development - participation by agreement
items.description: A local authority may enter into a participation agreement for the purposes of the Act.

items.label: Town development - re-transfers of land
items.description: A local authority must comply with any order made by the Minister regarding re-transfers of land or other adjustments.

items.label: Trading standards - compensation for goods seized
items.description: A local authority must pay compensation for certain goods seized in certain circumstances.

items.label: Trading standards - enforcement of remedies for copyright enfringement
items.description: It is the duty of every local weights and measures authority to enforce within their area the copyright provisions.

items.label: Trading standards - enforcing authorities
items.description: A local authority must enforce the Act and orders made thereunder utilising powers in Schedule 5 to the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and deliver reports to the Board of Trade.

items.label: Trading standards - entry to premises and seizure of goods and documents
items.description: An officer authorised by a local authority may enter premises and seize goods and documents for certain purposes connected with the enforcement of the Act.

items.label: Trading standards - entry to premises for tobacco advertising and promotion enforcement
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may enter premises and make purchases (subject to certain conditions and obligations) in order to enforce the Act.

items.label: Trading standards - notification of test results
items.description: An officer authorised by a local authority must notify the owner of goods of the results of certain tests.

items.label: Trading standards - packaging of goods
items.description: Local authorities (weights and measures authorities) in Great Britain must enforce the regulations on packaging to ensure that it satisfies essential requirements: that lead, cadmium, mercury and hexavalent chromium do not exceed prescribed levels and that technical documentation on compliance are made available to them on request.

items.label: Trading standards - sales of tobacco to children
items.description: A local authority must consider, at least once in every period of twelve months, the extent to which it is appropriate for them to carry out in their area a programme of enforcement action and carry out that enforcement action.

items.label: Trading standards - test purchases
items.description: A local authority may make test purchases for the purposes of the enforcement of the Act.

items.label: Trading standards - textile labelling
items.description: Local authorities (weights and measures authorities) are included as market surveillance authorities for the purposes of carrying out market surveillance checks on fibre composition and labelling under the EU Regulation. Those market surveillance checks are to be carried out in accordance with Articles 19 and 20 and Annexes VII, VIII and IX to the EU Regulation.  Local authorities are obliged to enforce the Regulations in their areas.

items.label: Trading standards - tobacco advertising and promotion enforcement
items.description: A local authority must enforce the Act and the provisions made therein.

items.label: Trading standards - trade marks
items.description: A local authority must enforce the prohibition on unauthorised use of trade marks in section 92 of the Act.

items.label: Training for planning authority members
items.description: A local planning authority must comply with Regulations issued by the Secretary of State regarding training for its Members.

items.label: Transparency - smaller authorities
items.description: Local authorities in England to which the Transparency code for smaller authorities issued on 17th December 2014 applies, must comply with that Code.

items.label: Transport - authorities review of arrangements
items.description: Any one or more local authorities for an area with an integrated transport authority may undertake review related to one or more integrated transport areas or proposed integrated transport areas.  With an incidental duty to prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - cab drivers' shelters
items.description: A local authority may provide, maintain, remove and charge for cab drivers' shelters and make byelaws in respect of the same.

items.label: Transport - co-operation between certain councils and London Regional Transport
items.description: Any non-metropolitan county or district council and Wales and Transport for London shall each have power to enter into any agreement or arrangements with the other under which they undertake to contribute towards any expenditure incurred by the other party to the agreement or arrangements in making payments to a person providing a public passenger transport service under any agreement entered into by that other party in exercise of any power that other party may have to secure the provision of that service.

items.label: Transport - compensation for temporary removal of bus shelter
items.description: A local authority must when requested to do so by a street works undertaker temporarily remove a bus shelter maintained by them or pay compensation.

items.label: Transport - competitive tender for services
items.description: It shall be the duty of an authority to enter into competitive tenders for transport services in certain circumstances.

items.label: Transport - compliance in respect of transport management
items.description: A local authority must comply with the intervention powers of the Secretary of State in relation to its management of the transport network in its area.

items.label: Transport - creation of sub national transport body
items.description: A local authority must comply with an Order of the Secretary of State regarding the creation of sub national transport bodies.

items.label: Transport - delegation of functions
items.description: Duty to comply with the delegation of functions by the Secretary of State in respect of an Integrated Transport Area including the conferral of a power to direct.

items.label: Transport - delegation of functions by Secretary of State
items.description: Duty to comply with the delegation of functions by the Secretary of State in respect of an Integrated Transport Area including the conferral of a power to direct.

items.label: Transport - directed review of transport effectiveness in area with an ITA
items.description: The Secretary of State may direct any one or more local authorities for an area with an integrated transport authority may undertake review of transport effectiveness in area and to prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - Directed review of transport effectiveness in area with no ITA
items.description: When directed by the Secretary of State any two or more local authorities for an area with no integrated transport authority must undertake review of transport effectiveness in area and prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - district securing provision of public transport services
items.description: A non-metropolitan district council shall have power to secure the provision of such public passenger transport services as they consider it appropriate to secure to meet any public transport requirements within their area which would not in their view be met apart from any action taken by them for that purpose.

items.label: Transport - expenditure on public passenger transport services
items.description: It shall be the duty of any authority responsible for expenditure on public passenger transport services to enter into agreements providing for service subsidies (however framed, and whether arising under this Act or under any other enactment) to co-operate with one another so as to secure, in the interests of the ratepayers of their areas

items.label: Transport - financial backing for establishment and operations of public transport companies
items.description: A district council shall have power to make loans to any associated company, or to guarantee loans made to any associated company by any other person, for the provision of working capital.

items.label: Transport - grants for bus services
items.description: A parish council or community council may make grants to any body towards expenditure incurred or to be incurred by that body in connection with the operation of a bus service appearing to the council to be wholly or mainly for the benefit of members of the public who are elderly or disabled; or a community bus service

items.label: Transport - grants for transport facilities and services
items.description: An authority to whom this applies may make grants to any other person towards expenditure incurred or to be incurred by that person in providing, maintaining or improving any vehicle, equipment or other facilities provided wholly or mainly for the purpose of facilitating travel by members of the public who are disabled; or any equipment or other facilities specially designed or adapted for that purpose which are incorporated in any vehicle, equipment or other facilities not provided wholly or mainly for that purpose.

items.label: Transport - grants to transport authorities
items.description: A local authority must comply with the conditions of any transport grant.

items.label: Transport - maintenance of existing bus shelters and queue barriers
items.description: A local authority may maintain existing bus shelters or queue barriers.

items.label: Transport - new integrated transport authority
items.description: Any two or more local authorities for an area with no integrated transport authority may undertake review of transport effectiveness in area.  With an incidental duty to prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - powers of investment and disposal in relation to public transport companies
items.description: A district council can subscribe for shares on formation of a company formed by them (whether alone or jointly with any other council) in pursuance of this Act; or acquire any shares in or other securities of a company.  Any such council shall have power to provide for the disposal, in such manner as they think fit, of any such shares or other securities.

items.label: Transport - promoting availability and convenience of use of public transport
items.description: A non-metropolitan county council and Wales shall have power to take any measures that appear to be appropriate for the purpose of or in connection with promoting the availability of public passenger transport services or the convenience of the public (including persons who are elderly or disabled) in using all available public passenger transport services

items.label: Transport - provision and maintenance of bus shelters
items.description: A local authority may provide and maintain bus shelters in their area subject to them obtaining required consents.

items.label: Transport - provision of services for public transport companies
items.description: A district council shall have power to enter into an agreement with any associated company, or with any subsidiary of an associated company,  for the provision of any administrative, professional or technical services.

items.label: Transport - provision, maintenance and operation of bus stations
items.description: Where a council who, at the time when section 66 of the Act came into force (January 11, 2010), were providing a service for the carriage of passengers by road which required a PSV operator's licence, that council shall have power to maintain, repair and operate bus stations and associated facilities provided by them under their former powers.

items.label: Transport - regard to guidance issued by Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the Secretary of State's guidance in respect of Integrated Transport Area.

items.label: Transport - regard to the Secretary of State’s guidance in respect of Integrated Transport Area
items.description: A local authority must have regard to the Secretary of State’s guidance in respect of Integrated Transport Area.

items.label: Transport - review directed by Secretary of State
items.description: The Secretary of State may direct any one or more local authorities for an area with an integrated transport authority may undertake review of transport effectiveness in area and to prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - review of the effectiveness and efficiency of transport
items.description: The Secretary of State may direct any two or more local authorities for an area with no integrated transport authority may undertake review of transport effectiveness in area and to prepare and publish a scheme for the establishment of an ITA for any area.

items.label: Transport - Review of transport effectiveness in area with ITA
items.description: Any one or more local authorities for an area with an integrated transport authority or where the area could be included in a proposed integrated transport authority may undertake review of transport effectiveness in area.  With an incidental duty to prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - Review of transport effectiveness in area with no ITA
items.description: Any two or more local authorities for an area with no integrated transport authority may undertake review of transport effectiveness in area.  With an incidental duty to prepare and publish a scheme.

items.label: Transport - securing of public transport provision by county
