items.description: In each non-metropolitan county of England and Wales it shall be the duty of the county council to secure the provision of such public passenger transport services as the council consider it appropriate to secure to meet requirements within the county that would not be provided by any other means.

items.label: Transport - travel concessions on services provided by local authorities
items.description: There is power to provide travel concessions for persons travelling on the service in accordance with a scheme established under section 93 of this Act or in accordance with section 145A(1) or 145B(1) of the Transport Act 2000

items.label: Transport – management of transport network
items.description: A local authority must manage and make arrangements for the management of the transport network in its area and have regard to the guidance of the secretary of state when so doing.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - complying with directions
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State (England) or Welsh Ministers (Wales) to do things within or outside its area to deal with the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - directions concerning transportation, storage or disposal of bodies
items.description: A designated local authority may give directions requiring a person (not acting as an individual or as part of a public authority) to do anything calculated to facilitate the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains within or from its area. Directions may include the provision of services or equipment and how the direction should be carried out. The local authority must have regard to certain matters before making that Direction.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - disclosure of information
items.description: A local authority may disclose any information obtained for the purposes of ascertaining the capacity within its area to deal with the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains only for that purpose or for complying with another legal obligation.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - failure to comply
items.description: A local authority must comply with a Direction form the Secretary of State (England) or Welsh Ministers (Wales) in relation to a perceived or actual failure to properly comply with its duties under this Schedule or its general duties relating to dead bodies, human remains, cremations or burials.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - information request from Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority must (subject to data protection legislation and the Investigatory Powers Act 2016) comply with a request for information from the Secretary of State, where that request is in writing and is for the purpose of ascertaining the capacity within its area to deal with the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains either locally or nationally.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - information request from Welsh Ministers
items.description: A local authority must (subject to data protection legislation and the Investigatory Powers Act 2016) comply with a request for information from Welsh Ministers, where that request is in writing and is for the purpose of ascertaining the capacity within its area to deal with the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains either locally or nationally.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - payment where directions issued
items.description: Where a local authority has given directions requiring a person (not acting as an individual or as part of a public authority) to do anything calculated to facilitate the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains within or from its area it must make payments in accordance with a scheme to be published by the appropriate national authority.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - provision of information
items.description: A local authority may require a person to give information for the purpose of ascertaining the capacity within its area to deal with the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains. The request must be made in writing and explain to whom the information is to be provided, how it is provided and by when it is to be provided. This power is subject to restrictions imposed by data protection legislation and by the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.

items.label: Transportation of dead bodies - regard to guidance
items.description: Where a local authority has been designated by the Secretary of State or Welsh Ministers it must have regard to guidance published by the Secretary of State or Welsh Ministers with regard to the exercise of its functions in relation to the transportation, storage or disposal of dead bodies or other human remains within or from its area.

items.label: Travel concessions - financial contributions
items.description: A local authority may contribute to the cost of travel concessions incurred by a another authority.

items.label: Unlawful use of drugs on premises - discharge of closure order
items.description: A local authority may make an application that a closure order is discharged in relation to premises where drugs are used unlawfully or may appeal against the refusal to make such an order.

items.label: Unlawful use of drugs on premises - reimbursement of costs
items.description: A local authority may apply to have the cost of cleaning, securing or maintaining premises where drugs are used unlawfully reimbursed.

items.label: Unlawfully deposited waste - compliance with directions
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State with regard to waste unlawfully deposited upon land and must in certain circumstances publicise those directions.

items.label: Unlawfully deposited waste - removal
items.description: A local authority may give directions regarding waste unlawfully deposited upon land and in certain circumstances may remove the waste itself and recover costs.

items.label: Unlawfully kept or disposed of waste - removal
items.description: A local authority may give directions regarding controlled or excavated waste unlawfully kept or disposed of deposited upon land and in certain circumstances may remove the waste itself and recover costs.

items.label: Use of spare capacity of computers of local authorities
items.description: A local authority may, in certain circumstances, enter into an agreement to allow others to share computer facilities and charge for the same.

items.label: Vehicles for repair or sale on road - fixed penalty notice
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may give a fixed penalty notice for a suspected breach of sections 3 or 4 of the Act (repairing or exposing vehicles for sale on the road).

items.label: Vehicles for repair or sale on road - information about receipts
items.description: A local authority must provide information about its use of receipts from fixed penalty notices to the appropriate person and comply with regulations..

items.label: Vehicles for repair or sale on road - request for personal details
items.description: An authorised officer may require the name and address of a person to whom he proposes to give a fixed penalty notice under section 6 of the Act.

items.label: Vehicles for repair or sale on road - use of receipts
items.description: Power to use receipts from fixed penalty notices for various purposes.

items.label: Video recordings - enforcement
items.description: The functions of a local weights and measures authority include the enforcement in their area of this Act.

items.label: Voluntary organisations - provision of information regarding financial assistance
items.description: A local authority must make the provision of certain financial assistance to voluntary organisations conditional upon provision of information regarding how that money has been spent.

items.label: Volunteering - Emergency Volunteering Certificates
items.description: Local authorities in England and Wales may issue Emergency Volunteering Certificates in connection with volunteering in the Health or Social Care Sectors from a specific date for a specific period of between 2 and 4 weeks. The production of a certificate allows a worker to be absent from work for the purposes of emergency volunteering but still entitled to receive the benefits under his or her contract of employment whilst on leave.

items.label: War memorials - maintenance and repair
items.description: A local authority may incur reasonable expenditure in the maintenance repair and protection of any war memorial within their district whether vested in them or not.

items.label: Ward councillor - exercise of any function of a local authority
items.description: A local authority may authorise a councillor for a ward or division to discharge its functions (to the extent allowed) in respect of that ward or division.

items.label: Waste collection - charges for provision of dustbins
items.description: A local authority may make an annual charge for the provision, maintenance, repair or renewal of dustbins in certain circumstances.

items.label: Waste collection - fixed penalty notices for offences related to receptacles
items.description: An officer duly authorised by a local authority may, in certain circumstances, issue a fixed penalty notice, in the manner prescribed, for offences under sections 46 and 47 of the Act.

items.label: Waste collection - fixed penalty notices regarding receptacles
items.description: An officer duly authorised by a local authority may, in certain circumstances, issue a fixed penalty notice, in the manner prescribed, for offences under sections 46 and 47 of the Act.

items.label: Waste disposal - fixed penalty notices for offences
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may issue fixed penalty notices for certain waste disposal offences.

items.label: Waste disposal - joint municipal waste management strategies
items.description: Local authorities in a two tier area must produce and publish a joint municipal waste management strategy and make the same available.

items.label: Waste disposal - landfills
items.description: A local authority must comply with regulations regarding performance of their functions with regard to disposal of waste in landfills.

items.label: Waste disposal - municipal waste management strategy
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations regarding its municipal waste management strategy.

items.label: Waste disposal - non-controlled waste
items.description: A local authority may collect information about, and make arrangements for the disposal of, waste which is situated or likely to be situated in its area and is not controlled waste.

items.label: Waste disposal - provision of information about waste
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations requiring it to provide information about waste.

items.label: Waste disposal - search and seizure of vehicles
items.description: An authorised officer of a local authority may in certain circumstances search and seize vehicles where it is believed  a vehicle was used in the commission of an offence.

items.label: Water conservation by public authorities
items.description: Local authorities must take water conservation into account when exercising their functions.

items.label: Water supply - corruption by gas washings
items.description: A local authority may by notice prohibit the pollution of the water supply by gas washings.

items.label: Waterways - assistance for maintenance for amenity purposes
items.description: A local authority may assist any other person (whether financially, by the provision of services or facilities, or otherwise) in maintaining or improving waterways for amenity or recreational purposes, including fishing.

items.label: Weights and measures - annual report
items.description: A local authority acting as a local weights and measures authority must provide an annual report to the Secretary of State for every financial year.

items.label: Weights and measures - appointment of chief inspectors and inspectors
items.description: A local authority must appoint a Chief Inspector and Inspectors.

items.label: Weights and measures - employment of officers
items.description: A local authority who are for the time being, or have at any time been, a local weights and measures authority under this Act or the Weights and Measures Act 1963 may provide and maintain within their area for use by the public such weighing or measuring equipment as may appear to the authority to be expedient.Without prejudice to the provisions of any other Act, and subject to section 18 above, a local authority may employ persons to attend to any weighing or measuring by means of equipment provided by that authority for use by the public.Except in the case of a weighing or measuring for which, under any other Act, the charge falls to be regulated from time to time by some other person, a local authority by whom any weighing or measuring equipment is provided for use by the public may make such charges for any weighing or measuring by means of that equipment as they may from time to time think fit.

items.label: Weights and measures - exchange of standards or equipment
items.description: A local authority may—provide a particular working standard or item of equipment by making arrangements with another person for the standard or item to be made available by him, andmake arrangements with another person for standards or equipment provided by the authority,  except stamping equipment, to be made available to the other person

items.label: Weights and measures - fees for work resulting from EU obligation
items.description: A local weights and measures authority may charge such reasonable fees as they may determine—for services or facilities provided by them, or by the inspectors appointed for their area, in pursuance of a EU obligation, and for authorisations, certificates or other documents issued by the authority or any such inspector in pursuance of a EU 1 obligation.

items.label: Weights and measures - hiring of equipment
items.description: A local authority may If they are of the opinion that any particular description of testing equipment is proper and sufficient for the efficient discharge of the functions of the inspectors appointed for the authority's area, butthat, having regard to the expenditure involved and the frequency with which such equipment is likely to be used by those inspectors, it would not be reasonable for the authority to provide and maintain such equipment,request the Secretary of State to provide and maintain such equipment and to make it available for hire to the authority

items.label: Weights and measures - investigatory powers
items.description: The investigatory powers available to a local weights and measures authority for the purposes of the enforcement of this Act, are set out in Schedule 5 to the Consumer Rights Act 2015.

items.label: Weights and measures - local standards
items.description: There shall be maintained by each local weights and measures authority such standards (in this Act referred to as “local standards”) of such of the measures and weights set out in Schedule 3 to this Act as the Secretary of State may from time to time approve or require in the case of that authority as being proper and sufficient for the purposes of this Act.

items.label: Weights and measures - measuring container bottles
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to measuring container bottles.

items.label: Weights and measures - measuring instruments
items.description: A local weights and measures authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to measuring instruments.

items.label: Weights and measures - non-automatic weighing equipment
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to non-automatic weighing instruments.

items.label: Weights and measures - packaged goods
items.description: The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to packaged goods.

items.label: Weights and measures - prosecutions
items.description: A local weights and measures authority may prosecute offences under the Act.

items.label: Weights and measures - special powers of inspectors with respect to certain goods
items.description: An inspector may, at all reasonable times, inspect and test any weighing or measuring equipment which is, or which he has reasonable cause to believe to be, used for trade or in the possession of any person or upon any premises for such use, inspect any goods regarding which a representation has been made as to the quantity of any goods offered or exposed for sale or sold, and enter any premises at which he has reasonable cause to believe there to be any such equipment or goods, not being premises used only as a private dwelling-house.

items.label: Weights and measures - weighing by inspectors
items.description: Local authority inspectors may weigh and measure goods, require the production of documents and weigh vehicles in certain circumstances.

items.label: Weights and measures - weighing equipment certificate
items.description: A local authority may issue a certificate for public weighing and measuring equipment and for individuals using such equipment.

items.label: Weights and measures – Working standards testing and stamping equipment
items.description: Each local weights and measures authority shall provide for use by the inspectors appointed for the authority's area, and maintain or from time to time replace—(a) such standards (in this Act referred to as “working standards”) of such of the measures and weights set out in Schedule 3 to this Act.(b) such testing equipment, and(c) such stamping equipment,as are proper and sufficient for the efficient discharge by those inspectors of their functions in the authority's area.

items.label: Welfare - arrangements for persons with a disability
items.description: A local authority may with the approval of the Secretary of State and to the extent directed by him make welfare arrangements for persons with a disability.

items.label: Welfare - charges for provision of accommodation
items.description: A local authority must recover charges for accommodation provided in certain circumstances

items.label: Welfare - expenses of officer applying to Court of Protection as a deputy
items.description: A local authority may defray the expenses of any of its officer's applying to the Court of Protection as a Deputy, under the Act, that are not recoverable elsewhere.

items.label: Welfare - management of premises in which accommodation provided
items.description: A local authority may make rules as to the conduct of premises under their management in which accommodation is provided and as to the preservation of order in the premises.

items.label: Welfare - provision of accommodation
items.description: A local authority must provide accommodation with the approval of the Secretary of State and to the extent directed by him and must take into account the welfare of persons for whom the accommodation is provided.

items.label: Welfare - provision of accommodation for person with no settled residence
items.description: A local authority may provide accommodation to a person of no settled residence as if he were ordinarily resident in their area.

items.label: Welfare - recovery in cases of misrepresentation or non-disclosure
items.description: A local authority may recover sums spent under the Act in cases of misrepresentation or non-disclosure.

items.label: Welfare - recovery of expenditure from another authority
items.description: A local authority may recover expenditure under the Act from another local authority in certain circumstances.

items.label: Welfare - recovery of money through criminal proceedings or civil debt actions
items.description: A local authority may institute certain criminal proceedings or civil debt actions to recover money.

items.label: Welfare - removal of persons needing care and attention
items.description: A local authority in Wales may remove persons in need of care and attention to certain premises in certain circumstances.

items.label: Welfare - research
items.description: A local authority may carry out or promote and assist research into local authority powers and duties related to welfare services under the Act.

items.label: Welfare of children - safeguarding practice and child death reviews
items.description: A local safeguarding board must comply with sections 16(C) to (P) of the Children Act 2004 when considering Local Child Safeguarding Practice Reviews and Child Death Reviews.

items.label: Welfare of old people - promotion
items.description: A local authority may to the extent approved by the Secretary of State and as directed make provision for the promotion of the welfare of old people.

items.label: Wellbeing strategy in England
items.description: A local authority must prepare and may modify a strategy for promoting economic, social and environmental well being in its area, in accordance with the prescribed procedure.

items.label: Wellbeing strategy in Wales
items.description: A Welsh authority may do anything (subject to limits) to promote or improve the economic, social or environmental well being of their area.

items.label: Welsh language - amendment of scheme
items.description: A local authority in Wales may amend its Welsh language scheme in certain circumstances.

items.label: Welsh language - consultation on preparation of scheme
items.description: A local authority in Wales must consult regarding its proposed Welsh language scheme and comply with any directions from the Board.

items.label: Welsh Language - directed amendment of scheme
items.description: A local authority in Wales must amend its Welsh language scheme in certain circumstances.

items.label: Welsh language - directions on scheme from Secretary of State
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with any directions made by the Secretary of State with regard to its Welsh language scheme following an investigation.

items.label: Welsh language - intervention in schemes
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with any intervention from the Secretary of State regarding Welsh language schemes.

items.label: Welsh language - periodic revision of scheme
items.description: A local authority in Wales must comply with a notice received from the Board requiring it to revise its Welsh language scheme.

items.label: Welsh language - preparation of scheme
items.description: A local authority in Wales must prepare a scheme regarding its usage of the Welsh language and comply with any direction or guidance from the Board.

items.label: Welsh language - submission of scheme
items.description: A local authority in Wales must submit its scheme to the Board in the prescribed manner.

items.label: Works - Joint working
items.description: Two or more local authorities may jointly carry out works and defray each other's expenses.

items.label: Young person - learning and support agreement
items.description: A local authority may enter into a conditional learning and support agreement with a young person.

items.label: Young person or young adult - information provision
items.description: A person or body as defined in the legislation may supply information about a young person or relevant young adult to an English local authority with an education function where that information is required for the provision of services under section 68 and 70 of the same act.

items.label: Youth detention - treatment as looked after child
items.description: A child who is remanded to youth detention accommodation is to be treated as a child who is looked after by the designated authority.The cost of this accommodation must be met by the designated local authority

items.label: Youth justice - aims of the service
items.description: It is the duty of all persons and bodies carrying out functions in relation to the youth justice system to have regard to the principal aim of the youth justice system to prevent offending by children and young persons.

items.label: Youth justice - EHC plan for detained persons
items.description: Local authorities (home authorities) must follow the procedures for carrying out a detained person's EHC needs assessment and making an EHC plan including: adhering to prescribed time-scales in which decisions need to be made; the factors which the home authority need to consider when carrying out an assessment and the information and advice which should be made available to the detained person or a detained child's parent.

items.label: Youth justice - guidance from Secretary of State
items.description: Local Authorities and other bodies who carry out youth justice duties are required to act in accordance with any guidance given to them by the Secretary of State

items.label: Youth justice - local provision of services
items.description: A local authority must, acting in co-operation with certain other bodies secure that, to such extent as is appropriate for their area, all youth justice services are available there.

items.label: Youth justice - notification of detention of child or young person
items.description: A youth offending team of a local authority must notify certain bodies when a young person is convicted of an offence.

items.label: Youth justice - payments
items.description: The local authority and every person or body mentioned in subsection (2) of this section shall have power to make payments towards expenditure incurred in the provision of youth justice services by making the payments directly orby contributing to a fund, established and maintained by the local authority, out of which the payments may be made.

items.label: Youth justice - prevention of offending
items.description: The Local Authority is under a duty to "reduce the need to bring criminal proceedings against children within their area" "encourage children within their area not to commit criminal offences" and "avoid the need for children within their area to be placed in secure accommodation" [secure accommodation means secure children's homes].

items.label: Youth justice - secure accommodation order
items.description: A local authority can apply to the court for a secure accommodation order if it either appears that the young person has a history of absconding and is likely to abscond from any other description of accommodation and if the young person absconds, he/she is likely to suffer significant harm or, that if he/she is kept in any other description of accommodation he/she is likely to injure himself or other persons.

items.label: Youth justice - youth justice plans
items.description: A local authority must, after consultation with the relevant persons and bodies, formulate and implement for each year a youth justice plan.

items.label: Youth justice - youth offending teams
items.description: A local authority must, acting in co-operation with certain other bodies establish one or more youth offending teams for their area.

items.label: Youth offending - electronic monitoring
items.description: Youth Offending Teams must inform the court that electronic monitoring is suitable when the court is considering the imposition of electronic monitoring on a young person aged between 12 and 17 released on bail.

items.label: Youth offending - referral orders
items.description: Youth Offending Teams must establish and support youth offender panels. Including the provision of staff and accommodation as well as supervision of youth offender contract

items.label: Youth offending - youth cautions
items.description: Where the Youth Offending Teams is advised of a young person being warned or cautioned the Youth Offending Team is required to assess the young person and arrange for him/her to participate in a rehabilitation programme if appropriate

items.label: Youth support -  provision of information by public bodies
items.description: A local authority in Wales may supply information about a young person to certain other bodies in connection with the provision of certain services to young people.

items.label: Youth support - conduct and effect of inspections
items.description: A local authority must take certain steps with regard to inspections relating to the provision of certain services to 11 to 25 year olds in Wales.

items.label: Youth support - directed services for 11 to 25 year olds
items.description: A local authority must comply with directions from the National Assembly and take other steps with regard to the provision of certain services to 11 to 25 year olds in Wales.

items.label: Youth support - discretionary services for 11 to 25 year olds
items.description: A local authority may exercise certain powers in connection with its duty to comply with Directions from the National Assembly and take other steps with regard to the provision of certain services to 11 to 25 year olds in Wales.
